_meta.note: Reference patterns, not programs. Each query is a starting point to adapt to your own data model; its output is a list of review candidates, never an automated denial or payment action. Every threshold is a starting point. Derived file, do not hand-edit.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Impossible day — >24 billed hours for one rendering provider
tests.hypothesis: If the quantity/frequency-limit edit is absent or tuned only at the claim-line level, an aide or agency can bill time units that sum across claims to more hours than exist in a day. Fraudulent and erroneous time-billing both leave the same signature: a per-NPI per-day minute total that no human schedule supports. Line-level MUE edits do not catch it because each individual line is plausible; only the daily aggregate is impossible.
tests.check: For each rendering provider (aide/nurse) and each service date, sum all billed service minutes across every claim line in the time-based service categories. Flag any provider-day above a physical-plausibility ceiling. Run a second, tighter pass at a sustained-workload ceiling (e.g. >16h) to catch the more common and more defensible-looking pattern.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 1 - Impossible day: total billed service minutes per rendering NPI per day
-- Pattern only. Run on your own warehouse. Output = review candidates, not dispositions.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :minutes_per_unit (15), :hard_ceiling_minutes (1440),
--         :soft_ceiling_minutes (960)

WITH timed_lines AS (
  SELECT
      cl.rendering_npi,
      cl.service_date,
      -- normalise units to minutes; adapt the unit->minute factor to YOUR fee schedule.
      -- Many personal-care HCPCS bill in 15-minute units (T1019, S5125, G0156).
      SUM(COALESCE(cl.service_minutes, cl.units * :minutes_per_unit)) AS billed_minutes,
      COUNT(*)                                   AS line_count,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cl.beneficiary_id)          AS distinct_beneficiaries,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cl.billing_npi)             AS distinct_billing_entities,
      SUM(cl.paid_amount)                        AS paid_amount
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide',
                                'private_duty_nursing','hcbs_in_home')   -- tune to your taxonomy
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND cl.rendering_npi IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY cl.rendering_npi, cl.service_date
)
SELECT
    rendering_npi,
    service_date,
    billed_minutes,
    ROUND(billed_minutes / 60.0, 2) AS billed_hours,
    line_count,
    distinct_beneficiaries,
    distinct_billing_entities,
    paid_amount,
    CASE
      WHEN billed_minutes > :hard_ceiling_minutes THEN 'IMPOSSIBLE'   -- >24h in a calendar day
      ELSE 'IMPLAUSIBLE'                                              -- above sustained-workload ceiling
    END AS severity
FROM timed_lines
WHERE billed_minutes > :soft_ceiling_minutes
ORDER BY billed_minutes DESC, paid_amount DESC;

-- Companion roll-up: providers with a RECURRING impossible-day pattern are the
-- stronger review candidates than a single-day outlier (which is often a keying error).
--   SELECT rendering_npi, COUNT(*) AS impossible_days, SUM(paid_amount) AS exposure
--   FROM ( <query above> ) x WHERE severity = 'IMPOSSIBLE'
--   GROUP BY rendering_npi HAVING COUNT(*) >= :recurrence_threshold;
tests.threshold: :hard_ceiling_minutes = 1440 (24h) is a physical fact, not a tuned threshold — a hit above it is an arithmetic impossibility and should always be reviewed. :soft_ceiling_minutes = 960 (16h) is the tunable one: start there and move it against your own population, because live-in and 24-hour-care programs, split-shift authorisations, and multi-payer aides legitimately produce long days. :minutes_per_unit is normally 15 for T-code personal care but MUST be read off your fee schedule per HCPCS. :recurrence_threshold = 3 impossible days in the period is a reasonable starting filter. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-08 (Quantity / frequency-limit edits — capped & time-based services). Secondary: CB-07 (MUE units-of-service edit enforcement), MD-14 (Utilization control & SURS medical-review program).

failure_map.reading: No daily-aggregate frequency edit exists — only line-level MUE. Build the per-NPI-per-day rollup edit; CB-08's evidence artifact (frequency-limit exception report) does not exist.
The exception report is specified but was not produced for the period. Restore the continuous cadence and name the owner (PI analyst / edit builder).
Impossible-day exceptions were produced and closed with no action or a blanket override. Require a written rationale per closure.
The edit runs at claim-line level only, so it never sees the daily aggregate — the rule is the defect, not the operation. Add the cross-claim daily rollup.
Staff assert the review happens but no dated, attributable exception log is retained. The control may be sound; the assurance is not.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Overlapping visit intervals — one aide in two places at once
tests.hypothesis: The daily-total test misses the case where an aide bills 8 plausible hours that happen to be the SAME 8 hours for two different beneficiaries. If the time-integrity edit has no interval-overlap rule, concurrent service intervals for one rendering provider pass adjudication cleanly. This is the single most durable signature of attendant-care fraud in the case base.
tests.check: Self-join billed service intervals for the same rendering provider on the same date and flag any pair whose [start, end) windows intersect for more than a de-minimis tolerance. Report the overlap minutes, both beneficiaries, and both billing entities — cross-agency overlaps are a distinct and stronger signal.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 2 - Overlapping billed service intervals for one rendering provider
-- Requires start/end timestamps. If you only hold date+units, this test is not
-- runnable on claims alone - run it against EVV check-in/check-out instead (see TEST 8).
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :overlap_tolerance_minutes (0-5)

WITH intervals AS (
  SELECT
      cl.claim_line_id,
      cl.rendering_npi,
      cl.billing_npi,
      cl.beneficiary_id,
      cl.service_date,
      cl.service_begin_datetime AS t_start,
      cl.service_end_datetime   AS t_end,
      cl.paid_amount
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide',
                                'private_duty_nursing','hcbs_in_home')
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND cl.service_begin_datetime IS NOT NULL
    AND cl.service_end_datetime   IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    a.rendering_npi,
    a.service_date,
    a.claim_line_id       AS line_a,
    b.claim_line_id       AS line_b,
    a.beneficiary_id      AS beneficiary_a,
    b.beneficiary_id      AS beneficiary_b,
    a.billing_npi         AS billing_entity_a,
    b.billing_npi         AS billing_entity_b,
    a.t_start AS a_start, a.t_end AS a_end,
    b.t_start AS b_start, b.t_end AS b_end,
    -- overlap in minutes between the two intervals
    (LEAST(a.t_end, b.t_end) - GREATEST(a.t_start, b.t_start)) AS overlap_window,
    (a.paid_amount + b.paid_amount) AS combined_paid,
    CASE WHEN a.billing_npi <> b.billing_npi THEN 'CROSS-AGENCY' ELSE 'SAME-AGENCY' END AS overlap_class
FROM intervals a
JOIN intervals b
  ON  a.rendering_npi = b.rendering_npi
  AND a.service_date  = b.service_date
  AND a.claim_line_id < b.claim_line_id          -- each pair once, no self-match
  AND a.t_start < b.t_end
  AND b.t_start < a.t_end                        -- classic interval-intersection test
WHERE a.beneficiary_id <> b.beneficiary_id       -- drop same-beneficiary split shifts
  -- the overlap must be longer than the tolerance (0 keeps every overlap)
  AND (LEAST(a.t_end, b.t_end) - GREATEST(a.t_start, b.t_start))
        > :overlap_tolerance_minutes * INTERVAL '1' MINUTE
ORDER BY a.rendering_npi, a.service_date;

-- NOTE ON DIALECT: timestamp subtraction returns an interval in Postgres, a number of
-- days in Oracle, and requires DATEDIFF/TIMESTAMPDIFF in SQL Server / BigQuery / Snowflake.
-- Replace the LEAST/GREATEST expression with your dialect's minute-difference function.
-- Portability: number * INTERVAL '1' MINUTE is PostgreSQL/DuckDB style; the portable form of the
-- tolerance test is DATEDIFF/TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, overlap_start, overlap_end) > :overlap_tolerance_minutes.
tests.threshold: There is no statistical threshold here — an overlap is either present or it is not. The tunable is :overlap_tolerance_minutes: allow 0–5 minutes to absorb rounding and clock skew; the query returns only pairs whose overlap is longer than that tolerance. Prioritise CROSS-AGENCY overlaps and providers with ≥5 overlapping pairs in the period; a single 3-minute same-agency overlap is almost always a documentation artifact. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-08 (Quantity / frequency-limit edits — capped & time-based services). Secondary: MD-14 (Utilization control & SURS), CD-09 (Proof-of-delivery / proof-of-service capture).

failure_map.reading: No interval-overlap rule exists anywhere in the edit set. Build it — this is the highest-yield single rule in the family.
The overlap monitor is designed but has not been run against the period's claims.
Overlap exceptions were dispositioned as 'documentation error' without correcting the paid claim or referring the pattern.
The rule compares dates but not times, or runs within a single agency only — so cross-agency and same-day overlaps are invisible.
No retained exception log ties an overlap hit to a named reviewer and a dated disposition.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Geographic impossibility — travel time between consecutive visits
tests.hypothesis: Where the NPI/credential-footprint consistency monitor is absent or checks only the enrolled service address, an aide can bill sequential non-overlapping visits that are geographically unreachable in the gap between them. Non-overlapping intervals defeat TEST 2; distance defeats the claim.
tests.check: Order each rendering provider's visits by start time within a date, compute the gap to the next visit and the straight-line distance between the two service locations, and flag pairs where the implied travel speed exceeds a plausible ceiling. Straight-line distance under-states real travel, so a violation on straight-line distance is conservative.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 3 - Geographic impossibility between consecutive visits
-- Uses service-location coordinates (EVV geo-stamp, or geocoded beneficiary service address).
-- If you hold no coordinates, degrade to ZIP-centroid distance and raise the speed ceiling.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :max_speed_mph (65), :min_distance_miles (5)
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.
-- Portability: EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM a - b) is PostgreSQL/DuckDB style; elsewhere use DATEDIFF or
--   TIMESTAMPDIFF in seconds.

WITH visits AS (
  SELECT
      cl.rendering_npi,
      cl.service_date,
      cl.beneficiary_id,
      cl.claim_line_id,
      cl.service_begin_datetime AS t_start,
      cl.service_end_datetime   AS t_end,
      loc.latitude,
      loc.longitude
  FROM claim_lines cl
  JOIN service_location loc                -- your geocoded service-address dimension
    ON loc.beneficiary_id = cl.beneficiary_id
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide',
                                'private_duty_nursing','hcbs_in_home')
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
),
sequenced AS (
  SELECT
      v.*,
      LEAD(t_start)       OVER w AS next_start,
      LEAD(latitude)      OVER w AS next_lat,
      LEAD(longitude)     OVER w AS next_lon,
      LEAD(beneficiary_id) OVER w AS next_beneficiary
  FROM visits v
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY rendering_npi, service_date ORDER BY t_start)
),
legs AS (
  SELECT
      rendering_npi, service_date, beneficiary_id, next_beneficiary,
      t_end, next_start,
      -- haversine, miles. Replace with ST_DISTANCE if your warehouse has geospatial types.
      3958.8 * 2 * ASIN(SQRT(
          POWER(SIN(RADIANS(next_lat - latitude) / 2), 2)
        + COS(RADIANS(latitude)) * COS(RADIANS(next_lat))
        * POWER(SIN(RADIANS(next_lon - longitude) / 2), 2)
      )) AS distance_miles,
      -- gap in hours between end of one visit and start of the next
      EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (next_start - t_end)) / 3600.0 AS gap_hours
  FROM sequenced
  WHERE next_start IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    rendering_npi, service_date,
    beneficiary_id AS from_beneficiary, next_beneficiary AS to_beneficiary,
    t_end AS left_at, next_start AS arrived_at,
    ROUND(distance_miles, 1) AS distance_miles,
    ROUND(gap_hours, 2)      AS gap_hours,
    ROUND(distance_miles / NULLIF(gap_hours, 0), 1) AS implied_mph
FROM legs
WHERE distance_miles > :min_distance_miles
  AND distance_miles / NULLIF(gap_hours, 0) > :max_speed_mph
ORDER BY implied_mph DESC;
tests.threshold: :max_speed_mph = 65 is a defensible urban/suburban starting ceiling; raise it in rural states with long interstate runs and lower it in dense metros where 65mph door-to-door is itself implausible. :min_distance_miles = 5 suppresses the noise from geocoding imprecision on adjacent addresses. Zero gap_hours (back-to-back visits at different addresses) is the strongest sub-case — surface it separately. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PI-20 (Provider NPI/credential-footprint consistency monitoring). Secondary: CB-08 (Quantity / frequency-limit edits).

failure_map.reading: No footprint-consistency monitor exists; PI-20's alert log does not exist.
PI-20 is specified as continuous/near-real-time but produced no alerts in the period.
Geographic alerts were cleared as 'aide relocated' with no corroborating record.
The monitor compares the billing NPI's enrolled address only, never the sequence of service locations within a day.
Alerts fire into a queue with no retained disposition record.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Billed-vs-verified variance — claims with no EVV visit record
tests.hypothesis: Where the proof-of-service capture control is absent, not reconciled, or reconciled only in one direction, claims exist for visits that no electronic visit verification record supports. Services-not-rendered leaves its cleanest signature as a claim with no matching verified visit — the payer holds both datasets and simply never joins them.
tests.check: Left-join paid time-based claim lines to the EVV visit table on beneficiary + attendant + date, and report (a) claims with no EVV visit at all, and (b) claims whose billed minutes materially exceed the EVV-verified minutes. Run the reciprocal direction too — verified visits never billed indicate a data pipeline problem rather than fraud, and distinguishing the two is the point.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 4 - Billed-vs-EVV-verified variance (services-not-rendered signature)
-- EVV is required for Medicaid personal care and home health services under
-- 21st Century Cures Act §12006 (SSA §1903(l)). Confirm your state's EVV scope.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :minutes_per_unit (15), :variance_tolerance_pct (0.10)

WITH billed AS (
  SELECT
      cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.rendering_npi, cl.billing_npi,
      cl.service_date, cl.hcpcs, cl.paid_amount,
      COALESCE(cl.service_minutes, cl.units * :minutes_per_unit) AS billed_minutes
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide','hcbs_in_home')
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
),
verified AS (
  SELECT
      v.beneficiary_id,
      v.attendant_npi,
      CAST(v.check_in_datetime AS DATE) AS service_date,
      SUM(v.verified_minutes)           AS verified_minutes,
      COUNT(*)                          AS verified_visits
  FROM evv_visit v
  WHERE v.visit_status = 'COMPLETE'
    AND CAST(v.check_in_datetime AS DATE) BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  GROUP BY v.beneficiary_id, v.attendant_npi, CAST(v.check_in_datetime AS DATE)
)
SELECT
    b.claim_line_id, b.beneficiary_id, b.rendering_npi, b.billing_npi,
    b.service_date, b.hcpcs, b.billed_minutes,
    COALESCE(v.verified_minutes, 0) AS verified_minutes,
    b.billed_minutes - COALESCE(v.verified_minutes, 0) AS excess_minutes,
    b.paid_amount,
    CASE
      WHEN v.beneficiary_id IS NULL THEN 'NO_EVV_RECORD'
      WHEN b.billed_minutes > v.verified_minutes * (1 + :variance_tolerance_pct)
           THEN 'BILLED_EXCEEDS_VERIFIED'
      ELSE 'WITHIN_TOLERANCE'
    END AS variance_class
FROM billed b
LEFT JOIN verified v
       ON  v.beneficiary_id = b.beneficiary_id
       AND v.attendant_npi  = b.rendering_npi
       AND v.service_date   = b.service_date
WHERE v.beneficiary_id IS NULL
   OR b.billed_minutes > v.verified_minutes * (1 + :variance_tolerance_pct)
ORDER BY excess_minutes DESC, b.paid_amount DESC;

-- Reciprocal pass (data-integrity, not fraud): verified visits with no matching claim.
-- A high reciprocal rate means your EVV-to-claims key is broken and the forward
-- direction above will over-report. Run the reciprocal FIRST and clear it.
tests.threshold: :variance_tolerance_pct = 0.10 absorbs rounding between EVV minutes and billed units; set it to 0 once your unit-to-minute mapping is proven. Before treating NO_EVV_RECORD as a finding, establish the match rate on the reciprocal pass — a match rate below ~95% means the join key (not the provider) is the problem. Prioritise agencies where NO_EVV_RECORD exceeds ~5% of paid lines. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CD-09 (Proof-of-delivery / proof-of-service capture and retention). Secondary: MD-24 (Self-directed-care approver-independence — carries the EVV / Cures Act §12006 anchor), CD-03 (Reasonable-and-necessary documentation).

failure_map.reading: No billed-vs-delivered reconciliation exists between EVV and claims. Build it — see the GAP NOTE below on the missing dedicated EVV-reconciliation control.
The variance report is defined but was not produced for the period.
Variances were resolved by accepting an after-the-fact manual visit entry with no independent corroboration.
Reconciliation runs at aggregate agency level and nets overs against unders, so line-level phantom visits vanish in the average.
The reconciliation is asserted but no dated variance report or disposition is retained.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Service billed after date of death
tests.hypothesis: If the Death Master File match is absent, run late, or matched only against eligibility rather than against paid claims, in-home services continue to be billed for a beneficiary who has died. The signature is unambiguous: a service date after the recorded date of death.
tests.check: Join paid time-based claim lines to the beneficiary date-of-death and flag any service date strictly after it. Report separately the claims dated after death but SUBMITTED before the death was recorded (a data-latency finding) and those submitted after (a stronger candidate).
tests.sql:
-- TEST 5 - Service dates after date of death
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :grace_days (0)
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.

SELECT
    cl.claim_id, cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id,
    cl.billing_npi, cl.rendering_npi, cl.hcpcs,
    cl.service_date, b.date_of_death,
    (cl.service_date - b.date_of_death) AS days_after_death,
    cl.units, cl.paid_amount,
    cl.claim_submission_date,
    CASE
      WHEN cl.claim_submission_date > b.death_record_load_date
        THEN 'SUBMITTED_AFTER_DEATH_KNOWN'      -- stronger review candidate
      ELSE 'SUBMITTED_BEFORE_DEATH_KNOWN'        -- likely data-latency; still recoverable
    END AS submission_class
FROM claim_lines cl
JOIN beneficiary b
  ON b.beneficiary_id = cl.beneficiary_id
WHERE b.date_of_death IS NOT NULL
  AND cl.service_date > b.date_of_death + :grace_days
  AND cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
ORDER BY days_after_death DESC, cl.paid_amount DESC;

-- Companion: the same test against CAPITATION payments, not just FFS claim lines,
-- which is where the larger dollar exposure usually sits.
tests.threshold: :grace_days = 0 for in-home services — unlike facility claims there is no legitimate post-death service. Some warehouses carry an imprecise date of death from a secondary source; if yours does, set :grace_days = 1 and treat same-day-as-death claims as a separate, lower-priority bucket rather than suppressing them. Escalate any provider with ≥3 post-death claims. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: MD-08 (Deceased-enrollee detection via SSA Death Master File match). Secondary: MD-06 (Enrollee eligibility verification via authoritative electronic data sources).

failure_map.reading: No DMF match runs. MD-08's monthly exception disposition does not exist.
MD-08 is specified monthly but the match did not run for one or more months in the period — establish what was exposed in the gap.
DMF matches were dispositioned as false positives in bulk without a documented identity-resolution step.
The match updates eligibility but never sweeps already-paid claims, so it prevents future capitation without recovering paid FFS.
No retained match output or dated disposition per exception.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: In-home services billed during incarceration or an institutional stay
tests.hypothesis: In-home attendant care cannot be furnished to someone who is in jail, in an inpatient bed, or in a nursing facility. Where the incarceration/institutional status match is absent or runs only against eligibility, home-care claims overlap institutional custody dates cleanly.
tests.check: Interval-join paid in-home claim lines against (a) the corrections roster and (b) inpatient/SNF/ICF institutional stays, and flag any service date falling inside a custody or admission window. The institutional-stay half of this test is usually higher-volume and entirely internal to the payer's own claims.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 6 - In-home service dates inside an incarceration or institutional-stay window
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end
-- Note CAA 2024 requires SUSPEND-not-terminate for incarcerated enrollees (eff. 1/1/2026);
-- the control objective is suspension of PAYMENT, not loss of eligibility.

-- 6a: overlap with corrections custody
SELECT
    'INCARCERATION' AS conflict_type,
    cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.billing_npi, cl.rendering_npi,
    cl.service_date, cl.hcpcs, cl.units, cl.paid_amount,
    inc.book_date, inc.release_date, inc.facility_id AS conflict_facility
FROM claim_lines cl
JOIN incarceration_roster inc
  ON  inc.beneficiary_id = cl.beneficiary_id
  AND cl.service_date >= inc.book_date
  AND cl.service_date <= COALESCE(inc.release_date, DATE '9999-12-31')
WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide','hcbs_in_home')
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'

UNION ALL

-- 6b: overlap with an inpatient / SNF / ICF stay (entirely internal to your claims)
SELECT
    'INSTITUTIONAL_STAY' AS conflict_type,
    cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.billing_npi, cl.rendering_npi,
    cl.service_date, cl.hcpcs, cl.units, cl.paid_amount,
    st.admit_date AS book_date, st.discharge_date AS release_date, st.facility_type
FROM claim_lines cl
JOIN institutional_stay st
  ON  st.beneficiary_id = cl.beneficiary_id
  -- exclude the admit and discharge days themselves: partial-day home care is legitimate
  AND cl.service_date >  st.admit_date
  AND cl.service_date <  COALESCE(st.discharge_date, DATE '9999-12-31')
WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide','hcbs_in_home')
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
ORDER BY paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: No statistical threshold — a conflict is categorical. The tunables are the boundary-day rules: EXCLUDE admit and discharge days (partial-day home care around a hospitalisation is legitimate and will otherwise generate large false-positive volume), and consider excluding the booking day for incarceration. Rank by paid_amount and by conflict days per beneficiary; a single boundary-adjacent day is noise, a 30-day run is not. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: MD-22 (Incarceration/institutional-status match — suspend claims/capitation during incarceration). Secondary: CD-17 (Coordination-of-benefits / setting documentation control), MD-06 (Enrollee eligibility verification).

failure_map.reading: No corrections-data feed and no cross-setting conflict edit. MD-22's monthly exception report does not exist.
MD-22 is specified monthly; the roster match did not run, or ran without the paid-claims join it specifies.
Conflicts were closed on an unverified assertion that the enrollee was released early.
The match suspends future capitation only and never tests already-paid in-home FFS claims — which is where this scheme lives.
Match runs but no dated exception report with dispositions is retained.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Excluded aide or agency with paid claims after the exclusion date
tests.hypothesis: If monthly exclusion re-screening is absent, run against a stale LEIE file, or screened against the enrolled provider roster but not the rendering-provider field on claims, an excluded individual continues to render and be paid for in-home services. Home care is the highest-risk setting for this because the rendering party is an individual aide, often not separately enrolled.
tests.check: Join paid claim lines to the exclusion list on both billing and rendering NPI (and, where you hold it, on the attendant roster identifier) and flag any service date on or after the exclusion date and before any reinstatement date.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 7 - Paid claims rendered or billed by an excluded party
-- Screen BOTH the billing entity and the rendering individual. In home care the
-- rendering individual is the usual gap.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.

WITH excluded AS (
  SELECT npi, exclusion_date, reinstate_date, exclusion_type, source_file_date
  FROM exclusion_list                       -- OIG LEIE + GSA SAM + state exclusion lists
  WHERE npi IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.service_date, cl.hcpcs, cl.paid_amount,
    cl.billing_npi, cl.rendering_npi,
    e.npi            AS excluded_npi,
    CASE WHEN e.npi = cl.rendering_npi THEN 'RENDERING' ELSE 'BILLING' END AS excluded_role,
    e.exclusion_date, e.reinstate_date, e.exclusion_type,
    (cl.service_date - e.exclusion_date) AS days_after_exclusion
FROM claim_lines cl
JOIN excluded e
  ON e.npi IN (cl.rendering_npi, cl.billing_npi)
WHERE cl.service_date >= e.exclusion_date
  AND (e.reinstate_date IS NULL OR cl.service_date < e.reinstate_date)
  AND cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
ORDER BY days_after_exclusion DESC, cl.paid_amount DESC;

-- Companion (the harder, more valuable pass): match the ATTENDANT ROSTER by
-- name + DOB-hash against LEIE for aides who hold no NPI. Do this inside your own
-- environment; it is identity matching and needs a documented resolution step.
tests.threshold: Categorical, not statistical — but exclusion matching by name is noisy, so treat NPI-keyed matches as high-confidence and name-keyed roster matches as candidates requiring identity resolution before any action. Screen against the LEIE file version dated closest to (and not after) each service date; PE-08 specifies monthly alignment to the ~10th-of-month LEIE release. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PE-08 (Monthly automated exclusion re-screening of active providers). Secondary: PE-07 (Exclusion screening at enrollment), MD-04 (Federal-database screening of providers/owners).

failure_map.reading: No monthly re-screen. PE-08's dated LEIE-version + roster-snapshot evidence does not exist.
Re-screen skipped one or more months; PE-08's evidence artifact names the file version precisely so gaps are provable.
A match was identified and the provider continued to be paid pending 'verification' with no payment hold.
The screen covers enrolled billing entities only and never touches the rendering/attendant population — the actual exposure in home care.
No retained record of the LEIE file version used or the roster snapshot screened.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Authorized-vs-billed hours overage against the service plan
tests.hypothesis: Where utilization control is absent or reviews medical necessity without comparing delivered units to the authorized service plan, billed hours drift above the authorization. Sustained overage against a person-centred service plan is both an overpayment signature and a plan-integrity signal.
tests.check: Aggregate billed units per beneficiary per HCPCS per week and compare to the authorized units for that period from the service plan / prior authorization. Report the overage ratio and the number of consecutive weeks in overage.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 8 - Billed units above the authorized service-plan units
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :overage_tolerance_pct (0.05)
-- Portability: DATE_TRUNC is PostgreSQL/Snowflake/DuckDB style; elsewhere use DATETRUNC (SQL Server),
--   TRUNC(date, 'MM') (Oracle) or DATE_TRUNC(date, MONTH) (BigQuery).

WITH billed_weekly AS (
  SELECT
      cl.beneficiary_id,
      cl.hcpcs,
      cl.billing_npi,
      DATE_TRUNC('week', cl.service_date) AS service_week,
      SUM(cl.units)       AS billed_units,
      SUM(cl.paid_amount) AS paid_amount
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide','hcbs_in_home')
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  GROUP BY cl.beneficiary_id, cl.hcpcs, cl.billing_npi, DATE_TRUNC('week', cl.service_date)
),
authorized AS (
  SELECT
      sp.beneficiary_id, sp.hcpcs,
      sp.authorized_units_per_week,
      sp.effective_start, sp.effective_end
  FROM service_plan sp                      -- or your prior_auth table
  WHERE sp.status = 'ACTIVE'
)
SELECT
    b.beneficiary_id, b.hcpcs, b.billing_npi, b.service_week,
    b.billed_units,
    a.authorized_units_per_week,
    b.billed_units - a.authorized_units_per_week AS overage_units,
    ROUND(b.billed_units / NULLIF(a.authorized_units_per_week, 0), 2) AS overage_ratio,
    b.paid_amount,
    CASE WHEN a.beneficiary_id IS NULL THEN 'NO_AUTHORIZATION_ON_FILE' ELSE 'OVER_AUTHORIZATION' END
      AS overage_class
FROM billed_weekly b
LEFT JOIN authorized a
       ON  a.beneficiary_id = b.beneficiary_id
       AND a.hcpcs          = b.hcpcs
       AND b.service_week BETWEEN a.effective_start AND COALESCE(a.effective_end, DATE '9999-12-31')
WHERE a.beneficiary_id IS NULL
   OR b.billed_units > a.authorized_units_per_week * (1 + :overage_tolerance_pct)
ORDER BY overage_ratio DESC NULLS LAST, b.paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: :overage_tolerance_pct = 0.05 absorbs legitimate week-boundary spill (a shift spanning midnight Sunday). NO_AUTHORIZATION_ON_FILE is usually the larger and more actionable bucket and often indicates a data-linkage break rather than fraud — separate it before reporting. Prioritise beneficiaries with ≥4 consecutive overage weeks or an overage_ratio ≥1.25. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: MD-14 (Utilization control & SURS medical-review program). Secondary: CB-08 (Quantity / frequency-limit edits), CD-10 (Continued-need / recertification documentation control).

failure_map.reading: No authorization-to-delivery comparison exists in the utilization-control program.
MD-14 is specified continuous but produced no case dispositions for the period.
Overages were retroactively authorized without a documented reassessment of need.
Review is triggered by cost thresholds only, so a low-rate service in chronic overage never surfaces.
Medical-review case dispositions are not retained in a form that ties back to the specific overage.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Duplicate time units across programs, payers, or agencies
tests.hypothesis: If duplicate detection keys only on (claim, line, provider) it will not catch the same beneficiary-hour billed by two different agencies, or under two different programs (waiver vs state plan), or to two different payers. The duplicate is real; the key is wrong.
tests.check: Group paid time-based lines by beneficiary + service date + service window and flag any group containing lines from more than one billing entity, program, or payer where the combined units exceed what a single beneficiary could receive.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 9 - Cross-agency / cross-program duplicate time units for one beneficiary-day
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :minutes_per_unit (15), :max_beneficiary_minutes_per_day (1440)

WITH bene_day AS (
  SELECT
      cl.beneficiary_id,
      cl.service_date,
      SUM(COALESCE(cl.service_minutes, cl.units * :minutes_per_unit)) AS total_minutes,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cl.billing_npi)   AS distinct_agencies,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cl.payer_program) AS distinct_programs,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cl.rendering_npi) AS distinct_aides,
      SUM(cl.paid_amount)              AS paid_amount
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide','hcbs_in_home')
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  GROUP BY cl.beneficiary_id, cl.service_date
)
SELECT
    beneficiary_id, service_date,
    total_minutes,
    ROUND(total_minutes / 60.0, 2) AS total_hours,
    distinct_agencies, distinct_programs, distinct_aides, paid_amount,
    CASE
      WHEN total_minutes > :max_beneficiary_minutes_per_day THEN 'EXCEEDS_24H_OF_CARE'
      WHEN distinct_agencies > 1 THEN 'MULTI_AGENCY_SAME_DAY'
      ELSE 'MULTI_PROGRAM_SAME_DAY'
    END AS duplicate_class
FROM bene_day
WHERE total_minutes > :max_beneficiary_minutes_per_day
   OR distinct_agencies > 1
   OR distinct_programs > 1
ORDER BY total_minutes DESC, paid_amount DESC;

-- Tighter companion: exact-duplicate line pairs across agencies - 
-- same beneficiary_id, service_date, hcpcs and units, different billing_npi.
tests.threshold: EXCEEDS_24H_OF_CARE is arithmetic and always reviewable. MULTI_AGENCY_SAME_DAY is legitimately common (a nurse visit plus an aide shift) and is a triage signal, not a finding — rank it by total_minutes and only escalate above roughly the 95th percentile of your own beneficiary-day minute distribution. Compute that percentile first; do not import a number. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-15 (Duplicate claim / line detection). Secondary: CD-17 (Coordination-of-benefits / setting documentation control).

failure_map.reading: No duplicate detection beyond exact claim resubmission.
CB-15's duplicate-hit disposition log is empty for the period.
Duplicate hits were overridden at adjudication to clear a backlog.
The duplicate key includes billing_npi, so cross-agency duplicates can never match. This is the defining defect for this test.
Hits are suppressed silently at the edit engine with no retained disposition log.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Representative-approver conflict in self-directed care
tests.hypothesis: In self-directed/consumer-directed programs the person approving the attendant's timesheet is often the beneficiary's representative. Where the approver-independence control is absent, a representative with a financial or household tie to the attendant approves their own household's hours. The data signature is a representative-attendant pair sharing address or contact details, or a representative approving an implausible concentration of hours.
tests.check: Join the representative registry to the attendant registry on hashed address and hashed phone, and separately rank representatives by total approved hours and by the share of a single attendant's hours they approve. Do the identity comparison on hashed values inside your own environment.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 10 - Self-directed care: representative-approver conflict
-- Identity comparison uses HASHED values, computed and compared inside your own
-- environment. No identifiers leave the payer.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_conflict_signals (1 for triage, 2 for a prioritised queue)

WITH approvals AS (
  SELECT
      ts.representative_id,
      ts.attendant_id,
      ts.beneficiary_id,
      SUM(ts.approved_minutes) AS approved_minutes,
      COUNT(*)                 AS approved_timesheets,
      SUM(ts.paid_amount)      AS paid_amount
  FROM timesheet_approval ts
  WHERE ts.approval_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND ts.program_type = 'SELF_DIRECTED'
  GROUP BY ts.representative_id, ts.attendant_id, ts.beneficiary_id
),
conflicts AS (
  SELECT
      a.*,
      CASE WHEN r.address_hash = at.address_hash THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS shared_address,
      CASE WHEN r.phone_hash   = at.phone_hash   THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS shared_phone,
      CASE WHEN r.surname_hash = at.surname_hash THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS shared_surname
  FROM approvals a
  JOIN representative r ON r.representative_id = a.representative_id
  JOIN attendant      at ON at.attendant_id    = a.attendant_id
)
SELECT
    representative_id, attendant_id, beneficiary_id,
    approved_minutes, ROUND(approved_minutes / 60.0, 2) AS approved_hours,
    approved_timesheets, paid_amount,
    shared_address, shared_phone, shared_surname,
    (shared_address + shared_phone + shared_surname) AS conflict_signal_count
FROM conflicts
WHERE (shared_address + shared_phone + shared_surname) >= :min_conflict_signals
ORDER BY conflict_signal_count DESC, paid_amount DESC;

-- Companion, no registry join required: representatives in the top percentile of
-- approved hours, or approving >:concentration_pct of one attendant's total hours.
tests.threshold: :min_conflict_signals = 1 for triage, 2 for a prioritised queue. Be careful: a shared address between representative and attendant is EXPECTED and lawful in many family-caregiver programs — this test identifies where the approver-independence control should have been APPLIED, not where fraud occurred. That distinction belongs in the output header. :concentration_pct = 0.90 of one attendant's hours approved by one representative is a reasonable companion cut. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: MD-24 (Self-directed-care approver-independence control). Secondary: PI-21 (Beneficiary-side integrity analytics — roster-overlap detection).

failure_map.reading: No conflict screen between representative and attendant registries exists.
MD-24 specifies a continuous screen plus quarterly sampling; neither ran.
Conflicts were identified and waived without the independent second-approver MD-24 requires.
The screen matches exact name strings only, so it misses hashed-address and phone ties and any name variation.
No retained conflict-screen result or sampling disposition.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Attendant–beneficiary roster overlap and recruiter clustering
tests.hypothesis: Where beneficiary-side integrity analytics are absent, schemes that pay beneficiaries to participate leave two signatures: individuals appearing on both the beneficiary roll and the staff/attendant roster, and beneficiaries whose enrollments cluster tightly around one recruiter, address, or referring entity.
tests.check: Intersect the attendant roster with the beneficiary roll on hashed identity, and separately count beneficiaries per shared residential address hash and per enrolling/referring entity, flagging clusters above the population norm.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 11 - Roster overlap + address/recruiter clustering
-- Hashed identity comparison inside your own environment only.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :cluster_threshold

-- 11a: individuals on BOTH the attendant roster and the beneficiary roll
SELECT
    'ROSTER_OVERLAP' AS signal,
    at.attendant_id,
    b.beneficiary_id,
    at.employer_billing_npi,
    COUNT(cl.claim_line_id) AS paid_lines,
    SUM(cl.paid_amount)     AS paid_amount
FROM attendant at
JOIN beneficiary b
  ON  b.identity_hash = at.identity_hash        -- e.g. sha256(lower(name)||dob||ssn_last4)
LEFT JOIN claim_lines cl
  ON  cl.rendering_npi = at.attendant_npi
  AND cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
GROUP BY at.attendant_id, b.beneficiary_id, at.employer_billing_npi

UNION ALL

-- 11b: beneficiaries clustered at one residential address served by one agency
SELECT
    'ADDRESS_CLUSTER' AS signal,
    CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR)      AS attendant_id,
    CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR)      AS beneficiary_id,
    cl.billing_npi             AS employer_billing_npi,
    COUNT(DISTINCT cl.beneficiary_id) AS paid_lines,
    SUM(cl.paid_amount)               AS paid_amount
FROM claim_lines cl
JOIN service_location loc ON loc.beneficiary_id = cl.beneficiary_id
WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide','hcbs_in_home')
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
GROUP BY loc.address_hash, cl.billing_npi
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT cl.beneficiary_id) >= :cluster_threshold
ORDER BY paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: :cluster_threshold = 5 distinct beneficiaries at one address hash served by one agency is a starting cut — but group homes, assisted-living settings and large apartment buildings will dominate the output, so exclude known congregate addresses FIRST or the test is unusable. For roster overlap, any hit is worth identity resolution; the volume is small. Compute your own distribution of beneficiaries-per-address before fixing the threshold. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PI-21 (Beneficiary-side integrity analytics). Secondary: PI-20 (Provider NPI/credential-footprint consistency monitoring), MD-24 (Self-directed-care approver-independence).

failure_map.reading: No enrollment+claims+HR-roster join exists. PI-21's recruiter-cluster / roster-overlap exception report does not exist.
PI-21 is specified monthly; the report was not produced.
Overlaps were dismissed as coincidence with no identity-resolution step recorded.
The analytic runs on claims only and never joins the HR/attendant roster, so the defining signal is unavailable to it.
No retained exception report or dispositions.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Uniform-duration visits — the templated-timesheet signature
tests.hypothesis: Real care visits vary in length. Where the copy-forward/templated-documentation control is absent or applies to clinical notes but not to time entry, manufactured timesheets show near-zero variance: every visit exactly the same duration, often starting on the same clock minute. Low variance is not proof of anything, but it is a cheap and effective prioritisation signal.
tests.check: For each rendering provider with enough volume, compute the standard deviation and the modal share of billed visit durations, and the share of visits starting at an exact quarter-hour. Rank providers by lowest duration variance.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 12 - Uniform-duration / templated-timesheet signature
-- Prioritisation signal only. A low-variance provider is a review candidate, never a finding.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :minutes_per_unit (15), :min_visits (30),
--         :max_coefficient_of_variation (0.05), :max_quarter_start_share (0.95)

WITH visit_durations AS (
  SELECT
      cl.rendering_npi,
      cl.billing_npi,
      cl.claim_line_id,
      COALESCE(cl.service_minutes, cl.units * :minutes_per_unit) AS duration_minutes,
      EXTRACT(MINUTE FROM cl.service_begin_datetime)             AS start_minute
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide','hcbs_in_home')
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
),
provider_stats AS (
  SELECT
      rendering_npi,
      billing_npi,
      COUNT(*)                       AS visit_count,
      AVG(duration_minutes)          AS mean_minutes,
      STDDEV(duration_minutes)       AS sd_minutes,
      AVG(CASE WHEN start_minute IN (0, 15, 30, 45) THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) AS exact_quarter_start_share
  FROM visit_durations
  GROUP BY rendering_npi, billing_npi
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_visits
)
SELECT
    rendering_npi, billing_npi, visit_count,
    ROUND(mean_minutes, 1) AS mean_minutes,
    ROUND(sd_minutes, 2)   AS sd_minutes,
    ROUND(sd_minutes / NULLIF(mean_minutes, 0), 4) AS coefficient_of_variation,
    ROUND(exact_quarter_start_share, 3) AS exact_quarter_start_share
FROM provider_stats
WHERE sd_minutes / NULLIF(mean_minutes, 0) < :max_coefficient_of_variation
   OR exact_quarter_start_share > :max_quarter_start_share
ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation ASC;
tests.threshold: :min_visits = 30 keeps the statistic meaningful. :max_coefficient_of_variation = 0.05 (i.e. duration SD under 5% of the mean) is a starting cut, but note that authorised fixed-length shifts legitimately produce near-zero variance — so this test's value depends entirely on excluding fixed-shift authorisations first. :max_quarter_start_share = 0.95 is a second, independent signal. Use both together; either alone is weak. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CD-07 (Copy-forward / templated-note control). Secondary: CD-06 (Signature legibility & attestation control), CD-09 (Proof-of-delivery / proof-of-service capture).

failure_map.reading: No cloned-documentation control covers time entry at all.
CD-07 specifies a quarterly cloned-note audit; it was not performed in the period.
The audit identified templated entries and no coding/documentation corrective action followed.
The control examines narrative notes only and never inspects the time fields, which is where the manufacture happens.
No retained cloned-note audit result.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Missing or invalid plan-of-care order behind ongoing in-home services
tests.hypothesis: Home-health and HCBS services require a signed order/plan of care from an enrolled practitioner. Where valid-order verification is absent or checks only that a field is populated, services are furnished against a missing order, an expired plan of care, or an ordering NPI that is not enrolled, is deceased, or is excluded.
tests.check: For each paid in-home claim line, confirm an active signed order exists covering the service date and that the ordering NPI resolves to an enrolled, non-excluded, living practitioner. Report each failure reason separately — they have different remediations.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 13 - Order integrity behind ongoing in-home services
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

WITH matched_order AS (
  -- for each claim line, pick one order that began on or before the service date: an order
  -- whose effective window covers the service date is preferred (latest started first);
  -- only when no order covers the date does the latest-started order stand in, so that the
  -- CASE below labels the line ORDER_EXPIRED rather than NO_ORDER_ON_FILE.
  SELECT cl.claim_line_id, o.order_id, o.signature_date, o.effective_start, o.effective_end,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cl.claim_line_id
                            ORDER BY CASE WHEN cl.service_date <= COALESCE(o.effective_end, DATE '9999-12-31')
                                          THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
                                     o.effective_start DESC) AS rn
  FROM claim_lines cl
  JOIN service_order o
    ON  o.beneficiary_id = cl.beneficiary_id
    AND o.hcpcs_group    = cl.hcpcs_group
    AND o.effective_start <= cl.service_date
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
)
SELECT
    cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.billing_npi, cl.ordering_npi,
    cl.service_date, cl.hcpcs, cl.paid_amount,
    o.order_id, o.signature_date, o.effective_start, o.effective_end,
    p.enrollment_status, p.date_of_death AS ordering_provider_dod,
    CASE
      WHEN o.order_id IS NULL                                   THEN 'NO_ORDER_ON_FILE'
      WHEN o.signature_date IS NULL                             THEN 'ORDER_UNSIGNED'
      WHEN cl.service_date > COALESCE(o.effective_end, DATE '9999-12-31')
                                                                THEN 'ORDER_EXPIRED'
      WHEN cl.service_date < o.signature_date                   THEN 'SERVICE_BEFORE_SIGNATURE'
      WHEN p.npi IS NULL                                        THEN 'ORDERING_NPI_NOT_FOUND'
      WHEN p.enrollment_status <> 'ACTIVE'                      THEN 'ORDERING_NPI_NOT_ENROLLED'
      WHEN p.date_of_death IS NOT NULL
           AND cl.service_date > p.date_of_death                THEN 'ORDERING_PROVIDER_DECEASED'
      ELSE 'OK'
    END AS order_defect
FROM claim_lines cl
LEFT JOIN matched_order o ON o.claim_line_id = cl.claim_line_id AND o.rn = 1
LEFT JOIN provider p ON p.npi = cl.ordering_npi
WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide',
                              'private_duty_nursing','hcbs_in_home')
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND (o.order_id IS NULL
       OR o.signature_date IS NULL
       OR cl.service_date > COALESCE(o.effective_end, DATE '9999-12-31')
       OR cl.service_date < o.signature_date
       OR p.npi IS NULL
       OR p.enrollment_status <> 'ACTIVE'
       OR (p.date_of_death IS NOT NULL AND cl.service_date > p.date_of_death))
ORDER BY order_defect, cl.paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: Categorical. But expect NO_ORDER_ON_FILE to be dominated by orders that exist on paper and are simply not in the queried system — so establish your order-capture completeness rate first and report it alongside. ORDERING_PROVIDER_DECEASED and ORDERING_NPI_NOT_ENROLLED are low-volume and high-signal; work those first regardless of dollar value. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CD-08 (Valid-order verification, including source-verified ordering-provider identity). Secondary: CD-10 (Continued-need / recertification documentation), CD-03 (Reasonable-and-necessary documentation).

failure_map.reading: No pre-service order verification. CD-08's signed-order-plus-verified-identity artifact does not exist.
CD-08 is per-service; a population of paid services in the period has no corresponding verification.
Services proceeded on a verbal order with the written order never obtained.
The check confirms an ordering NPI is present and syntactically valid but never source-verifies it against PECOS/NPPES — so stolen and deceased-provider NPIs pass.
Orders exist clinically but are not retrievable in the timeframe CD-11 requires.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Agency-level hours-per-beneficiary peer outlier
tests.hypothesis: Individual-visit tests miss the agency that bills a defensible amount per visit but far more visits per beneficiary than its peers. Where routine claims-aberrancy analytics are absent or run without a peer-group definition, this drift is invisible. This is the family's MEVIA-style peer-outlier test.
tests.check: Compute hours billed per beneficiary per month for each billing agency, compute the mean and standard deviation within a peer group (service type × region × program), and report agencies above a z-score cutoff.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 14 - Peer-group outlier: hours per beneficiary per month, by agency
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :minutes_per_unit (15), :z_threshold (2.5),
--         :min_beneficiaries (20), :min_peer_group_size (10)
-- Portability: DATE_TRUNC is PostgreSQL/Snowflake/DuckDB style; elsewhere use DATETRUNC (SQL Server),
--   TRUNC(date, 'MM') (Oracle) or DATE_TRUNC(date, MONTH) (BigQuery).
-- Portability: JOIN ... USING (...) is not accepted by SQL Server; write the ON equalities out there.

WITH agency_month AS (
  SELECT
      cl.billing_npi,
      pr.peer_region,
      cl.payer_program,
      DATE_TRUNC('month', cl.service_date) AS service_month,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cl.beneficiary_id)    AS beneficiaries,
      SUM(COALESCE(cl.service_minutes, cl.units * :minutes_per_unit)) / 60.0 AS billed_hours,
      SUM(cl.paid_amount) AS paid_amount
  FROM claim_lines cl
  JOIN provider pr ON pr.npi = cl.billing_npi
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide','hcbs_in_home')
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  GROUP BY cl.billing_npi, pr.peer_region, cl.payer_program,
           DATE_TRUNC('month', cl.service_date)
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT cl.beneficiary_id) >= :min_beneficiaries
),
rates AS (
  SELECT *, billed_hours / NULLIF(beneficiaries, 0) AS hours_per_beneficiary
  FROM agency_month
),
peer AS (
  SELECT peer_region, payer_program, service_month,
         AVG(hours_per_beneficiary)    AS peer_mean,
         STDDEV(hours_per_beneficiary) AS peer_sd,
         COUNT(*)                      AS peer_n
  FROM rates
  GROUP BY peer_region, payer_program, service_month
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_peer_group_size          -- a peer group of 3 is not a peer group
)
SELECT
    r.billing_npi, r.peer_region, r.payer_program, r.service_month,
    r.beneficiaries,
    ROUND(r.hours_per_beneficiary, 2) AS hours_per_beneficiary,
    ROUND(p.peer_mean, 2)             AS peer_mean,
    ROUND((r.hours_per_beneficiary - p.peer_mean) / NULLIF(p.peer_sd, 0), 2) AS z_score,
    p.peer_n,
    r.paid_amount
FROM rates r
JOIN peer p USING (peer_region, payer_program, service_month)
WHERE (r.hours_per_beneficiary - p.peer_mean) / NULLIF(p.peer_sd, 0) > :z_threshold
ORDER BY z_score DESC;
tests.threshold: :z_threshold = 2.5 is the conventional starting cut. :min_beneficiaries = 20 and :min_peer_group_size = 10 matter more than the z-cut: a z-score computed over a handful of agencies is noise dressed as statistics. Because the hours-per-beneficiary distribution is usually right-skewed, consider a robust alternative (median + MAD, or a raw percentile cut at the 95th) before defending a z-score. Persistence across ≥3 months is a far stronger signal than a single-month spike. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PI-01 (Routine claims-aberrancy analytics — peer-outlier / statistical). Secondary: MD-14 (Utilization control & SURS), PI-02 (Provider risk-scoring & review-prioritization model).

failure_map.reading: No routine peer-outlier analytics. PI-01's outlier-alert disposition log does not exist.
PI-01 is specified monthly; no run occurred in the period.
Outlier alerts were generated and closed without review to manage volume.
The peer group is defined too broadly (all providers statewide) so genuine outliers regress to the mean and never clear the cut.
Alerts exist in a BI tool with no retained, dated disposition record.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: New-agency billing velocity in the first 90 days
tests.hypothesis: Fly-by-night home-care agencies bill hard and fast before any review cycle reaches them. Where the new-provider billing-velocity watch is absent, an agency can reach peak billing within weeks of enrollment and exit before the first revalidation. The signature is a billing ramp far steeper than the peer norm in the first 60–90 days.
tests.check: For agencies enrolled within the lookback, compute cumulative paid amount and distinct beneficiaries by days-since-enrollment, and compare the 90-day figure to the peer-cohort distribution for agencies of the same type and region.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 15 - New-agency billing velocity (first 90 days)
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :velocity_window_days (90), :percentile_cut (0.95)
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.

WITH new_agencies AS (
  SELECT npi AS billing_npi, enrollment_effective_date, peer_region, provider_type
  FROM provider
  WHERE enrollment_effective_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND provider_type IN ('HOME_HEALTH_AGENCY','PERSONAL_CARE_AGENCY','HCBS_PROVIDER')
),
early_billing AS (
  SELECT
      n.billing_npi, n.enrollment_effective_date, n.peer_region, n.provider_type,
      SUM(cl.paid_amount)               AS paid_first_window,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cl.beneficiary_id) AS beneficiaries_first_window,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cl.rendering_npi)  AS aides_first_window,
      MIN(cl.service_date)              AS first_service_date,
      (MIN(cl.service_date) - n.enrollment_effective_date) AS days_to_first_claim
  FROM new_agencies n
  JOIN claim_lines cl
    ON  cl.billing_npi   = n.billing_npi
    AND cl.service_date >= n.enrollment_effective_date
    AND cl.service_date <  n.enrollment_effective_date + :velocity_window_days
  WHERE cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  GROUP BY n.billing_npi, n.enrollment_effective_date, n.peer_region, n.provider_type
)
SELECT
    e.*,
    PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY provider_type, peer_region
                         ORDER BY paid_first_window) AS cohort_percentile
FROM early_billing e
QUALIFY PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY provider_type, peer_region
                             ORDER BY paid_first_window) >= :percentile_cut
ORDER BY paid_first_window DESC;

-- QUALIFY is Snowflake/BigQuery/Teradata. In Postgres/SQL Server, wrap the
-- SELECT in a subquery and filter on cohort_percentile in the outer WHERE.
tests.threshold: :percentile_cut = 0.95 within a same-type, same-region cohort is more defensible than any absolute dollar figure, because it self-calibrates to your market. days_to_first_claim below ~7 is an independent signal worth surfacing separately — an agency billing within a week of enrollment had a patient panel before it was enrolled. A high beneficiaries-to-aides ratio in the first window is a third. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PE-15 (New-provider billing-velocity watch, first 60-90 days). Secondary: PE-16 (Acquisition-velocity flag), PI-02 (Provider risk-scoring & review-prioritization model).

failure_map.reading: No velocity watch on newly enrolled providers.
PE-15 exists on paper; no watch list was produced for the cohort enrolled in the period.
Velocity flags raised no prepayment review or site visit.
The watch uses a fixed statewide dollar threshold rather than a cohort percentile, so it misses fast-ramping agencies in low-cost regions.
No retained watch list or disposition.

tests.family_title: Home-health / attendant-care time integrity
tests.name: Recertification lapse on continuing in-home services
tests.hypothesis: Ongoing in-home services require periodic re-documentation of continued need. Where the continued-need control is absent or tracked in a system disconnected from claims, services continue to be billed past the recertification interval with no current documented need — the largest quiet driver of insufficient-documentation improper payments in this family.
tests.check: For each beneficiary with continuous service, compute days since the most recent recertification/reassessment as at each service date, and flag services billed beyond the required interval. Report the paid amount in the lapsed window, which is the exposure figure.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 16 - Services billed past the recertification interval
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :recert_interval_days (varies by program - set per HCPCS group)
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.

WITH latest_recert AS (
  SELECT
      r.beneficiary_id,
      r.hcpcs_group,
      r.recert_date,
      LEAD(r.recert_date) OVER (PARTITION BY r.beneficiary_id, r.hcpcs_group
                                ORDER BY r.recert_date) AS next_recert_date
  FROM recertification r
)
SELECT
    cl.beneficiary_id, cl.billing_npi, cl.hcpcs, cl.service_date, cl.paid_amount,
    lr.recert_date         AS last_recert_date,
    (cl.service_date - lr.recert_date) AS days_since_recert,
    :recert_interval_days  AS required_interval_days,
    (cl.service_date - lr.recert_date) - :recert_interval_days AS days_lapsed
FROM claim_lines cl
LEFT JOIN latest_recert lr
       ON  lr.beneficiary_id = cl.beneficiary_id
       AND lr.hcpcs_group    = cl.hcpcs_group
       AND cl.service_date >= lr.recert_date
       AND (lr.next_recert_date IS NULL OR cl.service_date < lr.next_recert_date)
WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.service_category IN ('personal_care','attendant_care','home_health_aide',
                              'private_duty_nursing','hcbs_in_home')
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND (lr.recert_date IS NULL
       OR (cl.service_date - lr.recert_date) > :recert_interval_days)
ORDER BY days_lapsed DESC NULLS FIRST, cl.paid_amount DESC;

-- Roll up by beneficiary and by agency: exposure = SUM(paid_amount) in the lapsed window.
tests.threshold: :recert_interval_days is NOT a tunable judgement call — it is set by program rule and differs by service and by state waiver (home-health certification periods, HCBS annual person-centred plan reassessment, private-duty nursing). Set it per hcpcs_group from your own coverage policy; do not use a single global value. A grace period of 15–30 days before flagging is reasonable to absorb scheduling reality, but the grace period is an operational tolerance, not a coverage rule. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CD-10 (Continued-need / recertification documentation control for ongoing services — home health, DME rental, hospice). Secondary: CD-03 (Reasonable-and-necessary documentation), MD-14 (Utilization control & SURS).

failure_map.reading: No recertification tracking exists for in-home services.
CD-10 is per-interval; recertifications were not performed for a population of active beneficiaries.
Recertification was completed as a form exercise with no reassessment of need documented.
Tracking lives in the care-management system and never blocks or flags claims, so a lapse has no payment consequence.
Reassessments occurred but the continued-need note is not retained or retrievable.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: E&M level distribution outlier — high-level share vs specialty peers
tests.hypothesis: Where E&M level validation against the 2021 MDM/time guidelines is absent or runs only as a chart audit with no distribution view, systematic upcoding is invisible at the claim level and obvious at the provider level. Each individual level-4 or level-5 visit is defensible; the provider whose panel is 85% level-4/5 against a peer mean of 40% is the finding. This is the canonical peer-benchmark test.
tests.check: For each rendering provider, compute the share of office/outpatient E&M visits coded at the two highest levels, compute the mean and standard deviation of that share within a specialty peer group, and report providers above a z-score cutoff. Separate new-patient (99202–99205) from established-patient (99211–99215) distributions — mixing them distorts the share for any provider with an unusual new-patient mix.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 1 - E&M level distribution outlier (upcoding)
-- Carries a new/established split, a minimum-volume floor, and a minimum
-- peer-group size.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :z_threshold (2.5), :min_visits (50), :min_peer_n (15)

WITH em_lines AS (
  SELECT
      cl.rendering_npi,
      pr.specialty,
      pr.peer_region,
      CASE WHEN cl.cpt BETWEEN '99202' AND '99205' THEN 'NEW'
           WHEN cl.cpt BETWEEN '99211' AND '99215' THEN 'ESTABLISHED'
      END AS visit_class,
      CASE WHEN cl.cpt IN ('99204','99205','99214','99215') THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END AS is_high_level,
      cl.paid_amount
  FROM claim_lines cl
  JOIN provider pr ON pr.npi = cl.rendering_npi
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND (cl.cpt BETWEEN '99202' AND '99205' OR cl.cpt BETWEEN '99211' AND '99215')
),
prov AS (
  SELECT
      rendering_npi, specialty, peer_region, visit_class,
      COUNT(*)                AS visits,
      AVG(is_high_level)      AS high_em_share,
      SUM(paid_amount)        AS paid_amount
  FROM em_lines
  WHERE visit_class IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY rendering_npi, specialty, peer_region, visit_class
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_visits
),
peer AS (
  SELECT
      specialty, peer_region, visit_class,
      AVG(high_em_share)     AS peer_mean,
      STDDEV(high_em_share)  AS peer_sd,
      COUNT(*)               AS peer_n
  FROM prov
  GROUP BY specialty, peer_region, visit_class
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_peer_n            -- a peer group of four is not a peer group
)
SELECT
    p.rendering_npi, p.specialty, p.peer_region, p.visit_class,
    p.visits,
    ROUND(p.high_em_share, 3) AS high_em_share,
    ROUND(k.peer_mean, 3)     AS peer_mean,
    ROUND((p.high_em_share - k.peer_mean) / NULLIF(k.peer_sd, 0), 2) AS z_score,
    k.peer_n,
    p.paid_amount,
    -- exposure if the provider coded at the peer mean instead
    ROUND(p.paid_amount * (p.high_em_share - k.peer_mean) / NULLIF(p.high_em_share, 0), 0)
      AS indicative_delta_dollars
FROM prov p
JOIN peer k USING (specialty, peer_region, visit_class)
WHERE (p.high_em_share - k.peer_mean) / NULLIF(k.peer_sd, 0) > :z_threshold
ORDER BY z_score DESC;

-- indicative_delta_dollars is an ORDERING aid, not an overpayment estimate. Do not
-- put it in front of a provider. Extrapolation requires a valid statistical sample
-- (control PI-05), not a z-score.
tests.threshold: :z_threshold = 2.5 is the conventional starting cut. Two other parameters matter more: :min_visits = 50 keeps the share stable, and :min_peer_n = 15 keeps the peer statistics meaningful. The high-E&M share distribution is bounded at 0 and 1 and is usually not normal, so a z-score is a convenience, not a claim about probability — consider a raw 95th-percentile cut or a logit transform before defending the number to a provider. Peer group definition drives everything: too broad and genuine outliers regress to the mean, too narrow and every provider is an outlier in a group of three. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-03 (E&M level validation vs 2021 MDM/time; peer-benchmark for upcoding). Secondary: PI-01 (Routine claims-aberrancy analytics), CB-19 (Coding audit program with statistically valid sampling).

failure_map.reading: No E&M distribution or outlier report exists. CB-03's named evidence artifact — the E&M distribution / outlier report — does not exist.
CB-03 is specified monthly; no scan was run for one or more months in the period. Establish what was exposed in the interval.
Outliers were identified and no chart validation, education (PI-12) or edit change followed.
The benchmark uses a national or all-specialty comparison group rather than a like-for-like peer group, so the provider's own specialty norm is never the reference.
The distribution exists in a BI tool but no dated report and no reviewer disposition are retained.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Modifier-25 overuse — separately identifiable E&M alongside a same-day procedure
tests.hypothesis: Modifier 25 asserts that a significant, separately identifiable E&M service was performed on the same day as a procedure. Where modifier governance is absent or reviews only modifier 59, a provider can append 25 as a default and collect an E&M on top of every procedure. The signature is a modifier-25 attachment rate far above the peer norm — and, in the strongest cases, a rate at or near 100%, which is a statement that no procedure the provider ever performs is routine.
tests.check: For each rendering provider, compute the share of same-day E&M-plus-procedure encounters carrying modifier 25, benchmark within specialty, and flag providers above the cutoff. Report the near-100% cohort separately — it needs no statistics.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 2 - Modifier-25 attachment rate vs specialty peers
-- Modifier 25 = significant, separately identifiable E&M by the same physician on the
-- same day as a procedure. NCCI PTP edits and the NCCI Policy Manual govern which
-- pairs it may bypass: https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coding-billing/ncci-medicaid
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :z_threshold (2.5), :min_encounters (30), :min_peer_n (15), :saturation_rate (0.95)

WITH same_day AS (
  -- encounters where an E&M and a procedure were billed for the same beneficiary/provider/day
  SELECT
      em.rendering_npi,
      em.beneficiary_id,
      em.service_date,
      MAX(CASE WHEN em.modifier_1 = '25' OR em.modifier_2 = '25'
                 OR em.modifier_3 = '25' OR em.modifier_4 = '25'
               THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_mod25,
      SUM(em.paid_amount)         AS em_paid
  FROM claim_lines em
  WHERE em.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND em.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND (em.cpt BETWEEN '99202' AND '99215' OR em.cpt BETWEEN '99281' AND '99285')
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM claim_lines px
      WHERE px.beneficiary_id = em.beneficiary_id
        AND px.rendering_npi  = em.rendering_npi
        AND px.service_date   = em.service_date
        AND px.cpt BETWEEN '10021' AND '69990'      -- surgical/procedure range; adapt
        AND px.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    )
  GROUP BY em.rendering_npi, em.beneficiary_id, em.service_date
),
prov AS (
  SELECT
      s.rendering_npi, pr.specialty, pr.peer_region,
      COUNT(*)          AS same_day_encounters,
      AVG(s.has_mod25)  AS mod25_rate,
      SUM(s.em_paid)    AS em_paid_on_same_day
  FROM same_day s
  JOIN provider pr ON pr.npi = s.rendering_npi
  GROUP BY s.rendering_npi, pr.specialty, pr.peer_region
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_encounters
),
peer AS (
  SELECT specialty, peer_region,
         AVG(mod25_rate) AS peer_mean, STDDEV(mod25_rate) AS peer_sd, COUNT(*) AS peer_n
  FROM prov GROUP BY specialty, peer_region HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_peer_n
)
SELECT
    p.rendering_npi, p.specialty, p.peer_region,
    p.same_day_encounters,
    ROUND(p.mod25_rate, 3) AS mod25_rate,
    ROUND(k.peer_mean, 3)  AS peer_mean,
    ROUND((p.mod25_rate - k.peer_mean) / NULLIF(k.peer_sd, 0), 2) AS z_score,
    p.em_paid_on_same_day,
    CASE WHEN p.mod25_rate >= :saturation_rate THEN 'SATURATED' ELSE 'OUTLIER' END AS class
FROM prov p
JOIN peer k USING (specialty, peer_region)
WHERE p.mod25_rate >= :saturation_rate
   OR (p.mod25_rate - k.peer_mean) / NULLIF(k.peer_sd, 0) > :z_threshold
ORDER BY p.mod25_rate DESC;

-- Companion: the same test for modifier 57 (decision for surgery) and for E&M
-- appended to a MINOR procedure only (global period 000/010), where the separately
-- identifiable claim is hardest to sustain.
tests.threshold: :saturation_rate = 0.95 identifies providers appending modifier 25 to essentially every eligible encounter — that cohort needs no statistical argument and should be worked first. :z_threshold = 2.5 handles the rest. Specialty matters enormously here: dermatology, ophthalmology and urgent care legitimately carry high modifier-25 rates because same-day minor procedures are their normal practice, so a cross-specialty comparison will produce a list of specialties rather than a list of providers. The CPT ranges in the query are illustrative — set the procedure range and the global-period filter from your own fee schedule. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-05 (Modifier governance & documentation review — its trigger is 'modifier appended to bypass an edit', which is exactly modifier 25, though the control's name currently reads 59/X{EPSU} only; see gap note G1). Secondary: CB-04 (NCCI PTP edit enforcement pre-submission), CB-10 (Global-surgical-package bundling control).

failure_map.reading: No modifier-use audit exists. CB-05's evidence artifact — the modifier-use audit sample — does not exist.
CB-05 is specified monthly; no sample was drawn or reviewed in the period.
Modifier-25 exceptions were reviewed and cleared without inspecting whether the record documents a significant, separately identifiable service.
The audit scope covers modifier 59 and X{EPSU} only, so modifier 25 — the highest-volume bypass modifier — is never sampled. This is the defining defect for this test.
Sampling occurred but no retained workpaper ties a sampled claim to a documented conclusion.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Modifier-59 / X{EPSU} concentration on PTP-edit code pairs
tests.hypothesis: NCCI procedure-to-procedure edits bundle code pairs that should not normally be billed together; modifier 59 and the X{EPSU} subset are the permitted bypass. Where PTP enforcement is absent, or enforced but never monitored for bypass volume, a provider can restore every bundled pair by reflex. The signature is a high bypass rate on the specific code pairs that carry a PTP edit — not modifier 59 volume generally.
tests.check: Join paid claim lines to your NCCI PTP edit file on the (column-1, column-2) code pair, and for each provider compute the share of edit-eligible pairs that were paid because a 59/X modifier was present. Report the providers, and separately the code pairs, with the highest bypass rates.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 3 - PTP-edit bypass rate via modifier 59 / X{EPSU}
-- Requires the NCCI PTP edit file loaded as a reference table. Medicaid NCCI files
-- (six methodologies, quarterly): https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coding-billing/ncci-medicaid
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_pairs (25), :bypass_rate_cut (0.50)

WITH paid_pairs AS (
  SELECT
      a.rendering_npi,
      a.beneficiary_id,
      a.service_date,
      a.cpt AS col1_code,
      b.cpt AS col2_code,
      CASE WHEN b.modifier_1 IN ('59','XE','XP','XS','XU')
             OR b.modifier_2 IN ('59','XE','XP','XS','XU')
             OR b.modifier_3 IN ('59','XE','XP','XS','XU')
             OR b.modifier_4 IN ('59','XE','XP','XS','XU')
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS bypass_modifier_present,
      b.paid_amount
  FROM claim_lines a
  JOIN claim_lines b
    ON  b.beneficiary_id = a.beneficiary_id
    AND b.rendering_npi  = a.rendering_npi
    AND b.service_date   = a.service_date
    AND b.claim_line_id <> a.claim_line_id
  JOIN ncci_ptp_edit e                       -- your loaded NCCI PTP reference table
    ON  e.column_1_code = a.cpt
    AND e.column_2_code = b.cpt
    AND e.modifier_indicator = '1'           -- '1' = a modifier may bypass this edit
    AND a.service_date BETWEEN e.effective_date
                           AND COALESCE(e.deletion_date, DATE '9999-12-31')
  WHERE a.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND a.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND b.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
),
by_provider AS (
  SELECT
      rendering_npi,
      COUNT(*)                       AS edit_eligible_pairs,
      AVG(bypass_modifier_present)   AS bypass_rate,
      SUM(CASE WHEN bypass_modifier_present = 1 THEN paid_amount ELSE 0 END) AS bypassed_paid
  FROM paid_pairs
  GROUP BY rendering_npi
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_pairs
)
SELECT
    p.rendering_npi, pr.specialty,
    p.edit_eligible_pairs,
    ROUND(p.bypass_rate, 3) AS bypass_rate,
    p.bypassed_paid
FROM by_provider p
JOIN provider pr ON pr.npi = p.rendering_npi
WHERE p.bypass_rate > :bypass_rate_cut
ORDER BY p.bypass_rate DESC, p.bypassed_paid DESC;

-- Second cut, by CODE PAIR rather than provider: which pairs are bypassed most often
-- across the whole population? A pair bypassed at 90% network-wide is usually an edit
-- or policy problem, not a provider problem - and belongs to CB-17, not to an audit.
tests.threshold: :bypass_rate_cut = 0.50 is a deliberately blunt starting cut — half of all edit-eligible pairs restored by modifier is high in most specialties, but there are legitimate exceptions (distinct anatomic sites in dermatology and podiatry, separate encounters in the same day). :min_pairs = 25 keeps the rate stable. Run the by-code-pair cut FIRST: if a pair is bypassed at high rates network-wide, you have found a policy or edit-configuration issue and the provider list derived from it will be noise. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-04 (NCCI PTP edit enforcement pre-submission). Secondary: CB-05 (Modifier-59 / X{EPSU} governance & documentation review), CB-16 (Unbundling detection analytics).

failure_map.reading: PTP edits are not enforced pre-submission. CB-04's PTP edit hit/disposition log does not exist.
The edit engine is configured but the edit file was not refreshed for the period — CB-06 requires quarterly Medicaid NCCI file loads.
PTP hits were overridden at adjudication to clear a claims backlog, with no modifier-documentation review.
Edits fire and the bypass modifier is accepted at face value with no downstream monitoring of bypass volume — the edit runs, the control does not work.
Hits are suppressed silently in the edit engine with no retained disposition log.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: New-patient E&M billed for an established patient
tests.hypothesis: New-patient E&M codes pay materially more than their established-patient equivalents and are defined by a bright-line rule: no face-to-face service from the same physician, or another physician of the same specialty in the same group, within the prior three years. Where the coding audit program does not test this specific rule, it goes unchecked, because no edit fires and no chart looks wrong.
