tests.check: For each new-patient E&M claim line, look back three years for any face-to-face professional service for the same beneficiary from the same provider — or from another provider sharing the same group TIN and specialty — and flag hits.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 4 - New-patient E&M where a prior encounter exists within the lookback
-- CPT defines "new patient" as no face-to-face service from the same physician, or
-- another physician of the same specialty in the same group practice, within 3 years.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end   (the lookback is three calendar years, not a day count)

SELECT
    n.claim_line_id, n.beneficiary_id, n.rendering_npi, n.group_tin,
    n.cpt, n.service_date, n.paid_amount,
    prior.prior_service_date,
    prior.prior_rendering_npi,
    (n.service_date - prior.prior_service_date) AS days_since_prior,
    CASE WHEN prior.prior_rendering_npi = n.rendering_npi
         THEN 'SAME_PROVIDER' ELSE 'SAME_GROUP_AND_SPECIALTY' END AS match_basis
FROM claim_lines n
JOIN provider pn ON pn.npi = n.rendering_npi
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (                      -- Postgres/Snowflake; use OUTER APPLY on SQL Server
    SELECT p.service_date AS prior_service_date,
           p.rendering_npi AS prior_rendering_npi
    FROM claim_lines p
    JOIN provider pp ON pp.npi = p.rendering_npi
    WHERE p.beneficiary_id = n.beneficiary_id
      AND p.service_date < n.service_date
      -- interval syntax is PostgreSQL and DuckDB; elsewhere use DATEADD(year, -3, n.service_date)
      AND p.service_date >= n.service_date - INTERVAL '3 years'   -- calendar years (1096 days across a leap day)
      AND p.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
      AND p.is_face_to_face = TRUE                    -- derive from POS + code range
      AND (p.rendering_npi = n.rendering_npi
           OR (pp.group_tin = pn.group_tin AND pp.specialty = pn.specialty))
    -- ordering by a boolean is PostgreSQL and DuckDB; elsewhere use
    -- ORDER BY CASE WHEN p.rendering_npi = n.rendering_npi THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
    ORDER BY (p.rendering_npi = n.rendering_npi) DESC,   -- same-provider prior first
             p.service_date DESC
    LIMIT 1
) prior
WHERE n.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND n.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND n.cpt IN ('99202','99203','99204','99205')      -- add 99341-99350, 99381-99387 as applicable
ORDER BY n.paid_amount DESC;

-- Roll up by rendering_npi and by group_tin. A single hit is a keying error;
-- a provider with a 30% new-patient-conflict rate is a control finding.
tests.threshold: The three-year rule is definitional, not tunable — but two things around it are. First, `is_face_to_face`: telehealth, lab-only and interpretation-only encounters do not reset new-patient status in the same way, so how you derive that flag determines your false-positive rate more than anything else. Second, group and specialty resolution: if your provider dimension has stale TINs or coarse specialty taxonomy, SAME_GROUP_AND_SPECIALTY matches will be unreliable — work SAME_PROVIDER matches first, they need no dimension quality at all. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-19 (Coding audit program with statistically valid sampling + error-rate tracking). Secondary: CB-03 (E&M level validation), CB-18 (Pre-submission claim scrubber, provider side). See gap note G2 — no control names the new-vs-established rule specifically.

failure_map.reading: No coding audit program covers the new-patient rule, and no scrubber edit tests it.
CB-19 is specified quarterly; no audit cycle covering E&M ran in the period.
The audit identified new-patient errors and no corrective-action or coder-education loop followed (CB-20).
The audit samples E&M level accuracy only and never tests new-vs-established status, so the error class is structurally out of scope.
Audit occurred but the workpaper does not record which attributes were tested.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: E&M billed inside a global surgical period
tests.hypothesis: Major and minor surgical procedures carry a global period during which routine post-operative E&M is bundled into the surgical payment. Where the global-surgical-package control is absent, or checks only the surgeon's own claims, post-operative visits are billed separately — sometimes with modifier 24 asserting they are unrelated, which is exactly the assertion that needs testing.
tests.check: For each paid surgical procedure, look forward across its global period for E&M claims from the same provider or group, and flag those paid without an appropriate modifier — and, separately, those paid WITH modifier 24 or 79, which are the assertions to sample.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 5 - E&M inside the global surgical period
-- Global-period days come from the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule relative value file
-- (000 / 010 / 090 / XXX / YYY / ZZZ). Load it as a reference dimension.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

WITH surgeries AS (
  SELECT
      s.claim_line_id AS surgery_line_id,
      s.beneficiary_id, s.rendering_npi, s.group_tin,
      s.cpt AS surgical_cpt, s.service_date AS surgery_date,
      CAST(f.global_period_days AS INT) AS global_days
  FROM claim_lines s
  JOIN fee_schedule f ON f.hcpcs = s.cpt
                      AND f.effective_year = EXTRACT(YEAR FROM s.service_date)   -- one row per code and year
  WHERE s.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND f.global_period_days IN ('010','090')       -- minor with follow-up, and major
    AND s.service_date BETWEEN :period_start - 90 AND :period_end
)
SELECT
    g.surgery_line_id, g.beneficiary_id, g.rendering_npi, g.surgical_cpt,
    g.surgery_date, g.global_days,
    e.claim_line_id AS em_line_id, e.cpt AS em_cpt, e.service_date AS em_date,
    (e.service_date - g.surgery_date) AS days_into_global,
    e.paid_amount,
    COALESCE(e.modifier_1, '') || COALESCE(e.modifier_2, '')
      || COALESCE(e.modifier_3, '') || COALESCE(e.modifier_4, '') AS em_modifiers,
    CASE
      WHEN e.modifier_1 IN ('24','79') OR e.modifier_2 IN ('24','79')
        OR e.modifier_3 IN ('24','79') OR e.modifier_4 IN ('24','79')
        THEN 'UNRELATED_ASSERTED'      -- sample these: the assertion is the finding
      WHEN e.modifier_1 IN ('58','78')  OR e.modifier_2 IN ('58','78')
        OR e.modifier_3 IN ('58','78') OR e.modifier_4 IN ('58','78')
        THEN 'STAGED_OR_RETURN'        -- usually legitimate; lower priority
      ELSE 'NO_MODIFIER'               -- should not have paid
    END AS global_class
FROM surgeries g
JOIN claim_lines e
  ON  e.beneficiary_id = g.beneficiary_id
  AND (e.rendering_npi = g.rendering_npi OR e.group_tin = g.group_tin)
  AND e.service_date >  g.surgery_date
  AND e.service_date <= g.surgery_date + g.global_days
  AND e.cpt BETWEEN '99202' AND '99215'
  AND e.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
WHERE e.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
ORDER BY global_class, e.paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: NO_MODIFIER hits are categorical — a bundled visit was paid separately, and the edit should have caught it. UNRELATED_ASSERTED (modifier 24 or 79) is the interesting bucket and needs a rate, not a list: compute each provider's share of in-global E&M carrying modifier 24 and benchmark it within specialty, as in TEST 2. Note the query looks back 90 days before :period_start so that surgeries preceding the window still have their global periods evaluated — omitting that truncates the first quarter of results. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-10 (Global-surgical-package bundling control). Secondary: CB-05 (Modifier governance & documentation review), CB-09 (Payment-modifier validation).

failure_map.reading: No global-period conflict report exists — CB-10's named evidence artifact.
CB-10 is specified monthly; no conflict report was produced.
Conflicts were resolved by accepting modifier 24 without documentation review.
The check matches on rendering NPI only, so a partner in the same group billing the post-op visit never conflicts.
Report produced, no retained dispositions.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Units of service above the MUE ceiling
tests.hypothesis: Medically Unlikely Edits cap the units of a code that could plausibly be furnished to one beneficiary on one day. Where MUE enforcement is absent, stale, or applied per line while the billing is split across lines, over-unit claims pay. The line-splitting variant is the one that survives most edit engines.
tests.check: Compare billed units to the MUE value for the code, at BOTH line level and date-of-service aggregate level, respecting the MUE adjudication indicator (MAI) which determines whether the edit is per line or per date of service.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 6 - MUE breach at line level and at date-of-service level
-- MUE values and MAI indicators come from the CMS NCCI MUE files (Practitioner,
-- Facility Outpatient, DME). MAI 1 = per line; MAI 2 = per date of service, absolute;
-- MAI 3 = per date of service, "not otherwise specified".
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :mue_file_type ('PRACTITIONER', 'FACILITY_OP' or 'DME')

WITH line_level AS (
  SELECT
      cl.claim_line_id, cl.claim_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.rendering_npi, cl.billing_npi,
      cl.cpt, cl.service_date, cl.units, cl.paid_amount,
      m.mue_value, m.mai
  FROM claim_lines cl
  JOIN ncci_mue m
    ON  m.hcpcs = cl.cpt
    AND m.mue_file = :mue_file_type          -- 'PRACTITIONER' | 'FACILITY_OP' | 'DME'
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
),
dos_level AS (
  SELECT
      beneficiary_id, rendering_npi, cpt, service_date,
      SUM(units)        AS dos_units,
      MAX(mue_value)    AS mue_value,
      MAX(mai)          AS mai,
      COUNT(*)          AS line_count,
      SUM(paid_amount)  AS paid_amount
  FROM line_level
  GROUP BY beneficiary_id, rendering_npi, cpt, service_date
)
-- 6a: single line above the MUE (MAI 1)
SELECT 'LINE_LEVEL_BREACH' AS breach_type,
       claim_line_id, beneficiary_id, rendering_npi, cpt, service_date,
       units AS billed_units, mue_value, units - mue_value AS excess_units,
       1 AS line_count, paid_amount
FROM line_level
WHERE mai = '1' AND units > mue_value

UNION ALL

-- 6b: units split across lines to stay under a per-line cap (MAI 2/3) - the harder case
SELECT 'DOS_LEVEL_BREACH' AS breach_type,
       CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS claim_line_id,
       beneficiary_id, rendering_npi, cpt, service_date,
       dos_units AS billed_units, mue_value, dos_units - mue_value AS excess_units,
       line_count, paid_amount
FROM dos_level
WHERE mai IN ('2','3') AND dos_units > mue_value
ORDER BY excess_units DESC, paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: Categorical against the published MUE value — but two cautions. MUE values are revised quarterly, so join on the MUE file version effective for the service date, not the current one, or you will manufacture historical breaches. And the DOS_LEVEL_BREACH bucket with a high line_count is the signal worth working: split lines that individually clear a per-line cap and jointly exceed a date-of-service cap are deliberate in a way a single over-unit line usually is not. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-07 (MUE units-of-service edit enforcement). Secondary: CB-08 (Quantity / frequency-limit edits), CB-18 (Pre-submission claim scrubber).

failure_map.reading: MUE edits are not enforced. CB-07's MUE hit / adjudication log does not exist.
The edit exists but the MUE file has not been refreshed through the quarterly cycle.
MUE hits were overridden without documentation of medical necessity for the excess units.
The edit applies per line only and ignores the MAI, so date-of-service caps are never enforced and line-splitting defeats it entirely.
No retained adjudication log of MUE hits and their disposition.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Place-of-service mismatch — non-facility rate paid for a facility service
tests.hypothesis: The place-of-service code drives whether a service pays at the higher non-facility rate (practice bears the overhead) or the lower facility rate. Where the POS control is absent, a provider can bill POS 11 (office) for a service actually furnished in a facility, collecting the overhead component twice. The OIG POS-32 finding referenced by CB-13 is the canonical instance.
tests.check: For each professional claim paid at the non-facility rate, look for a facility claim for the same beneficiary on the same date — an inpatient, outpatient, SNF or ASC claim — which contradicts the asserted place of service.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 7 - Non-facility POS asserted while a facility claim exists for the same encounter
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

SELECT
    p.claim_line_id, p.beneficiary_id, p.rendering_npi, p.billing_npi,
    p.cpt, p.service_date, p.place_of_service AS asserted_pos,
    p.paid_amount AS professional_paid,
    f.claim_type  AS contradicting_facility_claim,
    f.facility_npi,
    f.admit_date, f.discharge_date,
    fs.non_facility_rate - fs.facility_rate AS rate_differential
FROM claim_lines p
JOIN fee_schedule fs ON fs.hcpcs = p.cpt
JOIN facility_claim f
  ON  f.beneficiary_id = p.beneficiary_id
  AND (   (p.service_date >  f.admit_date            -- strictly inside the stay: admission and
           AND p.service_date <  COALESCE(f.discharge_date, DATE '9999-12-31'))  -- discharge days excluded; open stay runs on
       OR (f.claim_type IN ('OUTPATIENT','ASC')       -- same-day outpatient or ASC encounter: the
           AND f.discharge_date = f.admit_date        -- service date is the encounter itself
           AND p.service_date = f.admit_date))
WHERE p.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND p.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND p.place_of_service IN ('11','49','20')          -- office / independent clinic / urgent care
  AND f.claim_type IN ('INPATIENT','OUTPATIENT','SNF','ASC')
  AND fs.non_facility_rate > fs.facility_rate         -- only where the differential exists
ORDER BY rate_differential DESC, p.paid_amount DESC;

-- Companion, no facility-claim join required: providers whose POS-11 share is far above
-- their specialty peers while their patients' facility utilisation is comparable.
tests.threshold: Categorical where a contradicting facility claim exists on the same date — but false positives are real: a patient can legitimately be seen in an office in the morning and admitted in the afternoon. Exclude the admission date and the discharge date, as in the home-health family's institutional-stay test, and rank by rate_differential rather than by paid_amount so you surface the codes where the POS choice actually moved money. Providers with a recurring pattern across many beneficiaries are the finding; single instances are usually clinical reality. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-13 (Place-of-service / facility-vs-non-facility rate edit). Secondary: CB-18 (Pre-submission claim scrubber), CD-18 (Service-modality documentation control).

failure_map.reading: No POS-vs-rate exception report exists — CB-13's named evidence artifact.
CB-13 is specified continuous; no exception report covers the period.
Exceptions were closed on the provider's assertion with no cross-check against the facility claim.
The edit validates that the POS code is syntactically valid rather than that it is consistent with the beneficiary's other claims that day.
No retained exception report or dispositions.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Post-acute-transfer DRG — full DRG paid where a transfer occurred
tests.hypothesis: Under the post-acute-care transfer policy, a qualifying DRG discharged to certain post-acute settings pays a per-diem transfer amount rather than the full DRG. Where the discharge-status control is absent, a discharge-status code of 01 (home) is reported and the full DRG pays, even though a post-acute claim for the same beneficiary starts within days. This is one of the OIG's most repeated hospital findings and CB-14 cites it directly.
tests.check: For inpatient claims in transfer-qualifying DRGs coded with a non-transfer discharge status, look for a post-acute claim — SNF, home health, IRF, LTCH — starting within the transfer window, and report the DRG payment at risk.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 8 - Post-acute-transfer DRG: discharge status contradicted by a post-acute claim
-- Transfer-qualifying DRGs are published annually in the IPPS final rule; load as a
-- reference table with the fiscal year they apply to.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :postacute_window_days (3), :fiscal_year (the IPPS fiscal year of the transfer-DRG list)

SELECT
    i.claim_id             AS inpatient_claim_id,
    i.beneficiary_id, i.facility_npi, i.drg_code,
    i.admit_date, i.discharge_date,
    i.discharge_status_code,
    i.paid_amount          AS drg_paid,
    pa.claim_type          AS postacute_setting,
    pa.service_start_date  AS postacute_start,
    (pa.service_start_date - i.discharge_date) AS days_to_postacute
FROM inpatient_claim i
JOIN transfer_drg t
  ON  t.drg_code    = i.drg_code
  AND t.fiscal_year = :fiscal_year
JOIN post_acute_claim pa
  ON  pa.beneficiary_id      = i.beneficiary_id
  AND pa.service_start_date >= i.discharge_date
  AND pa.service_start_date <= i.discharge_date + :postacute_window_days
WHERE i.discharge_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND i.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND pa.claim_type IN ('SNF','HOME_HEALTH','IRF','LTCH','PSYCH')
  AND (
        -- discharge statuses that assert NO post-acute transfer
        i.discharge_status_code IN ('01','20','21')
        -- status 06 (home under organised home-health care) is a transfer status for the
        -- special-payment DRG subset, and is consistent with a following home-health claim;
        -- flag it only for a non-special DRG followed by a non-home-health post-acute claim
        OR (i.discharge_status_code = '06'
            AND pa.claim_type <> 'HOME_HEALTH'
            -- boolean column and literal; where there is no boolean type store 0/1 and
            -- use COALESCE(t.special_payment_subset, 0) = 0
            AND COALESCE(t.special_payment_subset, FALSE) = FALSE)
      )
ORDER BY i.paid_amount DESC;

-- Note: discharge status 06 (home under care of an organised home-health service) IS a
-- transfer status for the subset of DRGs on the special-payment list (transfer_drg
-- .special_payment_subset), so it is split out above and evaluated against that list.
tests.threshold: :postacute_window_days = 3 matches the conventional transfer window for home health; SNF and IRF transfers are generally evaluated on same-day or next-day admission. Set the window per post-acute setting rather than globally. The discharge-status list matters more than the window: status 06 behaves differently for the special-payment DRG subset and will dominate false positives if handled as a single bucket. Confirm the transfer-qualifying DRG list against the IPPS final rule for the correct fiscal year — it changes annually. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-14 (DRG & discharge-status coding accuracy review — transfer vs discharge). Secondary: CB-19 (Coding audit program), CD-17 (Coordination-of-benefits / setting documentation control).

failure_map.reading: No discharge-status audit exists. CB-14's discharge-status audit sample does not exist.
CB-14 is specified monthly; no sample was drawn in the period.
Discrepancies were identified and no claim adjustment or overpayment return followed (PI-07).
The audit reviews the coded discharge status against the medical record only, and never against the downstream post-acute claim — which is the only evidence that reliably contradicts it.
Audit sample not retained in a form that shows which claims were tested.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Same-sample UDT code stacking — presumptive plus definitive drug testing
tests.hypothesis: Urine drug testing is billed as a presumptive screen (CPT 80305–80307) and, where clinically indicated, a definitive confirmation (HCPCS G0480–G0483). Where unbundling analytics are absent, both are billed on the same sample as a matter of routine, and the definitive test is billed at the top tier regardless of how many drug classes were actually confirmed. CB-16 names this pattern explicitly.
tests.check: Find same-beneficiary, same-date pairs of a presumptive UDT code with a definitive UDT code, compute each billing provider's stacking rate (stacked samples over all UDT samples), and list the pairs only for billers with at least :min_tests samples and a stacking rate above :stack_rate_cut. Separately compute each provider's share of definitive tests billed at the highest tier (G0483, 22+ drug classes).
tests.sql:
-- TEST 9 - Same-sample presumptive + definitive UDT, and top-tier definitive concentration
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_tests (25), :stack_rate_cut (0.50), :top_tier_share_cut (0.80; read only by the commented 9b)

WITH udt AS (
  SELECT
      cl.beneficiary_id, cl.rendering_npi, cl.billing_npi, cl.service_date,
      cl.cpt, cl.paid_amount,
      CASE WHEN cl.cpt IN ('80305','80306','80307')             THEN 'PRESUMPTIVE'
           WHEN cl.cpt IN ('G0480','G0481','G0482','G0483')     THEN 'DEFINITIVE'
      END AS udt_class,
      CASE WHEN cl.cpt = 'G0483' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END AS is_top_tier
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND cl.cpt IN ('80305','80306','80307','G0480','G0481','G0482','G0483')
)
-- 9a: presumptive + definitive on the same sample/date, reported only for billers whose
-- stacking RATE is the signal (a single stack among many samples is not an assertion that
-- every screen was ambiguous)
, sample AS (                                   -- one row per biller, beneficiary and date
  SELECT billing_npi, beneficiary_id, service_date,
         MAX(CASE WHEN udt_class = 'PRESUMPTIVE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_presumptive,
         MAX(CASE WHEN udt_class = 'DEFINITIVE'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_definitive
  FROM udt
  GROUP BY billing_npi, beneficiary_id, service_date
),
biller_rate AS (
  SELECT billing_npi,
         COUNT(*) AS samples,
         SUM(has_presumptive * has_definitive) AS stacked_samples,
         SUM(has_presumptive * has_definitive) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS stack_rate
  FROM sample
  GROUP BY billing_npi
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_tests
     AND SUM(has_presumptive * has_definitive) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) > :stack_rate_cut
)
SELECT
    'SAME_SAMPLE_STACK' AS finding,
    p.beneficiary_id, p.rendering_npi, p.billing_npi, p.service_date,
    p.cpt AS presumptive_cpt, d.cpt AS definitive_cpt,
    p.paid_amount + d.paid_amount AS combined_paid,
    r.samples, r.stacked_samples, r.stack_rate
FROM udt p
JOIN udt d
  ON  d.beneficiary_id = p.beneficiary_id
  AND d.service_date   = p.service_date
  AND d.billing_npi    = p.billing_npi
JOIN biller_rate r ON r.billing_npi = p.billing_npi
WHERE p.udt_class = 'PRESUMPTIVE'
  AND d.udt_class = 'DEFINITIVE'
ORDER BY r.stack_rate DESC, combined_paid DESC;

-- 9b: providers whose definitive testing is almost entirely top-tier
--   SELECT rendering_npi, COUNT(*) AS definitive_tests, AVG(is_top_tier) AS top_tier_share,
--          SUM(paid_amount) AS paid
--   FROM udt WHERE udt_class = 'DEFINITIVE'
--   GROUP BY rendering_npi
--   HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_tests AND AVG(is_top_tier) > :top_tier_share_cut
--   ORDER BY top_tier_share DESC;
tests.threshold: The same-sample stack (9a) is a pattern, not an error — it is payable when the presumptive result genuinely drove the confirmation, so treat volume and RATE, not instances, as the signal: a provider stacking on 95% of samples is asserting that essentially every screen was ambiguous. :stack_rate_cut = 0.50 is the starting cut: pairs are listed only for billers who stack on more than half of their samples, so a biller with an occasional stack does not appear at all; lower it to widen the list. :top_tier_share_cut = 0.80 for 9b reflects that G0483 (22+ drug classes) should be the exception, not the default. :min_tests = 25 is the volume floor for both the stacking rate and the 9b share. Note that certain treatment populations legitimately justify broad panels — exclude opioid treatment programs before drawing conclusions. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-16 (Unbundling detection analytics, including the same-sample presumptive + definitive UDT code-pair edit). Secondary: CB-04 (NCCI PTP edit enforcement), CD-16 (Enhanced documentation review for high-cost / high-risk tests).

failure_map.reading: No unbundling analytics exist. CB-16's unbundling pattern alert does not exist.
CB-16 is specified monthly; no alert was produced for the period.
Alerts fired and no prepayment edit (CB-17) or provider education (PI-12) followed.
The analytic detects fragmented surgical billing generically but carries no UDT-specific code-pair rule, which is the pattern CB-16 was written to catch.
Alerts exist without retained dispositions.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Duplicate professional services across NPIs within one group
tests.hypothesis: Duplicate detection that keys on (beneficiary, date, code, rendering NPI) will not catch the same service billed twice by two providers in the same group, or by the group and by an individual. The duplicate is real; the key is wrong. This is the coding-family analogue of the cross-agency duplicate in the home-health pack, and OIG A-06-21-05003 (cited by CB-15) is the reference finding.
tests.check: Group paid professional lines by beneficiary + date + code and flag groups containing more than one line from different rendering NPIs sharing a group TIN, excluding codes where multiple same-day services are expected.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 10 - Same service, same day, same group, different rendering NPI
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

WITH candidate AS (
  SELECT
      cl.beneficiary_id, cl.service_date, cl.cpt, pr.group_tin,
      COUNT(*)                          AS line_count,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cl.rendering_npi)  AS distinct_renderers,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cl.billing_npi)    AS distinct_billers,
      SUM(cl.paid_amount)               AS combined_paid,
      MIN(cl.claim_line_id)             AS first_line,
      MAX(cl.claim_line_id)             AS last_line
  FROM claim_lines cl
  JOIN provider pr ON pr.npi = cl.rendering_npi
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND cl.claim_type = 'PROFESSIONAL'
    -- exclude codes where repeat same-day services are expected
    AND cl.cpt NOT IN (SELECT hcpcs FROM repeat_service_exception_list)
    -- exclude lines already carrying a repeat modifier, which asserts the duplication
    -- (all four modifier slots are read)
    AND COALESCE(cl.modifier_1,'') NOT IN ('76','77','91')
    AND COALESCE(cl.modifier_2,'') NOT IN ('76','77','91')
    AND COALESCE(cl.modifier_3,'') NOT IN ('76','77','91')
    AND COALESCE(cl.modifier_4,'') NOT IN ('76','77','91')
  GROUP BY cl.beneficiary_id, cl.service_date, cl.cpt, pr.group_tin
)
SELECT *,
       CASE WHEN distinct_billers > 1 THEN 'CROSS_ENTITY' ELSE 'INTRA_GROUP' END AS duplicate_class
FROM candidate
WHERE distinct_renderers > 1
ORDER BY combined_paid DESC;
tests.threshold: Categorical once the exception list is right — and the exception list is the whole test. Build `repeat_service_exception_list` before running: repeat labs, serial radiographs, anaesthesia, critical-care add-ons and therapy units all legitimately repeat within a day. Without it this query returns a large fraction of your professional claims and is useless. Modifiers 76, 77 and 91 explicitly assert a repeat service and are excluded above; if your population uses them heavily, sample those separately rather than excluding them silently. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-15 (Duplicate claim / line detection). Secondary: CB-09 (Payment-modifier validation), CD-17 (Coordination-of-benefits / setting documentation control).

failure_map.reading: Duplicate detection covers exact claim resubmission only.
CB-15's duplicate-hit disposition log is empty for the period.
Duplicate hits were overridden at adjudication to clear a backlog.
The duplicate key includes rendering_npi, so intra-group duplicates can never match. This is the defining defect for this test.
Hits suppressed silently in the edit engine with no retained log.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Retired, deleted or not-yet-effective code paid
tests.hypothesis: Code sets change annually (HCPCS/CPT effective 1 January; ICD-10 effective 1 October, with the 2027 set released 1 August 2026). Where code-set update governance is absent or the chargemaster is refreshed late, claims pay against codes retired before the service date or not yet effective on it. This is rarely fraud and almost always a control finding — which makes it a clean, low-abrasion first test to run.
tests.check: Join each paid line's code to the code-set reference table and flag any service date outside the code's effective/termination window. Roll up by billing entity and by code to distinguish a systemic chargemaster problem from a single provider.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 11 - Service dates outside the code's effective window
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

-- The code set is versioned by date: a code can have several rows (retired, then re-effective).
-- A line is clean when ANY version is in force on its service date; only a line with no version
-- in force is a defect, and it is classified against the code's whole history.
WITH code_range AS (
  SELECT code,
         MIN(effective_date) AS first_effective_date,
         MAX(COALESCE(termination_date, DATE '9999-12-31')) AS last_termination_date
  FROM code_set_reference
  GROUP BY code
)
SELECT
    cl.claim_line_id, cl.billing_npi, cl.rendering_npi, cl.beneficiary_id,
    cl.cpt AS billed_code, cl.service_date, cl.paid_amount,
    cr.first_effective_date, cr.last_termination_date,
    CASE
      WHEN cr.code IS NULL                                THEN 'CODE_NOT_IN_CODE_SET'
      WHEN cl.service_date < cr.first_effective_date      THEN 'NOT_YET_EFFECTIVE'
      ELSE 'RETIRED_CODE'
    END AS code_defect
FROM claim_lines cl
LEFT JOIN code_range cr ON cr.code = cl.cpt
WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND NOT EXISTS (                                  -- no version in force on the service date
    SELECT 1 FROM code_set_reference cs
    WHERE cs.code = cl.cpt
      AND cl.service_date BETWEEN cs.effective_date
                              AND COALESCE(cs.termination_date, DATE '9999-12-31')
  )
ORDER BY code_defect, cl.paid_amount DESC;

-- Roll up: SELECT billing_npi, billed_code, code_defect, COUNT(*), SUM(paid_amount)
-- A single billing entity concentrated on one retired code is a chargemaster problem
-- (CB-02). Many entities on the same code is an EDIT problem (CB-17).
tests.threshold: Categorical, with one important caveat: your code-set reference table must be versioned by date, not a current-state snapshot. A current-state table will report every claim for a code retired last year as a defect, including the claims that were correct when submitted. Verify that first — the count will be obviously implausible if you have not. The roll-up direction (one entity vs many) is what tells you which control to fix, and that distinction is the point of the test. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-02 (Annual code-set update governance — HCPCS/CPT/ICD-10). Secondary: CB-18 (Pre-submission claim scrubber), CB-17 (Prepayment edit maintenance & tuning).

failure_map.reading: No code-set update governance. CB-02's code-set update change log does not exist.
CB-02 is annual; the change log shows no entry for the most recent release.
The update was performed but exceptions were granted to keep legacy codes active in the chargemaster.
The encoder was updated and the chargemaster was not, or vice versa — so one path still emits retired codes.
The update happened but no dated change log records what changed and when.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Policy-required diagnosis absent from the claim
tests.hypothesis: Some services are payable only with a specific diagnosis — the OIG opioid treatment program finding cited by CB-12 is the reference case, where OTP bundles paid without an opioid-use-disorder diagnosis. Where the required-diagnosis edit is absent or not specified for a service class, these pay silently.
tests.check: For each service class carrying a policy-mandated diagnosis requirement, check whether any diagnosis on the claim (or on a related claim in the lookback) satisfies it, and flag those that do not.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 12 - Services paid without their policy-required diagnosis
-- Drive from a reference table of (service class -> acceptable ICD-10 set), maintained
-- alongside CB-12's required-dx edit specification.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :dx_lookback_days (365)

SELECT
    cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.billing_npi, cl.rendering_npi,
    cl.cpt, cl.service_date, cl.paid_amount,
    r.service_class, r.requirement_source,
    cd.claim_diagnoses
FROM claim_lines cl
JOIN required_dx_rule r
  ON  r.hcpcs = cl.cpt
  AND cl.service_date BETWEEN r.effective_date
                          AND COALESCE(r.termination_date, DATE '9999-12-31')
LEFT JOIN claim_diagnosis cd ON cd.claim_id = cl.claim_id
WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    -- required dx on THIS claim
    SELECT 1 FROM claim_diagnosis d
    JOIN required_dx_code rc ON rc.rule_id = r.rule_id AND rc.icd10_code = d.icd10_code
    WHERE d.claim_id = cl.claim_id
  )
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    -- or on any claim for this beneficiary in the lookback (a softer, fairer test)
    SELECT 1
    FROM claim_diagnosis d2
    JOIN claim_lines c2       ON c2.claim_id = d2.claim_id
    JOIN required_dx_code rc2 ON rc2.rule_id = r.rule_id AND rc2.icd10_code = d2.icd10_code
    WHERE c2.beneficiary_id = cl.beneficiary_id
      AND c2.service_date BETWEEN cl.service_date - :dx_lookback_days AND cl.service_date
  )
ORDER BY cl.paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: The requirement itself is categorical; the lookback is the judgement call. :dx_lookback_days = 365 is a fair starting window — requiring the diagnosis on the same claim is technically correct but produces findings that are really claim-completion errors rather than coverage failures. Run both: same-claim-only gives you the edit-configuration finding, lookback-inclusive gives you the coverage finding. They point at different controls (CB-12 vs CB-11) and should not be merged. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-12 (Required-diagnosis-code edit for policy-mandated diagnoses, e.g. OTP OUD). Secondary: CB-11 (Diagnosis-to-service medical-necessity linkage edit), PI-04 (Prepayment medical-review edits on high-risk codes/services).

failure_map.reading: No required-dx edit exists for the service class. CB-12's required-dx edit specification does not exist.
The specification exists but the edit is not deployed in the adjudication path.
The edit fires and is routinely overridden at adjudication.
The edit checks the primary diagnosis position only, so a valid diagnosis in a secondary position fails and an invalid claim with the code in position one passes.
No retained record of edit hits and their disposition.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Diagnosis-to-service medical-necessity linkage failure (NCD/LCD)
tests.hypothesis: National and local coverage determinations define which diagnoses support which services. Where the necessity-linkage edit is absent, or built once and never refreshed as coverage policy changes, services pay without a supporting diagnosis — the largest single category of insufficient-documentation improper payment.
tests.check: For services governed by an NCD or LCD with a covered-diagnosis list, check whether any diagnosis on the claim appears on that list for the applicable jurisdiction and effective period.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 13 - Services paid without an NCD/LCD-supported diagnosis
-- Coverage rules are jurisdiction-specific and dated. Load the Medicare Coverage
-- Database (or your own policy set) as a versioned reference; CB-11 and CD-02 own it.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

SELECT
    cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.billing_npi, cl.rendering_npi,
    cl.cpt, cl.service_date, cl.paid_amount,
    pol.policy_id, pol.policy_type, pol.jurisdiction, pol.title
FROM claim_lines cl
JOIN coverage_policy pol
  ON  pol.hcpcs        = cl.cpt
  AND pol.jurisdiction = cl.mac_jurisdiction
  AND cl.service_date BETWEEN pol.effective_date
                          AND COALESCE(pol.retirement_date, DATE '9999-12-31')
WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND pol.has_covered_dx_list = TRUE
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM claim_diagnosis d
    JOIN coverage_policy_dx pdx
      ON pdx.policy_id = pol.policy_id AND pdx.icd10_code = d.icd10_code
    WHERE d.claim_id = cl.claim_id
  )
ORDER BY cl.paid_amount DESC;

-- Roll up by policy_id: a policy generating a very high failure rate across many
-- providers usually means the covered-dx list is loaded incorrectly or is out of date
-- - a CD-02 coverage-policy-monitoring finding, not a provider finding. Check that
-- before you open a single provider review.
tests.threshold: Categorical against the policy — but this test has the highest false-positive risk in the family, because it depends entirely on the currency and completeness of your loaded coverage policies. Run the by-policy roll-up first and set aside any policy with an implausibly high failure rate; those are data problems. Restrict the first run to a handful of high-dollar, well-understood policies rather than the whole coverage database. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-11 (Diagnosis-to-service medical-necessity linkage edit — NCD/LCD). Secondary: CD-01 (Coverage-criteria application), CD-02 (Coverage-policy change monitoring).

failure_map.reading: No necessity-linkage edit exists. CB-11's necessity-edit disposition does not exist.
The edit is configured but not active in the adjudication path for the period.
Edit hits were overridden without a documented coverage rationale.
The covered-diagnosis lists were loaded once and never refreshed against the Medicare Coverage Database, so the edit enforces retired policy — CD-02 is the upstream control.
No retained edit-disposition record.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Assistant-at-surgery and co-surgery modifiers on ineligible procedures
tests.hypothesis: The physician fee schedule carries indicators governing whether an assistant surgeon, co-surgeon or team surgeon is payable for each procedure. Where payment-modifier validation is absent, modifiers 80/81/82/AS and 62/66 are appended to procedures where the indicator forbids payment. OIG A-01-20-00503 (22 Nov 2022), cited by CB-09, is the reference finding.
tests.check: Join each line carrying an assistant, co-surgery or team-surgery modifier to the fee-schedule indicator for that procedure and flag those where the indicator is restrictive. Report separately the bilateral modifier 50 applied to procedures whose bilateral indicator forbids it.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 14 - Surgical payment modifiers against fee-schedule indicators
-- Indicators: asst_surg 0/1/2/9, co_surg 0/1/2, team_surg 0/1/2, bilat_surg 0/1/2/3.
-- Restrictive values (0, and 9 for assistant) mean the modifier should not pay.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

WITH surgical AS (
  SELECT
      cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.rendering_npi, cl.billing_npi,
      cl.cpt, cl.service_date, cl.paid_amount,
      cl.modifier_1, cl.modifier_2, cl.modifier_3, cl.modifier_4,
      f.asst_surg_indicator, f.co_surg_indicator,
      f.team_surg_indicator, f.bilat_surg_indicator,
      -- one flag per modifier family, read from all four modifier slots
      CASE WHEN COALESCE(cl.modifier_1,'') IN ('80','81','82','AS') OR COALESCE(cl.modifier_2,'') IN ('80','81','82','AS')
             OR COALESCE(cl.modifier_3,'') IN ('80','81','82','AS') OR COALESCE(cl.modifier_4,'') IN ('80','81','82','AS')
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_assistant,
      CASE WHEN '62' IN (COALESCE(cl.modifier_1,''), COALESCE(cl.modifier_2,''), COALESCE(cl.modifier_3,''), COALESCE(cl.modifier_4,''))
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_co_surgery,
      CASE WHEN '66' IN (COALESCE(cl.modifier_1,''), COALESCE(cl.modifier_2,''), COALESCE(cl.modifier_3,''), COALESCE(cl.modifier_4,''))
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_team_surgery,
      CASE WHEN '50' IN (COALESCE(cl.modifier_1,''), COALESCE(cl.modifier_2,''), COALESCE(cl.modifier_3,''), COALESCE(cl.modifier_4,''))
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_bilateral
  FROM claim_lines cl
  JOIN fee_schedule f
    ON  f.hcpcs = cl.cpt
    AND f.effective_year = EXTRACT(YEAR FROM cl.service_date)
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
),
classified AS (
  SELECT s.*,
         CASE
           WHEN s.has_assistant    = 1 AND s.asst_surg_indicator IN ('0','9')      THEN 'ASSISTANT_NOT_PAYABLE'
           WHEN s.has_co_surgery   = 1 AND s.co_surg_indicator = '0'               THEN 'CO_SURGERY_NOT_PAYABLE'
           WHEN s.has_team_surgery = 1 AND s.team_surg_indicator = '0'             THEN 'TEAM_SURGERY_NOT_PAYABLE'
           WHEN s.has_bilateral    = 1 AND s.bilat_surg_indicator IN ('0','2','3') THEN 'BILATERAL_NOT_APPLICABLE'
         END AS modifier_defect
  FROM surgical s
  WHERE s.has_assistant = 1 OR s.has_co_surgery = 1 OR s.has_team_surgery = 1 OR s.has_bilateral = 1
)
SELECT
    claim_line_id, beneficiary_id, rendering_npi, billing_npi,
    cpt, service_date, paid_amount,
    modifier_1, modifier_2, modifier_3, modifier_4,
    asst_surg_indicator, co_surg_indicator, team_surg_indicator, bilat_surg_indicator,
    modifier_defect
FROM classified
WHERE modifier_defect IS NOT NULL          -- defect list only: lines whose modifier is payable are not returned
ORDER BY modifier_defect, paid_amount DESC;

-- Note assistant indicator '2' means an assistant MAY be paid; '1' means documentation
-- must support it. Only 0 and 9 are flatly restrictive. Indicator '1' lines are a
-- SAMPLING population for CB-09's modifier-vs-documentation review, not a defect list,
-- and are not returned above; select them from `classified` with modifier_defect IS NULL
-- and the indicator = '1' when drawing that sample.
tests.threshold: Categorical against the indicator — but only for indicators 0 and 9. Indicator 1 (payable with supporting documentation) is a sampling population, not a finding, and conflating the two is the most common error in this test. Join the fee schedule on the year effective for the service date; indicators change annually. Bilateral indicator 3 has different payment mechanics again — verify how your adjudication handles it before treating it as a defect. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-09 (Payment-modifier validation — co-surgery 62, assistant 80/AS, bilateral 50). Secondary: CB-04 (NCCI PTP edit enforcement), CB-19 (Coding audit program).

failure_map.reading: No payment-modifier validation exists. CB-09's modifier-vs-documentation review does not exist.
CB-09 is per-claim plus sample; no sample was reviewed in the period.
Restrictive-indicator hits were paid on override with no documentation review.
The edit validates that the modifier is a valid code rather than that it is payable for the specific procedure.
No retained modifier-vs-documentation review workpaper.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Telehealth modality — modifier, place of service and record disagree
tests.hypothesis: Telehealth and audio-only services are identified by place-of-service codes (02, 10) and modifiers (95, 93, GT, FQ). Where the service-modality documentation control is absent, these markers contradict each other — an in-person POS with a telehealth modifier, or a telehealth POS on a service that cannot be furnished remotely. The OIG psychotherapy-telehealth finding cited by CD-18 is the reference case.
tests.check: Cross-tabulate place of service against modality modifier for every service in the period and flag the contradictory combinations, plus telehealth-flagged claims for codes absent from the applicable telehealth services list.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 15 - Modality marker contradictions
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

WITH tele AS (
  SELECT
      cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.rendering_npi, cl.billing_npi,
      cl.cpt, cl.service_date, cl.place_of_service, cl.paid_amount,
      COALESCE(cl.modifier_1,'') AS mod1, COALESCE(cl.modifier_2,'') AS mod2,
      COALESCE(cl.modifier_3,'') AS mod3, COALESCE(cl.modifier_4,'') AS mod4,
      tl.hcpcs IS NOT NULL AS on_telehealth_list,
      -- COALESCE keeps a missing modifier from turning the test into NULL; all four slots read
      (COALESCE(cl.modifier_1,'') IN ('95','93','GT','FQ')
       OR COALESCE(cl.modifier_2,'') IN ('95','93','GT','FQ')
       OR COALESCE(cl.modifier_3,'') IN ('95','93','GT','FQ')
       OR COALESCE(cl.modifier_4,'') IN ('95','93','GT','FQ')) AS has_tele_modifier
  FROM claim_lines cl
  LEFT JOIN telehealth_service_list tl
         ON  tl.hcpcs = cl.cpt
         AND cl.service_date BETWEEN tl.effective_date
                                 AND COALESCE(tl.termination_date, DATE '9999-12-31')
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
),
classified AS (
  SELECT t.*,
    CASE
      WHEN t.place_of_service IN ('02','10') AND NOT t.has_tele_modifier
        THEN 'TELEHEALTH_POS_NO_MODIFIER'
      WHEN t.place_of_service NOT IN ('02','10') AND t.has_tele_modifier
        THEN 'MODIFIER_WITHOUT_TELEHEALTH_POS'
      WHEN t.place_of_service IN ('02','10') AND NOT t.on_telehealth_list
        THEN 'CODE_NOT_ON_TELEHEALTH_LIST'
    END AS modality_defect
  FROM tele t
)
SELECT
    claim_line_id, beneficiary_id, rendering_npi, billing_npi,
    cpt, service_date, place_of_service, paid_amount,
    mod1, mod2, mod3, mod4,
    on_telehealth_list, modality_defect
FROM classified
WHERE modality_defect IS NOT NULL                   -- only contradictions, not every telehealth claim
ORDER BY modality_defect, paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: Categorical, but heavily dependent on the effective-dated telehealth services list — which has changed repeatedly since 2020 and continues to. Load it versioned by date or CODE_NOT_ON_TELEHEALTH_LIST will be dominated by policy-vintage errors rather than billing errors. Modifier positions matter: if your warehouse holds four modifier columns, extend the checks past modifier_2 or you will miss any claim where the modality modifier landed in position three. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CD-18 (Service-modality documentation control — note and claim modifier support the billed modality). Secondary: CB-13 (Place-of-service rate edit), CB-17 (Prepayment edit maintenance & tuning).

failure_map.reading: No modality documentation control exists. CD-18's modality-supporting note + modifier artifact does not exist.
CD-18 is per-service; a population of paid telehealth services has no corresponding modality documentation.
Contradictions were corrected on the claim without reviewing whether the record supports the modality actually furnished.
The control checks that a modality modifier is present rather than that it agrees with the place of service and the record.
No retained evidence that modality was verified against the note.

tests.family_title: Coding & billing integrity — E&M level distribution and modifier overuse
tests.name: Edit-coverage blind spot — high-risk codes with zero prepayment edit activity
tests.hypothesis: This test inverts the others. Rather than looking for bad claims, it looks for controls that are not working by looking for edits that never fire. Where prepayment edit maintenance is absent, a code named in an OIG or GAO finding continues to pay at volume with no edit hit, no denial and no review — the control's silence is the signal.
tests.check: For each code on your high-risk register (OIG/GAO findings, CERT/PERM error causes, internal vulnerability list), compute paid volume, edit-hit count and denial rate in the period, and flag codes with material spend and effectively zero control activity.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 16 - High-risk codes with material spend and no prepayment edit activity
-- Drive from your own high-risk register: the codes named in open OIG/GAO
-- recommendations, CERT/PERM error causes, and internal vulnerability findings.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_paid (50000), :max_edit_hit_rate (0.001)

WITH paid AS (                              -- aggregate each side by code BEFORE joining,
  SELECT cl.cpt AS hcpcs,                   -- so neither side multiplies the other
         COUNT(cl.claim_line_id)       AS paid_lines,
         SUM(cl.paid_amount)           AS paid_amount,
         COUNT(DISTINCT cl.billing_npi) AS billing_entities
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  GROUP BY cl.cpt
),
hits AS (
  SELECT eh.hcpcs, SUM(eh.hit_count) AS edit_hits
  FROM edit_hit_log eh
  WHERE eh.hit_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  GROUP BY eh.hcpcs
),
activity AS (
  SELECT
      hr.hcpcs,
      hr.risk_source,                       -- e.g. 'OIG A-09-22-03010', 'CERT FY2025'
      hr.date_identified,
      COALESCE(p.paid_lines, 0)                                        AS paid_lines,
      COALESCE(p.paid_amount, 0)                                       AS paid_amount,
      COALESCE(p.billing_entities, 0)                                  AS billing_entities,
      COALESCE(h.edit_hits, 0)                                         AS edit_hits,
      COALESCE(h.edit_hits, 0) * 1.0 / NULLIF(p.paid_lines, 0)         AS edit_hit_rate   -- 1.0 avoids integer division
  FROM high_risk_code_register hr
  LEFT JOIN paid p ON p.hcpcs = hr.hcpcs
  LEFT JOIN hits h ON h.hcpcs = hr.hcpcs
)
SELECT
    hcpcs, risk_source, date_identified,
    paid_lines, paid_amount, billing_entities,
    edit_hits, ROUND(edit_hit_rate, 5) AS edit_hit_rate,
    CURRENT_DATE - date_identified AS days_since_risk_identified
FROM activity
WHERE paid_amount >= :min_paid
  AND edit_hit_rate <= :max_edit_hit_rate
ORDER BY paid_amount DESC;

-- This query's output is a CONTROL finding by construction, not a claim finding.
-- Do not open provider reviews from it; take it to the edit-change board (CB-17).
tests.threshold: :min_paid = 50,000 and :max_edit_hit_rate = 0.001 are arbitrary starting values and should be set from your own spend distribution — the useful framing is 'material spend with no control activity', and materiality is yours to define. The `days_since_risk_identified` column is the one that matters in a governance conversation: a code named in an open OIG recommendation two years ago, still paying at volume, with zero edit hits, is a complete and self-evident finding. This test requires an edit-hit log; if you do not have one, that absence is itself the CB-17 finding. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-17 (Prepayment edit maintenance & tuning from emerging vulnerabilities). Secondary: PI-04 (Prepayment medical-review edits on high-risk codes/services), CB-21 (High-risk-code monitoring dashboard to compliance/governance).

failure_map.reading: No edit-change board and no high-risk register. CB-17's edit-change board record does not exist.
CB-17 is quarterly; no edit-change board met or recorded a decision in the period.
The board reviewed the vulnerability and deferred the edit indefinitely without a documented risk acceptance.
Edits were added but configured so narrowly that they never fire — measurable precisely by this query's zero-hit result.
Edits were changed but no board record ties the change to the vulnerability that prompted it.

tests.family_title: High-cost CPT concentration — spinal fusion, cardiac EP, and high-cost diagnostics
tests.name: Single-code revenue concentration — one CPT carrying an outsized share of a provider's paid dollars
tests.hypothesis: Where high-risk-code monitoring is absent or reports volume rather than concentration, a provider whose practice has narrowed onto a single high-reimbursement code is invisible to leadership. The signature is not high volume — a busy spine surgeon has high volume — but a high *share* of one provider's total paid dollars flowing through one or two codes, against peers with a broader distribution.
tests.check: For each rendering provider, compute paid dollars by CPT as a share of that provider's total paid dollars, restrict to codes on the high-cost register, and benchmark the concentration share within specialty. Report the Herfindahl-style concentration index alongside the top-code share so a two-code practice is not mistaken for a diversified one.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 1 - Single-code revenue concentration vs specialty peers
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_paid (100000), :min_peer_n (15), :z_threshold (2.5)
-- Portability: JOIN ... USING (...) is not accepted by SQL Server; write the ON equalities out there.

WITH provider_code AS (
  SELECT
      cl.rendering_npi, pr.specialty, pr.peer_region,
      cl.cpt,
      SUM(cl.paid_amount) AS code_paid,
      COUNT(*)            AS code_lines
  FROM claim_lines cl
  JOIN provider pr ON pr.npi = cl.rendering_npi
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  GROUP BY cl.rendering_npi, pr.specialty, pr.peer_region, cl.cpt
),
code_share AS (
  -- share computed one step earlier: a window function cannot sit inside an aggregate
  SELECT pc.*,
         pc.code_paid / NULLIF(SUM(pc.code_paid) OVER (PARTITION BY pc.rendering_npi), 0)
           AS code_share
  FROM provider_code pc
),
provider_total AS (
  SELECT rendering_npi, specialty, peer_region,
         SUM(code_paid) AS total_paid,
         -- Herfindahl index of the provider's own code mix: 1.0 = a single-code practice
         SUM(POWER(code_share, 2)) AS code_concentration_index
  FROM code_share
  GROUP BY rendering_npi, specialty, peer_region
  HAVING SUM(code_paid) >= :min_paid
),
top_code AS (
  SELECT rendering_npi, cpt AS top_cpt, code_paid, code_lines,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rendering_npi ORDER BY code_paid DESC) AS rk
  FROM provider_code
),
shares AS (
  SELECT
      t.rendering_npi, pt.specialty, pt.peer_region,
      tc.top_cpt, tc.code_lines AS top_code_cases,
      tc.code_paid / NULLIF(pt.total_paid, 0) AS top_code_share,
      pt.total_paid, pt.code_concentration_index,
      hc.hcpcs IS NOT NULL AS top_code_is_high_cost
  FROM provider_total pt
  JOIN top_code tc  ON tc.rendering_npi = pt.rendering_npi AND tc.rk = 1
  JOIN provider_total t ON t.rendering_npi = pt.rendering_npi
  LEFT JOIN high_cost_code_register hc ON hc.hcpcs = tc.top_cpt
),
peer AS (
  SELECT specialty, peer_region,
         AVG(top_code_share) AS peer_mean, STDDEV(top_code_share) AS peer_sd, COUNT(*) AS peer_n
  FROM shares GROUP BY specialty, peer_region HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_peer_n
)
SELECT
    s.rendering_npi, s.specialty, s.peer_region,
    s.top_cpt, s.top_code_cases,
    ROUND(s.top_code_share, 3)           AS top_code_share,
    ROUND(k.peer_mean, 3)                AS peer_mean_share,
    ROUND((s.top_code_share - k.peer_mean) / NULLIF(k.peer_sd, 0), 2) AS z_score,
    ROUND(s.code_concentration_index, 3) AS concentration_index,
    s.total_paid, s.top_code_is_high_cost
FROM shares s
JOIN peer k USING (specialty, peer_region)
WHERE s.top_code_is_high_cost
  AND (s.top_code_share - k.peer_mean) / NULLIF(k.peer_sd, 0) > :z_threshold
ORDER BY z_score DESC, s.total_paid DESC;
tests.threshold: :z_threshold = 2.5 within a same-specialty, same-region peer group, with :min_paid = 100,000 and :min_peer_n = 15. Read the concentration_index alongside the z-score: a sub-specialist who does one thing well will show a high top-code share and a legitimately high concentration index, and that is a description of their practice, not a finding. What makes a hit interesting is concentration *plus* something else — a recent shift in concentration (test 2), an unusual level count (test 3), or a coverage-criteria gap (tests 4–6). Treat this test as a population filter that feeds the others, not as a standalone output. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.

CB-21 is specified monthly; no monitoring pack was produced for the period.
The pack reached governance and no review, edit change or education followed any flagged concentration.

tests.family_title: High-cost CPT concentration — spinal fusion, cardiac EP, and high-cost diagnostics
tests.name: Volume ramp — step change in a high-cost code after a policy or coverage change
tests.hypothesis: Where prepayment edit maintenance does not track emerging vulnerabilities, a coverage expansion, a new code, a competitor's exit or a removed prior-auth requirement produces a step change in volume that nobody edits against. The signature is a discontinuity, not a level: a provider or market whose monthly volume of a high-cost code jumps and stays jumped.
tests.check: For each high-cost code, compute monthly paid volume per provider and per market, compare each month to a trailing baseline, and flag sustained step changes — requiring the elevation to persist for several months so a single busy month does not register.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 2 - Sustained step change in high-cost code volume
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :baseline_months (6), :ramp_multiple (2.0),
--         :sustain_months (3), :min_baseline_cases (10)
-- Portability: DATE_TRUNC is PostgreSQL/Snowflake/DuckDB style; elsewhere use DATETRUNC (SQL Server),
--   TRUNC(date, 'MM') (Oracle) or DATE_TRUNC(date, MONTH) (BigQuery).
-- The run length is set once, by :sustain_months; the window frame derives its bound from it
-- as (:sustain_months - 1) FOLLOWING, so there is no second value to keep in step.
-- Portability: a bind parameter or expression as a window frame bound is accepted by PostgreSQL
-- and DuckDB; where the bound must be a literal, write the numbers in (6 PRECEDING, 2 FOLLOWING).

WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
      cl.rendering_npi,
      cl.cpt,
      DATE_TRUNC('month', cl.service_date) AS service_month,
      COUNT(*)            AS cases,
      SUM(cl.paid_amount) AS paid_amount
  FROM claim_lines cl
  JOIN high_cost_code_register hc ON hc.hcpcs = cl.cpt
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  GROUP BY cl.rendering_npi, cl.cpt, DATE_TRUNC('month', cl.service_date)
),
with_baseline AS (
  SELECT
      m.*,
      AVG(cases) OVER (
        PARTITION BY rendering_npi, cpt ORDER BY service_month
        ROWS BETWEEN :baseline_months PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS trailing_baseline_cases,
      COUNT(*) OVER (
        PARTITION BY rendering_npi, cpt ORDER BY service_month
        ROWS BETWEEN :baseline_months PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS baseline_months_available,
      LAG(cases) OVER (PARTITION BY rendering_npi, cpt ORDER BY service_month) AS prev_month_cases,
      -- the lowest volume over this month and the next (:sustain_months - 1) months
      MIN(cases) OVER (
        PARTITION BY rendering_npi, cpt ORDER BY service_month
        ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND (:sustain_months - 1) FOLLOWING
      ) AS min_cases_in_run,
      COUNT(*) OVER (
        PARTITION BY rendering_npi, cpt ORDER BY service_month
        ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND (:sustain_months - 1) FOLLOWING
      ) AS months_in_run
  FROM monthly m
),
run_starts AS (
  -- a month where every month of a :sustain_months run is at least :ramp_multiple times
  -- the baseline measured BEFORE the run began; the baseline is then frozen at that point
  SELECT *,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rendering_npi, cpt ORDER BY service_month) AS rk
  FROM with_baseline
  WHERE baseline_months_available >= :baseline_months
    AND trailing_baseline_cases >= :min_baseline_cases
    AND months_in_run >= :sustain_months
    AND prev_month_cases < trailing_baseline_cases * :ramp_multiple   -- the run starts here, not already under way
    AND min_cases_in_run >= trailing_baseline_cases * :ramp_multiple
),
first_run AS (
  SELECT rendering_npi, cpt, service_month AS ramp_started, trailing_baseline_cases
  FROM run_starts WHERE rk = 1
)
SELECT
    f.rendering_npi, f.cpt,
    f.ramp_started,
    COUNT(*)                                   AS ramp_months,
    ROUND(f.trailing_baseline_cases, 1)        AS baseline_cases_per_month,
    ROUND(AVG(m.cases), 1)                     AS ramp_cases_per_month,
    SUM(m.paid_amount)                         AS paid_in_ramp_months
FROM first_run f
JOIN monthly m ON m.rendering_npi = f.rendering_npi AND m.cpt = f.cpt
              AND m.service_month >= f.ramp_started
              AND m.cases >= f.trailing_baseline_cases * :ramp_multiple
GROUP BY f.rendering_npi, f.cpt, f.ramp_started, f.trailing_baseline_cases
HAVING COUNT(*) >= :sustain_months
ORDER BY paid_in_ramp_months DESC;

-- Run the SAME query aggregated by market (peer_region) instead of by provider FIRST.
-- A ramp visible across an entire market is a coverage/policy event and belongs to
-- CB-17 and CD-02 - not to any provider's review queue.
tests.threshold: :ramp_multiple = 2.0 against a 6-month trailing baseline, sustained for :sustain_months = 3, with :min_baseline_cases = 10 so that a provider going from one case to three does not register as a doubling. :sustain_months is the only run-length setting: the query derives its window bound from it. Growth is not misconduct: a practice that hires a second surgeon doubles legitimately. The value of this test is in the market-level pass, which tells you whether you are looking at a provider or at a policy change you have not edited for. Run that first, always. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-17 (Prepayment edit maintenance & tuning from emerging vulnerabilities). Secondary: CD-02 (Coverage-policy change monitoring), CB-21 (High-risk-code monitoring dashboard).

CB-17 is quarterly; no board convened or recorded a decision during the ramp.
The ramp was observed and the edit decision was deferred with no documented risk acceptance.
Edit review is triggered only by external findings (OIG/GAO) and never by the payer's own volume signals, so a novel local pattern is structurally out of scope.

tests.family_title: High-cost CPT concentration — spinal fusion, cardiac EP, and high-cost diagnostics
tests.name: Spinal fusion — levels and instrumentation add-ons per case above the peer norm
tests.hypothesis: Fusion payment scales with the number of levels and the instrumentation billed. Where MUE and add-on-code enforcement are absent or applied per line, a surgeon can bill additional-level add-on codes and interbody-device codes at counts above what the operative case supports. The signature is a per-case level count distribution shifted right of peers — visible only when add-on codes are aggregated back to the case, which most edit engines do not do.
tests.check: Reconstruct the surgical case (beneficiary + date + surgeon), sum the primary and add-on level codes and the interbody-device codes, and compare the per-case level count to the specialty peer distribution.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 3 - Spinal fusion levels per case vs peers
-- Code sets are illustrative: primary fusion (22551, 22554, 22558, 22612, 22630, 22633),
-- additional-level add-ons (22552, 22585, 22614, 22632, 22634), interbody device
-- (22853, 22854, 22859), instrumentation (22840-22847). VERIFY against current CPT.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_cases (10), :min_peer_n (15), :z_threshold (2.5)
-- Portability: JOIN ... USING (...) is not accepted by SQL Server; write the ON equalities out there.

WITH fusion_case AS (
  SELECT
      cl.beneficiary_id, cl.rendering_npi, cl.service_date,
      SUM(CASE WHEN cl.cpt IN ('22551','22554','22558','22612','22630','22633')
               THEN cl.units ELSE 0 END) AS primary_levels,
      SUM(CASE WHEN cl.cpt IN ('22552','22585','22614','22632','22634')
               THEN cl.units ELSE 0 END) AS additional_levels,
      SUM(CASE WHEN cl.cpt IN ('22853','22854','22859')
               THEN cl.units ELSE 0 END) AS interbody_devices,
      SUM(CASE WHEN cl.cpt BETWEEN '22840' AND '22847'
               THEN cl.units ELSE 0 END) AS instrumentation_units,
      SUM(cl.paid_amount) AS case_paid
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND cl.cpt IN ('22551','22552','22554','22558','22585','22612','22614','22630',
                   '22632','22633','22634','22853','22854','22859',
                   '22840','22841','22842','22843','22844','22845','22846','22847')
  GROUP BY cl.beneficiary_id, cl.rendering_npi, cl.service_date
  HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN cl.cpt IN ('22551','22554','22558','22612','22630','22633')
                  THEN cl.units ELSE 0 END) > 0        -- a primary fusion anchors the case
),
by_surgeon AS (
  SELECT
      f.rendering_npi, pr.specialty, pr.peer_region,
      COUNT(*)                                      AS cases,
      AVG(f.primary_levels + f.additional_levels)   AS mean_levels_per_case,
      AVG(f.interbody_devices)                      AS mean_devices_per_case,
      MAX(f.primary_levels + f.additional_levels)   AS max_levels_in_a_case,
      SUM(f.case_paid)                              AS paid_amount
  FROM fusion_case f
  JOIN provider pr ON pr.npi = f.rendering_npi
  GROUP BY f.rendering_npi, pr.specialty, pr.peer_region
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_cases
),
peer AS (
  SELECT specialty, peer_region,
         AVG(mean_levels_per_case) AS peer_mean, STDDEV(mean_levels_per_case) AS peer_sd,
         COUNT(*) AS peer_n
  FROM by_surgeon GROUP BY specialty, peer_region HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_peer_n
)
SELECT
    s.rendering_npi, s.specialty, s.peer_region, s.cases,
    ROUND(s.mean_levels_per_case, 2)  AS mean_levels_per_case,
    ROUND(k.peer_mean, 2)             AS peer_mean_levels,
    ROUND((s.mean_levels_per_case - k.peer_mean) / NULLIF(k.peer_sd, 0), 2) AS z_score,
    ROUND(s.mean_devices_per_case, 2) AS mean_devices_per_case,
    s.max_levels_in_a_case, s.paid_amount
FROM by_surgeon s
JOIN peer k USING (specialty, peer_region)
WHERE (s.mean_levels_per_case - k.peer_mean) / NULLIF(k.peer_sd, 0) > :z_threshold
ORDER BY z_score DESC;
tests.threshold: :z_threshold = 2.5 with :min_cases = 10. The CPT lists above are illustrative and MUST be verified against the current code set before use — fusion coding is revised regularly and an out-of-date add-on list silently under-counts levels. Deformity and revision surgery legitimately carry high level counts, so exclude or stratify scoliosis and revision-fusion cases before benchmarking, or the output will be a list of deformity surgeons. `max_levels_in_a_case` is worth eyeballing independently: a single implausibly high case is an anatomy question with a definite answer. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-07 (MUE units-of-service edit enforcement). Secondary: CB-16 (Unbundling detection analytics), CB-08 (Quantity / frequency-limit edits).

MUE values are loaded but the quarterly refresh did not run for the period.
Unit overrides were granted at adjudication without operative-report review.
Edits apply per claim line and never aggregate add-on codes back to the surgical case, so level stacking across lines passes untouched. This is the defining defect for this test.
No retained adjudication log showing which unit hits fired and how they were resolved.

tests.family_title: High-cost CPT concentration — spinal fusion, cardiac EP, and high-cost diagnostics
tests.name: Spinal fusion with no documented conservative care in the lookback
tests.hypothesis: Most coverage policies for elective lumbar fusion require a documented trial of conservative management — physical therapy, injections, medication — over a defined period before surgery. Where the reasonable-and-necessary documentation control is absent or is satisfied by a checkbox, fusions proceed with no conservative-care footprint anywhere in the beneficiary's claim history.
tests.check: For each elective fusion case, look back over the policy-defined window for claims evidencing conservative management, and flag cases with none. Exclude trauma, tumour, infection and neurological-deficit indications, where conservative care is not expected.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 4 - Elective fusion with no conservative-care claims in the lookback
-- This test infers documentation from CLAIMS, which is a proxy. A clean claim history
-- does not prove the record is absent - care may have been delivered elsewhere or
-- self-paid. Output is a chart-review queue, nothing more.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :conservative_lookback_days (180)
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.

SELECT
    f.claim_line_id, f.beneficiary_id, f.rendering_npi, f.cpt AS fusion_cpt,
    f.service_date, f.paid_amount,
    dx.icd10_code AS primary_icd10,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM claim_lines c
      WHERE c.beneficiary_id = f.beneficiary_id
        AND c.service_date BETWEEN f.service_date - :conservative_lookback_days
                               AND f.service_date - 1
        AND c.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
        AND c.cpt IN (SELECT hcpcs FROM conservative_care_code_list)) AS conservative_claims
FROM claim_lines f
JOIN claim_diagnosis dx ON dx.claim_id = f.claim_id AND dx.diagnosis_sequence = 1
WHERE f.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND f.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND f.cpt IN ('22551','22554','22558','22612','22630','22633')       -- primary fusion
  -- exclude indications where conservative care is not expected
  AND dx.icd10_code NOT IN (SELECT icd10_code FROM fusion_urgent_indication_list)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM claim_lines c
    WHERE c.beneficiary_id = f.beneficiary_id
      AND c.service_date BETWEEN f.service_date - :conservative_lookback_days
                             AND f.service_date - 1
      AND c.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
      AND c.cpt IN (SELECT hcpcs FROM conservative_care_code_list)
  )
ORDER BY f.paid_amount DESC;

-- conservative_care_code_list: PT/OT (97110, 97112, 97140, 97530), epidural and
-- facet injections (62321-62323, 64483-64484, 64490-64495), chiropractic (98940-98942),
-- plus your own additions. Build it with clinical input, not from this comment.
tests.threshold: :conservative_lookback_days = 180 is a common policy window but is NOT universal — read it off the applicable NCD/LCD or plan policy rather than adopting the default. Two structural caveats govern how far this test can be pushed. First, absence of a claim is not absence of care: therapy delivered under a different payer, self-paid, or bundled into a global episode leaves no trace here. Second, the exclusion lists do the real work — build `conservative_care_code_list` and `fusion_urgent_indication_list` with clinical input before the first run. This is a chart-review queue, and it should never be described as anything else. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CD-03 (Reasonable-and-necessary documentation control). Secondary: CD-05 (Item/service-category documentation-eligibility checklist), CD-16 (Enhanced documentation review for high-cost / high-risk services).

failure_map.reading: No R&N documentation control operates for elective high-cost surgery. CD-03's R&N-supporting note requirement is not enforced for this category.
CD-03 is per-service; a population of paid fusion cases has no corresponding documentation verification.
Conservative-care attestation was accepted as a form field with no underlying record.
The control requires documentation to exist but never tests whether it substantiates the specific coverage criterion — presence, not sufficiency.
Documentation exists clinically but is not retrievable within the CD-11 retention and retrieval requirement.

tests.family_title: High-cost CPT concentration — spinal fusion, cardiac EP, and high-cost diagnostics
tests.name: Cardiac EP ablation without a supporting arrhythmia diagnosis or prior drug trial
tests.hypothesis: Catheter ablation is covered for defined arrhythmias, and many policies expect a documented trial of, or contraindication to, antiarrhythmic therapy. Where the diagnosis-to-service linkage edit is absent or checks only the primary diagnosis position, ablations pay with no supporting arrhythmia diagnosis anywhere on the claim and no pharmacological history.
tests.check: For each ablation claim, test whether any diagnosis position carries a covered arrhythmia code, and separately whether the beneficiary has any antiarrhythmic drug claim in the lookback. Report the two conditions independently — they fail for different reasons and point at different controls.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 5 - Ablation without supporting diagnosis or prior antiarrhythmic therapy
-- Ablation CPTs (illustrative): 93653, 93654, 93656 (comprehensive EP with ablation),
-- 93655, 93657 (add-on). VERIFY against current CPT and the applicable LCD.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :drug_lookback_days (365)
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.

SELECT
    a.claim_line_id, a.beneficiary_id, a.rendering_npi, a.billing_npi,
    a.cpt AS ablation_cpt, a.service_date, a.paid_amount,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM claim_diagnosis d
        JOIN covered_arrhythmia_dx cd ON cd.icd10_code = d.icd10_code
        WHERE d.claim_id = a.claim_id
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_covered_arrhythmia_dx,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM pharmacy_claim rx
        JOIN antiarrhythmic_drug_list ad ON ad.ndc = rx.ndc
        WHERE rx.beneficiary_id = a.beneficiary_id
          AND rx.fill_date BETWEEN a.service_date - :drug_lookback_days AND a.service_date
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_prior_antiarrhythmic,
    CASE
      WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claim_diagnosis d
                       JOIN covered_arrhythmia_dx cd ON cd.icd10_code = d.icd10_code
                       WHERE d.claim_id = a.claim_id)
        THEN 'NO_SUPPORTING_DIAGNOSIS'      -- edit failure: CB-11
      ELSE 'NO_PRIOR_DRUG_TRIAL'            -- coverage-criteria question: CD-01, chart review
    END AS finding_class
FROM claim_lines a
WHERE a.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND a.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND a.cpt IN ('93653','93654','93655','93656','93657')
  AND (
    NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claim_diagnosis d
                JOIN covered_arrhythmia_dx cd ON cd.icd10_code = d.icd10_code
                WHERE d.claim_id = a.claim_id)
    OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pharmacy_claim rx
                   JOIN antiarrhythmic_drug_list ad ON ad.ndc = rx.ndc
                   WHERE rx.beneficiary_id = a.beneficiary_id
                     AND rx.fill_date BETWEEN a.service_date - :drug_lookback_days
                                          AND a.service_date)
  )
ORDER BY finding_class, a.paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: NO_SUPPORTING_DIAGNOSIS is close to categorical and is an edit-configuration finding — the claim should not have adjudicated. NO_PRIOR_DRUG_TRIAL is not a finding at all on its own: drug intolerance, contraindication, and patient preference are all legitimate paths to first-line ablation, and pharmacy data may sit with a different payer entirely. Work the diagnosis bucket first; treat the drug bucket as a chart-review sample sized to your review capacity, not as a worklist. If you do not hold pharmacy claims, drop that half of the test rather than substituting a weaker proxy. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-11 (Diagnosis-to-service medical-necessity linkage edit — NCD/LCD). Secondary: CD-01 (Coverage-criteria application), CD-16 (Enhanced documentation review for high-cost / high-risk services).

failure_map.reading: No necessity-linkage edit covers this procedure family. CB-11's necessity-edit disposition does not exist.
The edit is specified but not active in the adjudication path for these codes.
Edit hits were overridden without a documented coverage rationale.
The edit inspects the primary diagnosis position only, so a supporting arrhythmia code in a secondary position fails the edit while an unsupported claim with the right code in position one passes.
No retained record of edit hits and dispositions for this code family.

tests.family_title: High-cost CPT concentration — spinal fusion, cardiac EP, and high-cost diagnostics
tests.name: Implantable cardiac device inside an NCD waiting period
tests.hypothesis: The ICD national coverage determination imposes waiting periods — for example after myocardial infarction, after revascularisation, and after a new diagnosis of heart failure — before a prophylactic implant is covered. Where the coverage-criteria control is absent or applies stale criteria, implants pay inside those windows. This is the single most litigated coverage-criteria area in cardiology and the basis of a national hospital settlement programme.
tests.check: For each device implant, look back for a qualifying index event — MI, CABG, PCI, or first heart-failure diagnosis — and flag implants falling inside the applicable waiting period, excluding the indications that override it.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 6 - ICD implant inside an NCD waiting period
-- Waiting periods and exceptions are set by the applicable NCD/LCD and change over time.
-- Load them as a versioned reference table (ncd_waiting_period); do not hardcode.
-- Event dating: MI, CABG and PCI are dated at the LATEST qualifying claim before the implant.
-- A first-diagnosis event (NEW_HF_DX) is dated at the EARLIEST qualifying claim held, so a
-- long-standing heart-failure patient with a recent pre-operative visit is not read as new.
-- That is only as good as the claims history you hold: require enough look-back per patient.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end
