    c.entity_npi, c.cluster_size, c.linked_entities, c.distinct_link_types, c.link_types,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cl.paid_amount), 0) FROM claim_lines cl
      WHERE cl.billing_npi = c.entity_npi
        AND cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
        AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID') AS entity_paid,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ownership_disclosure od WHERE od.entity_npi = c.entity_npi)
      AS disclosed_owners
FROM clusters c
WHERE c.cluster_size >= :min_cluster_size
ORDER BY c.distinct_link_types DESC, entity_paid DESC;
tests.threshold: :min_cluster_size = 3 entities (the entity itself plus two linked directly to it), and every member of a cluster is listed. `distinct_link_types` is the discriminating column — two entities sharing an address is a medical office building, two entities sharing an address *and* a bank account *and* a phone is something else. Rank on link-type diversity, not edge count. The exclusion lists are mandatory rather than optional: commercial registered agents serve thousands of entities, medical office buildings and billing companies legitimately share addresses and phones, and without those exclusions the largest cluster in your data will be a registered-agent artifact. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PE-05 (Beneficial-ownership network/graph analysis). Secondary: PE-04 (Owner reconciliation vs. record + OIG/SAM/adverse databases), MD-03 (Ownership/control & business-transaction disclosure capture + verification).

failure_map.reading: No graph or network analysis exists. PE-05's network-link alert disposition does not exist.
PE-05 is monthly; no portfolio scan ran in the period.
Network links were surfaced and no enhanced screening or investigation followed.
The analysis uses disclosed ownership only and no shared-attribute edges, so networks that hide ownership — which is the point of a shell ring — are invisible to it.
Analysis performed with no retained alert or disposition record.

tests.family_title: Provider identity, credential integrity, and incident-to billing
tests.name: Undisclosed ownership or control change within the reporting window
tests.hypothesis: 42 CFR 424.516 requires reporting of ownership and control changes within 30 days. Where enforcement and unreported-change detection are absent, entities change hands silently — and a change of control without disclosure is how an excluded or adverse party takes over a clean billing number. PE-06 also cites the 2025 OIG EFT payment-diversion recommendation, which is the same failure seen from the banking side.
tests.check: Compare the enrollment ownership record against external sources — Secretary of State filings, corporate registries, banking changes — and flag entities where an external change has no corresponding disclosure within the reporting window.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 10 - External ownership/control change with no corresponding disclosure
-- 42 CFR 424.516 (30-day reporting).
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :report_window_days (30)
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.

SELECT
    ext.entity_npi,
    ext.source,                       -- 'SOS_FILING' | 'EFT_CHANGE' | 'REGISTRY' | 'SAM'
    ext.change_type,                  -- 'OFFICER' | 'OWNER' | 'AGENT' | 'BANKING' | 'NAME'
    ext.change_date,
    ext.old_value_hash, ext.new_value_hash,
    d.disclosure_id, d.disclosure_date,
    CASE
      WHEN d.disclosure_id IS NULL THEN 'NO_DISCLOSURE'
      WHEN d.disclosure_date > ext.change_date + :report_window_days THEN 'LATE_DISCLOSURE'
      ELSE 'TIMELY'
    END AS disclosure_status,
    COALESCE(d.disclosure_date, CURRENT_DATE) - ext.change_date AS days_to_disclosure,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cl.paid_amount), 0) FROM claim_lines cl
      WHERE cl.billing_npi = ext.entity_npi
        AND cl.service_date > ext.change_date
        AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID') AS paid_since_change
FROM external_entity_change ext
-- earliest disclosure on or after the change, whenever it was filed; the CASE then
-- separates timely from late (a join limited to the window could never see a late one)
LEFT JOIN (SELECT e.entity_npi, e.change_date, MIN(o.disclosure_date) AS first_disclosure_date
           FROM external_entity_change e
           JOIN ownership_disclosure o
             ON o.entity_npi = e.entity_npi AND o.disclosure_date >= e.change_date
           GROUP BY e.entity_npi, e.change_date) fd
       ON  fd.entity_npi = ext.entity_npi AND fd.change_date = ext.change_date
LEFT JOIN ownership_disclosure d
       ON  d.entity_npi = fd.entity_npi
       AND d.disclosure_date = fd.first_disclosure_date
WHERE ext.change_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND (d.disclosure_id IS NULL
       OR d.disclosure_date > ext.change_date + :report_window_days)
ORDER BY paid_since_change DESC;

-- Cross-check every NO_DISCLOSURE hit against the exclusion lists for the NEW owner or
-- officer. An undisclosed change of control TO an excluded party is a different and much
-- more serious finding than a late filing, and it is the reason the rule exists.
tests.threshold: The 30-day window is regulatory, not tunable. What is tunable is which external sources you trust and how you resolve their entity identifiers to NPIs, and that resolution is the hard part — Secretary of State records use legal entity names that map imperfectly to enrolled provider names. Expect a meaningful false-positive rate from name-matching alone and treat unresolved matches as candidates. The `paid_since_change` column sizes the exposure; the exclusion cross-check noted in the query is what separates an administrative lapse from the case the rule exists to prevent. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PE-06 (30-day ownership-change enforcement & unreported-change detection). Secondary: MD-03 (Ownership/control & business-transaction disclosure capture + verification), PE-04 (Owner reconciliation vs. record + OIG/SAM/adverse databases).

failure_map.reading: No unreported-change detection. PE-06's change-report tracking log does not exist.
PE-06 specifies continuous monitoring with monthly external-feed reconciliation; no reconciliation ran.
Undisclosed changes were identified and no enrollment action, re-screening or payment hold followed.
The control tracks disclosures received but never reconciles against an external feed, so it can only detect late filings, never absent ones.
No retained tracking log evidencing which changes were reconciled.

tests.family_title: Provider identity, credential integrity, and incident-to billing
tests.name: Multi-source link analysis — cross-provider scheme convergence
tests.hypothesis: Individual providers in a coordinated scheme each look ordinary. The scheme is visible only where claims, enrollment, encounter and external data converge: shared beneficiary panels, sequential referral chains, common staff moving between entities, synchronised billing patterns. Where multi-source link analysis is absent, cross-provider schemes are missed by construction — PI-03's stated failure mode.
tests.check: Build provider-to-provider edges from beneficiary overlap, referral flow and shared rendering personnel, and surface tightly-connected components whose internal linkage far exceeds what geography and specialty would predict.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 11 - Provider convergence: shared panels, referral chains, shared personnel
-- Edge list for a graph platform.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_shared_beneficiaries (25), :jaccard_threshold (0.30)

WITH panel_overlap AS (
  SELECT
      a.billing_npi AS provider_a,
      b.billing_npi AS provider_b,
      COUNT(DISTINCT a.beneficiary_id) AS shared_beneficiaries
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT billing_npi, beneficiary_id FROM claim_lines
        WHERE service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
          AND adjudication_status = 'PAID') a
  JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT billing_npi, beneficiary_id FROM claim_lines
        WHERE service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
          AND adjudication_status = 'PAID') b
    ON a.beneficiary_id = b.beneficiary_id AND a.billing_npi < b.billing_npi
  GROUP BY a.billing_npi, b.billing_npi
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.beneficiary_id) >= :min_shared_beneficiaries
),
panel_sizes AS (
  SELECT billing_npi, COUNT(DISTINCT beneficiary_id) AS panel_size
  FROM claim_lines
  WHERE service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end AND adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  GROUP BY billing_npi
),
shared_staff AS (
  SELECT a.billing_npi AS provider_a, b.billing_npi AS provider_b,
         COUNT(DISTINCT a.rendering_npi) AS shared_renderers
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT billing_npi, rendering_npi FROM claim_lines
        WHERE service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end) a
  JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT billing_npi, rendering_npi FROM claim_lines
        WHERE service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end) b
    ON a.rendering_npi = b.rendering_npi AND a.billing_npi < b.billing_npi
  GROUP BY a.billing_npi, b.billing_npi
)
SELECT
    po.provider_a, po.provider_b,
    po.shared_beneficiaries,
    pa.panel_size AS panel_a, pb.panel_size AS panel_b,
    -- Jaccard: overlap relative to combined panel size, not raw count
    ROUND(po.shared_beneficiaries * 1.0 /
          NULLIF(pa.panel_size + pb.panel_size - po.shared_beneficiaries, 0), 3) AS jaccard,
    COALESCE(ss.shared_renderers, 0) AS shared_renderers
FROM panel_overlap po
JOIN panel_sizes pa ON pa.billing_npi = po.provider_a
JOIN panel_sizes pb ON pb.billing_npi = po.provider_b
LEFT JOIN shared_staff ss ON ss.provider_a = po.provider_a AND ss.provider_b = po.provider_b
WHERE po.shared_beneficiaries * 1.0 /
      NULLIF(pa.panel_size + pb.panel_size - po.shared_beneficiaries, 0) > :jaccard_threshold
ORDER BY jaccard DESC, po.shared_beneficiaries DESC;
tests.threshold: Use the Jaccard coefficient rather than the raw overlap count — two large practices in one city will share hundreds of patients and mean nothing by it, while two small entities sharing 80% of a panel mean a great deal. :jaccard_threshold = 0.30 is a starting cut. Referral relationships, hospital-affiliated groups, ACOs and integrated delivery systems all produce high overlap legitimately and should be excluded via a known-affiliation list before the first run. `shared_renderers` is the second dimension worth ranking on: shared patients plus shared staff plus no disclosed affiliation is the interesting conjunction. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PI-03 (Multi-source link analysis — claims + enrollment + encounter + external). Secondary: PE-05 (Beneficial-ownership network/graph analysis), PI-22 (Entity-network cash-loop detection).

failure_map.reading: No link analysis capability. PI-03's network-link alert disposition does not exist.
PI-03 is monthly; no scheme-detection scan ran.
Networks were surfaced and no case was opened or referral made.
The analysis runs on claims only, so enrollment, ownership and external attributes never enter the graph and the links that define a scheme are unavailable to it.
Analysis run with no retained output or disposition.

tests.family_title: Provider identity, credential integrity, and incident-to billing
tests.name: Credentialing re-attestation lapse in payer networks
tests.hypothesis: Payer network credentialing depends on providers re-attesting to the currency of their data on a defined cycle. Where re-attestation is not enforced, network directories and credentialing files carry stale data — PE-18's stated failure mode — and the payer's assurance about who is in its network degrades quietly while claims continue to pay.
tests.check: For each network provider, compute days since last attestation and last primary-source verification, flag those beyond the cycle, and attach the claims paid during the lapsed interval to size the exposure.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 12 - Attestation and PSV currency across the network
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :attestation_cycle_days (120)
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.

SELECT
    c.npi, c.provider_name_hash, c.network_id, c.specialty,
    c.last_attestation_date,
    CURRENT_DATE - c.last_attestation_date AS days_since_attestation,
    c.last_psv_date,
    CURRENT_DATE - c.last_psv_date         AS days_since_psv,
    c.licence_expiry, c.dea_expiry, c.malpractice_expiry,
    CASE
      WHEN c.licence_expiry   < CURRENT_DATE                          THEN 'LICENCE_EXPIRED'
      WHEN c.malpractice_expiry < CURRENT_DATE                        THEN 'COVERAGE_EXPIRED'
      WHEN c.last_attestation_date IS NULL                            THEN 'NEVER_ATTESTED'
      WHEN CURRENT_DATE - c.last_attestation_date > :attestation_cycle_days
                                                                      THEN 'ATTESTATION_LAPSED'
    END AS credential_defect,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cl.paid_amount), 0) FROM claim_lines cl
      WHERE cl.rendering_npi = c.npi
        AND cl.service_date > COALESCE(c.last_attestation_date, DATE '1900-01-01')
                              + :attestation_cycle_days
        AND cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
        AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID') AS paid_during_lapse
FROM credentialing_record c
WHERE c.network_status = 'ACTIVE'
  AND (c.last_attestation_date IS NULL
       OR CURRENT_DATE - c.last_attestation_date > :attestation_cycle_days
       OR c.licence_expiry     < CURRENT_DATE
       OR c.malpractice_expiry < CURRENT_DATE)
ORDER BY paid_during_lapse DESC;
tests.threshold: :attestation_cycle_days = 120 matches the CAQH ProView cadence PE-18 names; confirm against your own delegated-credentialing agreements, which may differ. Note what this test does and does not show: an attestation lapse is an assurance failure, not evidence that anything is wrong with the provider, and `paid_during_lapse` sizes the volume of claims paid without current assurance rather than an overpayment. Expired licence and expired malpractice coverage are materially more serious than a late attestation and should be reported separately rather than as one defect count. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PE-18 (CAQH ProView primary-source verification & 120-day re-attestation). Secondary: PE-01 (Primary-source verification of enrollment data), MC-11 (FDR inventory, pre-contract screening & periodic audit).

failure_map.reading: No re-attestation cycle operates. PE-18's attestation/PSV record does not exist.
The cycle is defined but a population of active network providers is past due.
Lapsed providers remained in-network and payable with no restriction applied.
Attestation is collected but not primary-source verified, so the control confirms the provider said something rather than that it is true.
Credentialing is delegated and no attestation evidence is retained by the payer.

tests.family_title: Provider identity, credential integrity, and incident-to billing
tests.name: Synthetic-identity indicators at enrollment
tests.hypothesis: PE-20 exists because AI-fabricated and synthetic provider identities can pass document-based screening. Where identity-proofing is absent, a synthetic identity enrolls successfully and every downstream control then operates faithfully on a person who does not exist. The data signature is thin history: an identity with a credential but no corroborating footprint anywhere else.
tests.check: For each recently enrolled individual provider, count corroborating records across independent sources — NPPES history, state licence board, DEA registry, medical school and residency verification, prior claims history under any payer, Open Payments — and flag identities corroborated by few or none.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 13 - Corroboration thinness for recently enrolled individual providers
-- A synthetic identity is characterised by ABSENCE across independent sources.
-- This is a screening-quality test; it does not identify fraud on its own.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_corroborating_sources (3)
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.

WITH recent AS (
  SELECT e.npi, e.enrollment_effective_date, e.provider_type, e.risk_level
  FROM provider_enrollment e
  WHERE e.enrollment_effective_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND e.entity_type = 'INDIVIDUAL'
)
SELECT
    r.npi, r.enrollment_effective_date, r.provider_type, r.risk_level,
    CASE WHEN n.npi IS NOT NULL AND n.enumeration_date < r.enrollment_effective_date - 365
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS nppes_history,
    CASE WHEN lic.npi IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS state_licence_verified,
    CASE WHEN dea.npi IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS dea_registered,
    CASE WHEN edu.npi IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS education_verified,
    CASE WHEN hist.npi IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS prior_claim_history,
    CASE WHEN op.physician_npi IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS open_payments_presence,
    CASE WHEN idp.npi IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS identity_proofing_performed,
    (CASE WHEN n.npi IS NOT NULL AND n.enumeration_date < r.enrollment_effective_date - 365 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     + CASE WHEN lic.npi  IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     + CASE WHEN dea.npi  IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     + CASE WHEN edu.npi  IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     + CASE WHEN hist.npi IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     + CASE WHEN op.physician_npi IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS corroborating_sources,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cl.paid_amount), 0) FROM claim_lines cl
      WHERE cl.rendering_npi = r.npi AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID') AS paid_to_date
FROM recent r
LEFT JOIN nppes_snapshot n       ON n.npi = r.npi
LEFT JOIN provider_licence lic   ON lic.npi = r.npi AND lic.licence_status = 'ACTIVE'
LEFT JOIN dea_registration dea   ON dea.npi = r.npi
LEFT JOIN education_verification edu ON edu.npi = r.npi
LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT rendering_npi AS npi FROM claim_lines
            WHERE service_date < :period_start) hist ON hist.npi = r.npi
LEFT JOIN open_payments_summary op ON op.physician_npi = r.npi
LEFT JOIN identity_proofing_log idp ON idp.npi = r.npi
WHERE (CASE WHEN n.npi IS NOT NULL AND n.enumeration_date < r.enrollment_effective_date - 365 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     + CASE WHEN lic.npi  IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     + CASE WHEN dea.npi  IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     + CASE WHEN edu.npi  IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     + CASE WHEN hist.npi IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     + CASE WHEN op.physician_npi IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) < :min_corroborating_sources
ORDER BY corroborating_sources ASC, paid_to_date DESC;
tests.threshold: :min_corroborating_sources = 3 is a starting cut and must be read with real care, because thin corroboration is the normal condition of a genuinely new provider. A newly-licensed clinician has no prior claim history, no Open Payments presence, possibly no DEA registration, and a recent NPPES enumeration — they will score low and be entirely legitimate. This test is therefore not a fraud detector; it is a measure of whether identity-proofing (the `identity_proofing_performed` column) was applied where corroboration was thin. Read those two columns together: thin corroboration *and* no identity proofing is the PE-20 finding. Thin corroboration with proofing performed is the control working. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PE-20 (Synthetic-identity & deepfake identity-proofing at enrollment / high-risk change). Secondary: PE-01 (Primary-source verification of enrollment data), PE-13 (Fingerprint-based background checks).

failure_map.reading: No identity proofing at enrollment. PE-20's identity-proofing log does not exist.
PE-20 is per-application; a population of approved individual enrollments has no proofing record.
Proofing returned an inconclusive or adverse result and the enrollment proceeded.
Proofing verifies documents rather than liveness and registry cross-match, which is precisely the check a synthetic or deepfaked identity is built to pass.
Proofing performed by a vendor with no per-applicant result retained.

tests.family_title: Provider identity, credential integrity, and incident-to billing
tests.name: Downstream entity rendering services but absent from the FDR inventory
tests.hypothesis: Plans are accountable for first-tier, downstream and related entities. Where the FDR inventory is incomplete, entities render or bill services with no screening, no training and no audit coverage — MC-11's stated failure mode, 'downstream entity fraud unmonitored'. The inventory is an assertion; the claim stream is the fact against which to test it.
tests.check: Extract every distinct entity appearing as billing, rendering or referring party on the plan's claims and encounters, and reconcile against the FDR register and the contracted-provider file. Report entities present in the data but absent from both.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 14 - Entities in the claim stream absent from the FDR / contracted-provider registers
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end
-- Portability: date +/- integer days and date - date (a day count) are PostgreSQL/DuckDB style;
--   elsewhere use DATEADD / DATE_ADD for the offset and DATEDIFF / DATE_DIFF for the difference.

WITH entities_in_data AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT plan_npi, billing_npi AS entity_npi, 'BILLING' AS role
  FROM claim_lines
  WHERE service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end AND adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT plan_npi, rendering_npi, 'RENDERING'
  FROM claim_lines
  WHERE service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end AND adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND rendering_npi IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT plan_npi, vendor_npi, 'DELEGATED_VENDOR'
  FROM delegated_service_log
  WHERE service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
)
SELECT
    e.plan_npi, e.entity_npi, e.role,
    fdr.fdr_id, fdr.screening_date, fdr.last_audit_date,
    cp.contract_id, cp.contract_effective,
    CASE
      WHEN fdr.fdr_id IS NULL AND cp.contract_id IS NULL THEN 'NOT_IN_ANY_REGISTER'
      WHEN fdr.fdr_id IS NULL                            THEN 'CONTRACTED_NOT_IN_FDR_REGISTER'
      WHEN fdr.screening_date IS NULL                    THEN 'IN_REGISTER_NEVER_SCREENED'
      WHEN fdr.last_audit_date IS NULL
        OR fdr.last_audit_date < CURRENT_DATE - 365      THEN 'AUDIT_OVERDUE'
      WHEN cp.contract_id IS NULL
       AND e.role <> 'DELEGATED_VENDOR'                  THEN 'IN_FDR_REGISTER_NOT_CONTRACTED'
    END AS register_defect,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cl.paid_amount), 0) FROM claim_lines cl
      WHERE cl.billing_npi = e.entity_npi
        AND cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
        AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID') AS entity_paid
FROM entities_in_data e
LEFT JOIN fdr_register fdr      ON fdr.entity_npi = e.entity_npi AND fdr.plan_npi = e.plan_npi
LEFT JOIN contracted_provider cp ON cp.provider_npi = e.entity_npi AND cp.plan_npi = e.plan_npi
WHERE fdr.fdr_id IS NULL
   OR (cp.contract_id IS NULL AND e.role <> 'DELEGATED_VENDOR')   -- a screened, audited FDR vendor needs no provider contract
   OR fdr.screening_date IS NULL
   OR fdr.last_audit_date IS NULL
   OR fdr.last_audit_date < CURRENT_DATE - 365
ORDER BY register_defect, entity_paid DESC;
tests.threshold: Categorical against the registers, but the register definitions do real work here. Not every entity in a claim stream is an FDR — out-of-network emergency providers, one-off referrals and non-contracted ancillary providers legitimately appear without a contract or an FDR entry, and NOT_IN_ANY_REGISTER will be dominated by them unless out-of-network claims are excluded first. The genuinely interesting classes are IN_REGISTER_NEVER_SCREENED and AUDIT_OVERDUE, which are about the plan's own execution against entities it has already acknowledged. Start there. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: MC-11 (FDR inventory, pre-contract screening & periodic audit). Secondary: PE-18 (CAQH ProView PSV & re-attestation), MD-10 (MCO contract PI safeguards).

failure_map.reading: No FDR register exists. MC-11's FDR audit report does not exist.
The register exists but no annual audit cycle ran in the period.
Entities were identified as unscreened and continued to render services with no remediation.
The register is populated from contracts only and never reconciled against the claim stream, so entities operating without a contract are invisible to it.
Audits performed by the FDR itself with no evidence retained by the plan.

tests.family_title: Provider identity, credential integrity, and incident-to billing
tests.name: Entity-network cash loop — claim proceeds recycling among related parties
tests.hypothesis: Where follow-the-money analytics are absent, entity clusters can recycle claim proceeds through inter-entity transfers inconsistent with legitimate operations — converting payments into cash for kickbacks or extraction. PI-22 cites an adult day-care self-funding loop from the enforcement record. The signature is circularity: money leaving an entity and returning to the network it came from.
tests.check: Build a payment graph across related entities from claim payments and inter-entity transfers, and detect cycles — money paid to entity A flowing to B and back toward A's owners or A itself — weighted by the share of receipts that recirculate.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 15 - Circular value flow within an entity cluster
-- Requires inter-entity payment data (vendor payments, management fees, rent, payroll to
-- related parties). Many payers do not hold this; where it exists it is usually obtained
-- in an investigation rather than standing.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :recirculation_threshold (0.20)

WITH receipts AS (
  SELECT cl.billing_npi AS entity_npi, SUM(cl.paid_amount) AS claim_receipts
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  GROUP BY cl.billing_npi
),
transfers AS (
  SELECT t.payer_entity_npi, t.payee_entity_npi, t.transfer_category,
         SUM(t.amount) AS amount
  FROM inter_entity_transfer t
  WHERE t.transfer_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  GROUP BY t.payer_entity_npi, t.payee_entity_npi, t.transfer_category
),
two_hop_cycles AS (
  -- A -> B -> A, and A -> B -> C where C shares an owner with A
  SELECT
      t1.payer_entity_npi AS origin,
      t1.payee_entity_npi AS hop1,
      t2.payee_entity_npi AS hop2,
      t1.amount AS leg1_amount, t2.amount AS leg2_amount,
      t1.transfer_category AS leg1_category, t2.transfer_category AS leg2_category,
      CASE WHEN t2.payee_entity_npi = t1.payer_entity_npi THEN 'DIRECT_LOOP'
           ELSE 'OWNER_LINKED_LOOP' END AS loop_type
  FROM transfers t1
  JOIN transfers t2 ON t2.payer_entity_npi = t1.payee_entity_npi
  WHERE t2.payee_entity_npi = t1.payer_entity_npi
     OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ownership_disclosure o1
                JOIN ownership_disclosure o2
                  ON o1.owner_identity_hash = o2.owner_identity_hash
                WHERE o1.entity_npi = t1.payer_entity_npi
                  AND o2.entity_npi = t2.payee_entity_npi)
)
SELECT
    c.origin, c.hop1, c.hop2, c.loop_type,
    c.leg1_category, c.leg2_category,
    c.leg1_amount, c.leg2_amount,
    r.claim_receipts,
    ROUND(LEAST(c.leg1_amount, c.leg2_amount) / NULLIF(r.claim_receipts, 0), 3)
      AS recirculated_share
FROM two_hop_cycles c
JOIN receipts r ON r.entity_npi = c.origin
WHERE LEAST(c.leg1_amount, c.leg2_amount) / NULLIF(r.claim_receipts, 0) > :recirculation_threshold
ORDER BY recirculated_share DESC, r.claim_receipts DESC;
tests.threshold: :recirculation_threshold = 0.20 of claim receipts recirculating through a two-hop loop is a starting cut. Be clear about what this test can and cannot be: inter-entity transfers are overwhelmingly legitimate — management fees, rent to a related property company, shared services, payroll through a PEO — and circularity in a commonly-owned group is normal corporate structure, not evidence of anything. The `transfer_category` columns matter more than the amounts: loops running through categories with no plausible service content are the ones worth asking about. Most payers will not hold this data at all, in which case that absence is the PI-22 finding and the query is a specification for what investigators would need to request. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PI-22 (Entity-network cash-loop detection). Secondary: PE-05 (Beneficial-ownership network/graph analysis), PI-23 (MSO/investment-disguised kickback detection).

failure_map.reading: No follow-the-money capability. PI-22's entity-network transfer-pattern alert does not exist.
PI-22 is quarterly; no analysis ran in the period.
Loops were identified and no investigation, referral or legal assessment followed.
The analysis runs on claim payments only, with no inter-entity transfer data, so it can see money going out and never where it goes next — which is the entire question.
Analysis performed inside an investigation with no standing alert record or disposition.

tests.family_title: Provider identity, credential integrity, and incident-to billing
tests.name: AI-fabricated supporting documentation — corroboration mismatch
tests.hypothesis: PI-24 states the principle directly: treat submitted documentation as a claim to be independently corroborated rather than as evidence. Where that control is absent, AI-generated records that pass visual and structural review support payment. Because fabricated documentation is internally consistent by construction, the only reliable signal is external: the document asserts facts that independent data contradicts or cannot confirm.
tests.check: For documentation submitted in support of high-risk or audit-flagged claims, test each externally checkable assertion — the ordering provider existed and was active, the referenced prior encounter exists, the referenced test result has a corresponding lab claim, the signing clinician was licensed on the signature date — and report documents with assertions that fail corroboration.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 16 - Documentation assertions that independent data cannot corroborate
-- Pair with CD-20 (C2PA / Content Credentials provenance screening), which tests the
-- ARTIFACT; this tests the CLAIMS the artifact makes. Both are needed.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

SELECT
    d.document_id, d.claim_id, d.document_type, d.received_date,
    d.asserted_author_npi, d.asserted_signature_date,
    d.asserted_prior_encounter_date, d.asserted_test_result_date,
    -- corroboration checks, each independently verifiable
    CASE WHEN p.npi IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS author_npi_exists,
    CASE WHEN lic.npi IS NOT NULL
          AND d.asserted_signature_date BETWEEN lic.licence_effective
                                            AND COALESCE(lic.licence_expiry, DATE '9999-12-31')
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS author_licensed_on_signature_date,
    CASE WHEN p.date_of_death IS NOT NULL
          AND d.asserted_signature_date > p.date_of_death
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS signed_after_author_death,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claim_lines e
                      WHERE e.beneficiary_id = d.beneficiary_id
                        AND e.rendering_npi  = d.asserted_author_npi
                        AND e.service_date   = d.asserted_prior_encounter_date
                        AND e.adjudication_status = 'PAID')
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS prior_encounter_corroborated,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claim_lines l
                      WHERE l.beneficiary_id = d.beneficiary_id
                        AND l.service_date   = d.asserted_test_result_date
                        AND l.hcpcs IN (SELECT hcpcs FROM lab_service_code_list)
                        AND l.adjudication_status = 'PAID')
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS test_result_corroborated,
    prov.provenance_result, prov.c2pa_present
FROM submitted_document d
LEFT JOIN provider p        ON p.npi = d.asserted_author_npi
LEFT JOIN provider_licence lic ON lic.npi = d.asserted_author_npi
LEFT JOIN document_provenance prov ON prov.document_id = d.document_id
WHERE d.received_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND (p.npi IS NULL
       OR (p.date_of_death IS NOT NULL AND d.asserted_signature_date > p.date_of_death)
       OR (d.asserted_prior_encounter_date IS NOT NULL      -- only test what the document asserts
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claim_lines e
                      WHERE e.beneficiary_id = d.beneficiary_id
                        AND e.rendering_npi  = d.asserted_author_npi
                        AND e.service_date   = d.asserted_prior_encounter_date
                        AND e.adjudication_status = 'PAID'))
       OR (d.asserted_test_result_date IS NOT NULL
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claim_lines l
                      WHERE l.beneficiary_id = d.beneficiary_id
                        AND l.service_date   = d.asserted_test_result_date
                        AND l.hcpcs IN (SELECT hcpcs FROM lab_service_code_list)
                        AND l.adjudication_status = 'PAID')))
ORDER BY d.received_date DESC;
tests.threshold: Each corroboration check is binary, but they are not equal. `signed_after_author_death` and a non-existent author NPI are near-conclusive. An uncorroborated prior encounter or test result is much weaker: care delivered under another payer, self-paid services and simple date transcription errors all produce it, and a document describing real care will frequently fail these checks. Count the failures rather than acting on any single one, and read the result alongside CD-20's provenance screening — an absent C2PA manifest proves nothing on its own (most legitimate documents lack one today), but absent provenance combined with multiple failed corroborations is a coherent picture. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PI-24 (AI-fabricated-evidence corroboration analytics). Secondary: CD-20 (AI-generated / altered document & image provenance screening), CD-07 (Copy-forward / templated-note control).

failure_map.reading: Submitted documentation is accepted at face value. PI-24's corroboration-mismatch exception report does not exist.
PI-24 is continuous / per review cycle; no corroboration was performed on documentation received in the period.
Corroboration failed and the claim was paid on the strength of the document anyway.
Review inspects the document for internal consistency and legibility — exactly the properties generated documentation has in abundance — and never tests its assertions against independent data.
Reviews occurred with no retained record of which assertions were corroborated.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Order-to-encounter gap — DMEPOS with no encounter between beneficiary and ordering provider
tests.hypothesis: Applicable DMEPOS items require a documented face-to-face encounter with the ordering practitioner. Where face-to-face and written-order verification is absent, items are ordered by clinicians who never saw the beneficiary — the defining signature of the telemarketing-driven DME schemes. The pattern is visible without any documentation at all: no claim anywhere shows the ordering provider and the beneficiary in the same encounter.
tests.check: For each paid DMEPOS claim, look back over the applicable window for any professional or telehealth encounter between the beneficiary and the ordering NPI. Report items with no encounter at all, and separately those where the only encounter is a brief telehealth contact on or immediately before the order date.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 1 - DMEPOS with no encounter between beneficiary and ordering provider
-- Applies the F2F window, separates 'no encounter at all' from 'telehealth-only
-- immediately before the order', and carries the supplier so the roll-up works in both
-- directions.
-- 42 CFR 410.38. Params: :period_start, :period_end, :f2f_window_days (180)

WITH dme AS (
  SELECT
      d.claim_id, d.claim_line_id, d.beneficiary_id,
      d.ordering_npi, d.billing_npi AS supplier_npi,
      d.hcpcs, d.service_date, d.paid_amount
  FROM claim_lines d
  WHERE d.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND d.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND d.claim_type = 'DMEPOS'
    AND d.ordering_npi IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    dme.*,
    enc.any_encounters,
    enc.inperson_encounters,
    enc.telehealth_encounters,
    enc.last_encounter_date,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(enc.any_encounters, 0) = 0            THEN 'NO_ENCOUNTER_AT_ALL'
      WHEN COALESCE(enc.inperson_encounters, 0) = 0
       AND enc.telehealth_encounters > 0                  THEN 'TELEHEALTH_ONLY'
      ELSE 'ENCOUNTER_PRESENT'
    END AS encounter_class
FROM dme
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS any_encounters,
        SUM(CASE WHEN e.place_of_service NOT IN ('02','10') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS inperson_encounters,
        SUM(CASE WHEN e.place_of_service IN ('02','10')     THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS telehealth_encounters,
        MAX(e.service_date) AS last_encounter_date
    FROM claim_lines e
    WHERE e.beneficiary_id = dme.beneficiary_id
      AND e.rendering_npi  = dme.ordering_npi
      AND e.claim_type IN ('PROFESSIONAL','TELEHEALTH')
      AND e.cpt BETWEEN '99202' AND '99215'
      AND e.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
      AND e.service_date BETWEEN dme.service_date - :f2f_window_days AND dme.service_date
) enc ON TRUE
WHERE COALESCE(enc.any_encounters, 0) = 0
   OR COALESCE(enc.inperson_encounters, 0) = 0
ORDER BY encounter_class, dme.paid_amount DESC;

-- Roll up BOTH ways: by ordering_npi (test 2) and by supplier_npi. A supplier whose
-- entire book has no encounter footprint is a different proposition from one with a
-- handful of gaps, and the supplier roll-up is the one that sizes the exposure.
tests.threshold: :f2f_window_days = 180 is a generous starting window; the applicable requirement is six months for many items but read it off the current rule for the item category rather than adopting a single value. Two structural caveats. Claims-based inference understates the encounter footprint: care delivered under another payer, in a facility bundled payment, or by a covered non-billing encounter leaves no trace, so NO_ENCOUNTER_AT_ALL is not proof of no encounter. And TELEHEALTH_ONLY is not itself improper — telehealth satisfies the face-to-face requirement for many items — which is why it is separated rather than flagged: it is the population test 3 examines more closely, not a finding on its own. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-04 (Face-to-face encounter & Written Order Prior to Delivery verification for applicable DMEPOS). Secondary: CD-08 (Valid-order verification), PI-20 (Provider NPI/credential-footprint consistency monitoring).

failure_map.reading: No face-to-face or WOPD verification operates. PA-04's F2F note + WOPD on file artifact does not exist.
PA-04 is per-order; a population of delivered items has no corresponding verification record.
Items were delivered on a supplier-prepared order form signed after the fact, with the face-to-face requirement treated as a formality.

Verification confirms a face-to-face note exists in the file without testing whether the signing clinician had any relationship with the beneficiary — which is precisely what a generated order is built to satisfy.
Encounters occurred but no retained F2F documentation ties them to the order.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Ordering-provider fan-out across unrelated suppliers
tests.hypothesis: A clinician selling signatures produces a signature pattern no clinical practice produces: very high order volume, spread across many unrelated suppliers, for beneficiaries concentrated in geographies the clinician has no presence in. Where footprint monitoring is absent, each individual order looks ordinary and only the aggregate is diagnostic. This is the Gold Rush structure.
tests.check: For each ordering provider on DMEPOS claims, count orders, distinct beneficiaries, distinct suppliers and distinct beneficiary states, and compute the share of orders with no encounter footprint. Rank by supplier fan-out and geographic spread rather than by volume alone.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 2 - Ordering-provider fan-out and geographic spread on DMEPOS
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_orders (50), :supplier_fanout_cut (5), :f2f_window_days (180)

WITH orders AS (
  SELECT
      d.ordering_npi, d.billing_npi AS supplier_npi, d.beneficiary_id,
      d.claim_line_id, d.service_date, d.paid_amount,
      b.state_code AS beneficiary_state,
      CASE WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM claim_lines e
        WHERE e.beneficiary_id = d.beneficiary_id
          AND e.rendering_npi  = d.ordering_npi
          AND e.claim_type IN ('PROFESSIONAL','TELEHEALTH')
          AND e.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
          AND e.service_date BETWEEN d.service_date - :f2f_window_days AND d.service_date
      ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_encounter
  FROM claim_lines d
  JOIN beneficiary b ON b.beneficiary_id = d.beneficiary_id
  WHERE d.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND d.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND d.claim_type = 'DMEPOS'
    AND d.ordering_npi IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    o.ordering_npi, pr.specialty, pr.practice_state,
    COUNT(*)                                   AS orders,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.beneficiary_id)           AS beneficiaries,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.supplier_npi)             AS distinct_suppliers,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.beneficiary_state)        AS distinct_beneficiary_states,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.beneficiary_state <> pr.practice_state THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0
      / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)                    AS out_of_state_share,
    ROUND(1 - AVG(o.has_encounter), 3)         AS no_encounter_share,
    SUM(o.paid_amount)                         AS ordered_paid,
    ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT o.service_date), 0), 1) AS orders_per_active_day
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN provider pr ON pr.npi = o.ordering_npi
GROUP BY o.ordering_npi, pr.specialty, pr.practice_state
HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_orders
   AND COUNT(DISTINCT o.supplier_npi) >= :supplier_fanout_cut
ORDER BY no_encounter_share DESC, ordered_paid DESC;

-- The conjunction is the signal, not any single column: high supplier fan-out AND high
-- out-of-state share AND high no-encounter share AND high orders-per-active-day. Any one
-- alone has ordinary explanations; all four together do not.
tests.threshold: :min_orders = 50 and :supplier_fanout_cut = 5 distinct suppliers are starting cuts. Read the four signal columns together rather than thresholding any one: a hospitalist orders for many suppliers, a telehealth practice legitimately serves many states, and a busy practice has high orders-per-day. What no ordinary practice produces is all four at once alongside a no-encounter share near 1.0. `orders_per_active_day` is the most under-appreciated column — a clinician signing hundreds of orders on a handful of days is describing a batch-signing workflow, not a clinical one. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PI-20 (Provider NPI/credential-footprint consistency monitoring). Secondary: PE-15 (New-provider billing-velocity watch), PI-03 (Multi-source link analysis).

failure_map.reading: No ordering-provider footprint monitoring. PI-20's alert log does not cover the ordering role.
PI-20 is continuous; no alerts covering DMEPOS ordering were produced.
Fan-out was identified and no review, education or ordering-privilege action followed.
The monitor evaluates billing and rendering NPIs only and never the ordering NPI, so the party generating the demand is outside its scope entirely.
Alerts fire with no retained disposition.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Telehealth contact immediately preceding an order, with no other relationship
tests.hypothesis: Telehealth satisfies the face-to-face requirement for many items, which is exactly why order-generation schemes route through it. Where the service-modality documentation control is absent, the pattern is a single brief telehealth contact on or within a day or two of the order, from a clinician with no prior or subsequent relationship with the beneficiary, followed immediately by a high-value item.
tests.check: Identify DMEPOS orders whose only qualifying encounter is a telehealth contact within a short window before the order, and test whether that clinician has any other relationship with the beneficiary before or after. Report the encounter's billed level as a proxy for its substance.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 3 - Telehealth-originated orders with no surrounding relationship
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :proximity_days (7), :relationship_window_days (365)

WITH tele_originated AS (
  SELECT
      d.claim_line_id, d.beneficiary_id, d.ordering_npi, d.billing_npi AS supplier_npi,
      d.hcpcs, d.service_date AS order_service_date, d.paid_amount,
      t.claim_line_id AS telehealth_line_id,
      t.service_date  AS telehealth_date,
      t.cpt           AS telehealth_cpt,
      t.paid_amount   AS telehealth_paid,
      (d.service_date - t.service_date) AS days_order_after_contact
  FROM claim_lines d
  JOIN claim_lines t
    ON  t.beneficiary_id = d.beneficiary_id
    AND t.rendering_npi  = d.ordering_npi
    AND t.place_of_service IN ('02','10')
    AND t.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND t.service_date BETWEEN d.service_date - :proximity_days AND d.service_date
  WHERE d.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND d.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND d.claim_type = 'DMEPOS'
)
SELECT
    tо.*,
    -- any other contact with this clinician, before or after, of any modality
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM claim_lines o
      WHERE o.beneficiary_id  = tо.beneficiary_id
        AND o.rendering_npi   = tо.ordering_npi
        AND o.claim_line_id  <> tо.telehealth_line_id
        AND o.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
        AND o.service_date BETWEEN tо.order_service_date - :relationship_window_days
                               AND tо.order_service_date + :relationship_window_days)
      AS other_contacts_with_clinician,
    CASE WHEN tо.telehealth_cpt IN ('99202','99211','99212') THEN 'LOW_LEVEL_CONTACT'
         ELSE 'HIGHER_LEVEL_CONTACT' END AS contact_substance
FROM tele_originated tо
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM claim_lines o
    WHERE o.beneficiary_id  = tо.beneficiary_id
      AND o.rendering_npi   = tо.ordering_npi
      AND o.claim_line_id  <> tо.telehealth_line_id
      AND o.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
      AND o.service_date BETWEEN tо.order_service_date - :relationship_window_days
                             AND tо.order_service_date + :relationship_window_days)
ORDER BY tо.paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: :proximity_days = 7 and :relationship_window_days = 365. Be careful with the framing here, because the pattern this test describes is also what legitimate specialist telehealth consultation looks like: a patient is referred, seen once remotely, an appropriate item is ordered, and the relationship ends. That is good care, not fraud. The discriminating factors are volume at the *clinician* level (test 2), the value of the item relative to the substance of the contact, and whether the beneficiary was solicited — which claims data cannot show at all. Treat individual rows as context for a clinician-level review, never as findings in themselves. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CD-18 (Service-modality documentation control — note and claim modifier support the billed modality). Secondary: PA-04 (Face-to-face encounter & WOPD verification), CD-03 (Reasonable-and-necessary documentation).

failure_map.reading: No modality documentation control operates. CD-18's modality-supporting note + modifier artifact does not exist.
CD-18 is per-service; a population of telehealth encounters behind DMEPOS orders has no modality documentation.
Modality was recorded correctly and no one asked whether the encounter supported the order that followed it.
The control tests that the modifier matches the place of service, which a scripted telehealth contact satisfies perfectly — it says nothing about clinical substance.
No retained note evidencing what occurred in the encounter.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Delivery before the written order — WOPD sequence failure
tests.hypothesis: For applicable items the written order must precede delivery. Where valid-order verification is absent or checks only that an order exists, items are delivered first and the order is papered afterward — a sequence failure that is invisible to any control that looks only for the presence of a document.
tests.check: Compare the order signature date to the delivery date for every item subject to the written-order-prior-to-delivery requirement, and report deliveries preceding signature, orders with no signature date, and orders signed by a provider who was not active on the signature date.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 4 - Written order date versus delivery date
-- 42 CFR 410.32; 42 CFR 410.38. Params: :period_start, :period_end
-- Needs provider.enrollment_end_date (or an enrollment history): provider status is judged on the
-- signature date, not today.

SELECT
    d.claim_line_id, d.beneficiary_id, d.billing_npi AS supplier_npi,
    d.ordering_npi, d.hcpcs, d.paid_amount,
    o.order_id, o.signature_date, o.order_received_date,
    pod.delivery_date,
    (pod.delivery_date - o.signature_date) AS days_signature_to_delivery,
    p.enrollment_status AS ordering_provider_status,
    CASE
      WHEN o.order_id IS NULL                        THEN 'NO_ORDER_RECORD'
      WHEN o.signature_date IS NULL                  THEN 'ORDER_UNSIGNED'
      WHEN pod.delivery_date IS NULL                 THEN 'NO_DELIVERY_RECORD'
      WHEN pod.delivery_date < o.signature_date      THEN 'DELIVERED_BEFORE_ORDER_SIGNED'
      -- death first: the cleanest signal, and it must not be shadowed by the not-active label
      WHEN p.date_of_death IS NOT NULL
           AND o.signature_date > p.date_of_death    THEN 'SIGNED_AFTER_PROVIDER_DEATH'
      -- status on the signature date, not today's status: use the enrollment end date when held
      WHEN (p.enrollment_end_date IS NOT NULL AND o.signature_date > p.enrollment_end_date)
        OR (p.enrollment_end_date IS NULL AND p.enrollment_status <> 'ACTIVE')
                                                     THEN 'ORDERING_PROVIDER_NOT_ACTIVE'
    END AS wopd_defect
FROM claim_lines d
JOIN wopd_required_item w ON w.hcpcs = d.hcpcs
                         AND d.service_date BETWEEN w.effective_date
                                                AND COALESCE(w.termination_date, DATE '9999-12-31')
LEFT JOIN dme_order o        ON o.claim_id = d.claim_id
LEFT JOIN proof_of_delivery pod ON pod.claim_id = d.claim_id
LEFT JOIN provider p         ON p.npi = d.ordering_npi
WHERE d.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND d.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND d.claim_type = 'DMEPOS'
  AND (o.order_id IS NULL
       OR o.signature_date IS NULL
       OR pod.delivery_date IS NULL
       OR pod.delivery_date < o.signature_date
       OR (p.enrollment_end_date IS NOT NULL AND o.signature_date > p.enrollment_end_date)
       OR (p.enrollment_end_date IS NULL AND p.enrollment_status <> 'ACTIVE')
       OR (p.date_of_death IS NOT NULL AND o.signature_date > p.date_of_death))
ORDER BY wopd_defect, d.paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: Categorical throughout — dates are either in sequence or they are not. Two practical notes. NO_ORDER_RECORD and NO_DELIVERY_RECORD will usually reflect documents held by the supplier and not surfaced in the payer's systems, so establish your document-capture completeness before treating them as findings; they are more often an evidence-availability question than a compliance one. SIGNED_AFTER_PROVIDER_DEATH is low-volume and near-conclusive, and should be worked first regardless of dollar value — it is the single cleanest signal in this family. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CD-08 (Valid-order verification — signed order on file before the service, source-verified ordering-provider identity). Secondary: PA-04 (Face-to-face & WOPD verification), CD-09 (Proof-of-delivery capture and retention).

failure_map.reading: No order verification before delivery. CD-08's signed-order artifact does not exist for this category.
CD-08 is per-service; a population of delivered items has no verification record.
Delivery proceeded on a verbal or pending order and the written order was obtained afterward.
The check confirms an order document exists without comparing its signature date to the delivery date — presence, not sequence, which is the whole requirement.
Orders exist at the supplier but are not retrievable within the retention requirement.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Prior authorisation affirmed but no UTN linked to the claim
tests.hypothesis: Where the unique tracking number is not captured and linked, claims bill without an affirmed prior authorisation — or, just as importantly, with a UTN belonging to a different item, beneficiary or date. PA-05's stated failure mode is 'billing without an affirmed PA', and the linkage is the control.
tests.check: For claims in PA-required categories, test that a UTN is present, that it resolves to a real affirmation, and that the affirmation matches on beneficiary, HCPCS and date range. Report each mismatch class separately.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 5 - UTN presence and affirmation linkage integrity
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

SELECT
    d.claim_line_id, d.beneficiary_id, d.billing_npi AS supplier_npi,
    d.hcpcs, d.service_date, d.paid_amount,
    d.utn,
    a.affirmation_id, a.decision, a.decision_date,
    a.beneficiary_id AS affirmed_beneficiary, a.hcpcs AS affirmed_hcpcs,
    a.valid_from, a.valid_to,
    CASE
      WHEN d.utn IS NULL                             THEN 'NO_UTN_ON_CLAIM'
      WHEN a.affirmation_id IS NULL                  THEN 'UTN_DOES_NOT_RESOLVE'
      WHEN a.decision <> 'AFFIRMED'                  THEN 'UTN_RESOLVES_TO_NON_AFFIRMATION'
      WHEN a.beneficiary_id <> d.beneficiary_id      THEN 'UTN_BENEFICIARY_MISMATCH'
      WHEN a.hcpcs <> d.hcpcs                        THEN 'UTN_ITEM_MISMATCH'
      WHEN d.service_date NOT BETWEEN a.valid_from AND a.valid_to
                                                     THEN 'UTN_OUTSIDE_VALIDITY_WINDOW'
    END AS utn_defect
FROM claim_lines d
JOIN pa_required_item pr
  ON  pr.hcpcs = d.hcpcs
  AND d.service_date BETWEEN pr.effective_date
                         AND COALESCE(pr.termination_date, DATE '9999-12-31')
LEFT JOIN pa_affirmation a ON a.utn = d.utn
WHERE d.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND d.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND (d.utn IS NULL
       OR a.affirmation_id IS NULL
       OR a.decision <> 'AFFIRMED'
       OR a.beneficiary_id <> d.beneficiary_id
       OR a.hcpcs <> d.hcpcs
       OR d.service_date NOT BETWEEN a.valid_from AND a.valid_to)
ORDER BY utn_defect, d.paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: Categorical against the PA-required item list, and that list's currency is the dependency — see test 7. The mismatch classes are worth keeping separate because they mean different things: NO_UTN_ON_CLAIM is usually a billing-configuration failure, UTN_BENEFICIARY_MISMATCH and UTN_ITEM_MISMATCH suggest a UTN reused across claims, and UTN_RESOLVES_TO_NON_AFFIRMATION means a non-affirmed request was billed anyway. The reuse classes are small in volume and high in significance. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-05 (Affirmation/UTN capture & claim linkage). Secondary: PA-01 (Prospective PA-scoping check), PA-18 (Proof-of-delivery / service-vs-affirmation post-payment match).

failure_map.reading: No UTN capture or linkage. PA-05's 'UTN present on claim' evidence does not exist.
The linkage is specified per claim; a population of PA-required claims carries no UTN.
Claims without a UTN were released to billing to avoid a hold.
The control checks that a UTN field is populated but never validates it against the affirmation record, so a reused or fabricated number passes.
Affirmations were obtained but no retained linkage evidences which claim they belong to.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Item on the Required PA List furnished with no prior authorisation at all
tests.hypothesis: The prospective scoping check exists to catch, before delivery, that an item requires prior authorisation. Where it is absent, items are furnished and billed with no PA request ever submitted — not a mismatched UTN but no request in the system at all. PA-01's failure mode names the consequence: furnishing a listed item without required PA, which auto-denies.
tests.check: For each paid claim in a PA-required category, test whether any PA request exists for that beneficiary and item in the applicable window, regardless of outcome. Report by supplier, since a scoping failure is an operational pattern.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 6 - PA-required items with no PA request of any kind
-- 42 CFR 414.234. Params: :period_start, :period_end, :request_window_days (180)

WITH pa_required_claims AS (
  SELECT d.claim_line_id, d.claim_id, d.beneficiary_id, d.billing_npi AS supplier_npi,
         d.hcpcs, d.service_date, d.paid_amount, pr.list_name, pr.added_to_list_date
  FROM claim_lines d
  JOIN pa_required_item pr
    ON  pr.hcpcs = d.hcpcs
    AND d.service_date BETWEEN pr.effective_date
                           AND COALESCE(pr.termination_date, DATE '9999-12-31')
  WHERE d.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND d.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
)
SELECT
    c.supplier_npi,
    COUNT(*)                          AS claims_without_any_pa,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.hcpcs)           AS distinct_items,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.beneficiary_id)  AS beneficiaries,
    SUM(c.paid_amount)                AS paid_amount,
    MIN(c.service_date)               AS earliest,
    MAX(c.service_date)               AS latest,
    -- how much of the supplier's PA-required volume this represents
    ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / NULLIF(
      (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pa_required_claims x WHERE x.supplier_npi = c.supplier_npi), 0), 3)
      AS share_of_pa_required_volume
FROM pa_required_claims c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pa_request r
    WHERE r.beneficiary_id = c.beneficiary_id
      AND r.hcpcs          = c.hcpcs
      AND r.request_date BETWEEN c.service_date - :request_window_days AND c.service_date
)
GROUP BY c.supplier_npi
ORDER BY paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: Categorical. The `share_of_pa_required_volume` column is what distinguishes an operational gap from an isolated miss — a supplier at 2% has a process with holes, one at 60% does not have a process. Two exclusions to build first: emergency and expedited furnishing pathways that permit delivery before authorisation, and items recently added to the list where a transition period applies (test 7 covers the list-currency side of that). Without them the newest list additions will dominate and misattribute a governance lag as a supplier failure. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-01 (Prospective PA-scoping check against the current DMEPOS Required PA List and OPD PA list before delivery). Secondary: PA-02 (Required PA List update governance), PA-05 (Affirmation/UTN capture & claim linkage).

failure_map.reading: No scoping check before delivery. PA-01's PA-applicability determination does not exist.
PA-01 is per-order; a population of orders for listed items has no applicability determination.
The item was identified as PA-required and furnished anyway, ahead of a decision.
The check runs against a stale item master, so newly listed items are never identified as requiring PA — the failure belongs upstream to PA-02.
Determinations were made but no retained record shows which orders were scoped.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Required PA List currency — newly listed items still paying without authorisation
tests.hypothesis: The Required PA List and Master List change through the Federal Register and the CMS PA site. Where update governance is absent, the item master goes stale and newly listed items continue to pay unauthorised. This is the upstream cause of most of test 6's volume, and distinguishing the two is the point of running both.
tests.check: For each item added to the list during or before the period, measure the interval between the list effective date and the date your item master reflected it, and quantify the claims paid without PA inside that lag.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 7 - Item-master lag behind the published Required PA List
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

WITH list_changes AS (
  SELECT pl.hcpcs, pl.list_name, pl.published_date, pl.effective_date,
         im.item_master_updated_date
  FROM published_pa_list pl
  LEFT JOIN item_master_pa_flag im
         ON im.hcpcs = pl.hcpcs AND im.list_name = pl.list_name
  WHERE pl.effective_date BETWEEN :period_start - 730 AND :period_end
)
SELECT
    lc.hcpcs, lc.list_name, lc.published_date, lc.effective_date,
    lc.item_master_updated_date,
    CASE WHEN lc.item_master_updated_date IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE lc.item_master_updated_date - lc.effective_date END AS update_lag_days,
    CASE
      WHEN lc.item_master_updated_date IS NULL                    THEN 'NEVER_UPDATED'
      WHEN lc.item_master_updated_date > lc.effective_date        THEN 'UPDATED_LATE'
      ELSE 'TIMELY'
    END AS governance_status,
    -- exposure inside the lag: paid claims for the item with no PA request
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cl.paid_amount), 0)
       FROM claim_lines cl
      WHERE cl.hcpcs = lc.hcpcs
        AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
        AND cl.service_date >= lc.effective_date
        AND cl.service_date <  COALESCE(lc.item_master_updated_date, CURRENT_DATE)
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pa_request r
                        WHERE r.beneficiary_id = cl.beneficiary_id
                          AND r.hcpcs = cl.hcpcs)) AS paid_unauthorised_in_lag
FROM list_changes lc
WHERE lc.item_master_updated_date IS NULL
   OR lc.item_master_updated_date > lc.effective_date
ORDER BY paid_unauthorised_in_lag DESC;
tests.threshold: No threshold — the lag is a measured number and the exposure inside it is a measured dollar amount. This output is a governance finding by construction and belongs to compliance and coding, not to any supplier's review queue. Note the published date and effective date are different things and both matter: a list published with thirty days' notice and updated on day thirty-one is a different control posture from one published with six months' notice and updated late anyway. Read `published_date` alongside the lag before characterising the failure. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-02 (Master List / Required PA List update governance — monitor annual Federal Register + CMS PA site, refresh item-to-HCPCS mapping). Secondary: PA-01 (Prospective PA-scoping check), CB-17 (Prepayment edit maintenance & tuning).

failure_map.reading: No list monitoring. PA-02's list-version change log does not exist.
PA-02 is quarterly; the change log shows no entry against a published list update.
The update was identified and the item-master change was deferred.
Monitoring covers the annual Federal Register notice but not interim CMS PA-site updates, so mid-year additions are missed.
Updates occurred but no dated change log records what changed and when.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Proof of delivery absent or inconsistent with the affirmation
tests.hypothesis: An affirmed prior authorisation says an item may be furnished; proof of delivery says it was. Where the post-payment match between the two is absent, claims pay for items never delivered, or for items different from those authorised. PA-18 exists specifically to reconcile these two records and its failure mode names both cases.
tests.check: Reconcile paid DMEPOS claims to proof-of-delivery records and to the affirmation, testing existence, completeness of required POD elements, and agreement on item, beneficiary and date.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 8 - POD existence, completeness and agreement with the affirmation
-- Program Integrity Manual Pub 100-08 Ch.5; 42 CFR 410.38.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :pod_tolerance_days (2)

SELECT
    d.claim_line_id, d.beneficiary_id, d.billing_npi AS supplier_npi,
    d.hcpcs, d.service_date, d.paid_amount, d.utn,
    pod.pod_id, pod.delivery_date, pod.delivery_method,
    pod.recipient_signature_present, pod.item_description_present,
    pod.quantity_present, pod.delivery_address_present,
    a.hcpcs AS affirmed_hcpcs, a.quantity AS affirmed_quantity,
    CASE
      WHEN pod.pod_id IS NULL                                THEN 'NO_POD'
      WHEN pod.recipient_signature_present = FALSE
        OR pod.item_description_present   = FALSE
        OR pod.quantity_present           = FALSE
        OR pod.delivery_address_present   = FALSE            THEN 'POD_INCOMPLETE'
      WHEN a.affirmation_id IS NOT NULL AND a.hcpcs <> d.hcpcs
                                                             THEN 'ITEM_DIFFERS_FROM_AFFIRMATION'
      WHEN a.affirmation_id IS NOT NULL AND d.units > a.quantity
                                                             THEN 'QUANTITY_EXCEEDS_AFFIRMATION'
      WHEN pod.delivery_date > d.service_date + :pod_tolerance_days
        OR pod.delivery_date < d.service_date - :pod_tolerance_days
                                                             THEN 'DELIVERY_DATE_MISMATCH'
    END AS pod_defect
FROM claim_lines d
LEFT JOIN proof_of_delivery pod ON pod.claim_id = d.claim_id
LEFT JOIN pa_affirmation a      ON a.utn = d.utn
WHERE d.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND d.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND d.claim_type = 'DMEPOS'
  AND (pod.pod_id IS NULL
       OR pod.recipient_signature_present = FALSE
       OR pod.item_description_present   = FALSE
       OR pod.quantity_present           = FALSE
       OR pod.delivery_address_present   = FALSE
       OR (a.affirmation_id IS NOT NULL AND (a.hcpcs <> d.hcpcs OR d.units > a.quantity))
       OR ABS(pod.delivery_date - d.service_date) > :pod_tolerance_days)
ORDER BY pod_defect, d.paid_amount DESC;
tests.threshold: :pod_tolerance_days = 2 absorbs the ordinary gap between a shipment date and the billed date of service; shipping-based delivery legitimately spans several days, so set the tolerance by delivery method rather than globally. The NO_POD class depends entirely on whether the payer holds POD records at all — most do not outside an audit, in which case PA-18's monthly post-payment sample is the mechanism and this query describes what that sample should test rather than something you can run across the whole population. ITEM_DIFFERS_FROM_AFFIRMATION is the highest-value class and is testable without POD data. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-18 (Proof-of-delivery / service-vs-affirmation post-payment match). Secondary: CD-09 (Proof-of-delivery capture and retention with all required elements), PA-05 (Affirmation/UTN capture & claim linkage).

failure_map.reading: No post-payment POD-to-PA reconciliation. PA-18's reconciliation artifact does not exist.
PA-18 is monthly; no sample was drawn or reconciled in the period.
Mismatches were identified and no recovery or supplier action followed.
The match confirms a POD document exists without testing its required elements or its agreement with the affirmation.
Reconciliation performed with no retained workpaper showing which claims were matched.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Rental continuation and repairs without current documented medical need
tests.hypothesis: Rentals continue and repairs are billed on the strength of a need documented once, sometimes years earlier. Where continued-medical-necessity re-documentation is absent, monthly rental and repair claims accumulate with no current record — the OIG power-mobility-device repair finding PA-07 cites is the reference case.
tests.check: For each rental month and each repair claim, compute time since the most recent continued-need documentation and flag those beyond the applicable interval. Quantify the paid amount inside the lapsed window, which is the exposure figure.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 9 - Rental months and repairs beyond the continued-need interval
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :cmn_interval_days (365)

WITH rental_and_repair AS (
  SELECT d.claim_line_id, d.beneficiary_id, d.billing_npi AS supplier_npi,
         d.hcpcs, d.service_date, d.paid_amount,
         CASE WHEN d.modifier_1 IN ('RR') OR d.modifier_2 IN ('RR') THEN 'RENTAL'
              WHEN d.modifier_1 IN ('RB','RP') OR d.modifier_2 IN ('RB','RP') THEN 'REPAIR'
              ELSE 'OTHER' END AS claim_nature
  FROM claim_lines d
  WHERE d.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND d.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND d.claim_type = 'DMEPOS'
),
claim_cmn AS (
  -- the latest document ON OR BEFORE each claim's service date, so a later re-documentation
  -- does not make an earlier, validly documented month look undocumented
  SELECT r.*, ec.equipment_category,
         (SELECT MAX(c.documented_date)
            FROM continued_need_document c
           WHERE c.beneficiary_id     = r.beneficiary_id
             AND c.equipment_category = ec.equipment_category
             AND c.documented_date   <= r.service_date) AS last_documented
  FROM rental_and_repair r
  JOIN equipment_category_map ec ON ec.hcpcs = r.hcpcs
  WHERE r.claim_nature IN ('RENTAL','REPAIR')
)
SELECT
    r.claim_line_id, r.beneficiary_id, r.supplier_npi, r.hcpcs,
    r.claim_nature, r.service_date, r.paid_amount,
    r.last_documented,
    CASE WHEN r.last_documented IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE r.service_date - r.last_documented END AS days_since_documented,
    CASE WHEN r.last_documented IS NULL THEN 'NO_CONTINUED_NEED_RECORD'
         ELSE 'STALE_CONTINUED_NEED' END AS cmn_defect
FROM claim_cmn r
WHERE r.last_documented IS NULL
   OR r.service_date - r.last_documented > :cmn_interval_days
ORDER BY r.paid_amount DESC;

-- Roll up by supplier and by beneficiary. Exposure = SUM(paid_amount) in the lapsed
-- window, which is the figure that belongs in a report; individual months are small.
tests.threshold: :cmn_interval_days = 365 reflects the twelve-month power-mobility interval PA-07 names, but intervals differ by equipment category and by payer policy — set it per category from your own coverage rules rather than globally. The modifier-based identification of rentals and repairs is approximate: modifier usage varies and some suppliers bill repairs without RB/RP, so validate the classification against a sample before trusting the counts. NO_CONTINUED_NEED_RECORD will usually reflect documentation held clinically and not surfaced to the payer, which makes this an evidence-retrieval finding as much as a coverage one. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-07 (Continued-medical-necessity re-documentation for rentals/repairs within the required timeframe). Secondary: CD-10 (Continued-need / recertification documentation control), CD-03 (Reasonable-and-necessary documentation).

failure_map.reading: No continued-need re-documentation operates. PA-07's timely continued-need record does not exist.
PA-07 is per-event; rentals continued and repairs were billed with no re-documentation.
Re-documentation was produced as a form renewal with no reassessment of need.
Documentation is tracked in the supplier's system and never blocks or flags a claim, so a lapse carries no payment consequence.
Reassessments occurred but the record is not retained or retrievable.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Capped-rental cap exceeded — rental payments beyond the purchase transition
tests.hypothesis: Capped rental items transition to ownership after a defined number of rental months, after which continued rental billing is not payable. Where quantity and frequency edits do not track cumulative rental months per beneficiary per item, rental billing continues past the cap — and because each month is individually small and individually valid, nothing fires.
tests.check: Accumulate rental months per beneficiary per equipment item across the whole history, not just the reporting period, and flag months beyond the applicable cap. Report cumulative rental paid against the item's purchase price as a second view.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 10 - Rental months beyond the capped-rental limit
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :default_rental_cap_months (13)

WITH rental_months AS (
  SELECT
      d.beneficiary_id, ec.equipment_category, d.hcpcs, d.billing_npi AS supplier_npi,
      DATE_TRUNC('month', d.service_date) AS rental_month,
      SUM(d.paid_amount) AS month_paid
  FROM claim_lines d
  JOIN equipment_category_map ec ON ec.hcpcs = d.hcpcs
  WHERE d.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
    AND d.claim_type = 'DMEPOS'
    AND (d.modifier_1 = 'RR' OR d.modifier_2 = 'RR')
  GROUP BY d.beneficiary_id, ec.equipment_category, d.hcpcs, d.billing_npi,
           DATE_TRUNC('month', d.service_date)
),
sequenced AS (
  SELECT
      rm.*,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY beneficiary_id, equipment_category
                         ORDER BY rental_month) AS rental_month_number,
      SUM(month_paid) OVER (PARTITION BY beneficiary_id, equipment_category
                            ORDER BY rental_month) AS cumulative_rental_paid
  FROM rental_months rm
)
SELECT
    s.beneficiary_id, s.equipment_category, s.hcpcs, s.supplier_npi,
    s.rental_month, s.rental_month_number,
    COALESCE(cap.cap_months, :default_rental_cap_months) AS cap_months,
    s.month_paid, s.cumulative_rental_paid,
    fs.purchase_price,
    ROUND(s.cumulative_rental_paid / NULLIF(fs.purchase_price, 0), 2) AS rental_to_purchase_ratio
FROM sequenced s
LEFT JOIN rental_cap_reference cap ON cap.equipment_category = s.equipment_category
LEFT JOIN fee_schedule fs          ON fs.hcpcs = s.hcpcs
WHERE s.rental_month BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND s.rental_month_number > COALESCE(cap.cap_months, :default_rental_cap_months)
ORDER BY s.cumulative_rental_paid DESC;

-- rental_to_purchase_ratio > 1.0 means the payer has rented an item for more than it
-- would have cost to buy. That is a payment-policy conversation as much as a compliance
-- one, and it is a persuasive number to put in front of governance.
tests.threshold: :default_rental_cap_months = 13 reflects the common capped-rental period, but caps differ by item category and by payer, so drive them from a reference table. The critical implementation point is that the rental-month count must accumulate across the beneficiary's entire history and across suppliers — a beneficiary who changes supplier mid-rental will otherwise restart the count, which is exactly how caps are defeated in practice. Confirm your identification of rental claims before trusting the sequence; the RR modifier is the usual marker but not a universal one. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-08 (Quantity / frequency-limit edits — capped & time-based services). Secondary: CB-07 (MUE units-of-service edit enforcement), PA-07 (Continued-medical-necessity re-documentation for rentals/repairs).

failure_map.reading: No cumulative rental tracking. CB-08's frequency-limit exception report does not cover capped rentals.
The edit exists but produced no exceptions in the period.
Cap exceptions were overridden at adjudication without establishing the rental history.
The count resets on a change of supplier or a change of HCPCS within the same equipment category, so the cap is trivially defeated.
No retained exception log for cap hits.

tests.family_title: DMEPOS and telemedicine — the order-to-encounter gap
tests.name: Resupply before the item's reasonable useful lifetime
tests.hypothesis: Durable items carry a reasonable useful lifetime before replacement is payable, and consumable supplies carry expected utilisation rates. Where the continued-need and recertification control does not test replacement timing, items are replaced early and supplies are shipped faster than they can be used — the auto-ship pattern, where resupply is driven by a shipping schedule rather than by need.
tests.check: For durable items, flag replacements inside the reasonable useful lifetime with no documented loss, theft or irreparable damage. For consumables, compute the shipment interval against expected utilisation and flag suppliers whose resupply cadence systematically outruns it.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 11 - Early replacement and accelerated resupply
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end

-- 11a: durable item replaced inside its reasonable useful lifetime
SELECT
    'EARLY_REPLACEMENT' AS finding,
    new.claim_line_id, new.beneficiary_id, new.billing_npi AS supplier_npi,
    new.hcpcs, new.service_date, new.paid_amount,
    prior.service_date AS prior_supply_date,
    (new.service_date - prior.service_date) AS days_since_prior,
    rul.rul_months * 30 AS rul_days
FROM claim_lines new
JOIN equipment_category_map ec ON ec.hcpcs = new.hcpcs
JOIN reasonable_useful_life rul ON rul.equipment_category = ec.equipment_category
JOIN claim_lines prior
  ON  prior.beneficiary_id = new.beneficiary_id
  AND prior.hcpcs          = new.hcpcs
  AND prior.service_date   < new.service_date
  AND prior.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
WHERE new.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  AND new.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
  AND (new.service_date - prior.service_date) < rul.rul_months * 30
  -- exclude documented loss / theft / irreparable damage replacements
  AND COALESCE(new.modifier_1,'') NOT IN ('RA') AND COALESCE(new.modifier_2,'') NOT IN ('RA')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM replacement_justification j
                  WHERE j.claim_id = new.claim_id)

UNION ALL

-- 11b: consumable resupply faster than expected utilisation. The previous supply date is
-- looked up over a year before the period so the first in-period claim has a prior; only gaps
-- shorter than the expected supply interval are returned. Lines are first collapsed to one
-- row per beneficiary, code and service date: two lines for the same code on the same day
-- are one supply event, not a resupply after zero days.
SELECT
    'ACCELERATED_RESUPPLY',
    x.claim_line_id, x.beneficiary_id, x.billing_npi,
    x.hcpcs, x.service_date, x.paid_amount,
    x.prior_date,
    x.service_date - x.prior_date,
    x.expected_supply_days
FROM (
  SELECT d.*,
         LAG(d.service_date) OVER (PARTITION BY d.beneficiary_id, d.hcpcs
