tests.pair: PA-11 (Decision-timeliness SLA control). Secondary: PA-17 (PA metrics reporting), PA-12 (Specific denial-reason communication + electronic PA).

failure_map.reading: No SLA timer exists on the PA workflow, so elapsed time cannot be computed from the system of record at all.
PA-11 specifies continuous SLA monitoring; no timeliness report was produced for the period.

The clock is restarted by issuing a documentation request, and requests are issued routinely rather than because the package is incomplete. Check the rate of documentation requests against the incompleteness the package actually shows.
The report is computed over closed cases only, so requests that were never decided — the worst outcome for the beneficiary — are structurally invisible to it.
Decision timestamps are overwritten on status change rather than appended, so elapsed time cannot be reconstructed for any closed case.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: Denial notices that cannot be appealed — reason specificity and channel
tests.hypothesis: A denial communicated with a generic reason code is functionally unappealable: the requester cannot tell what to correct or what evidence to add. Where the specific-denial-reason control is absent, denial-reason distributions collapse onto a handful of catch-all codes, and appeal rates on those codes fall — not because the denials are correct, but because nobody can construct an appeal against them.
tests.check: Rank denial-reason codes by volume and compute, per code, the appeal rate and the overturn rate on appeal. A high-volume code with a low appeal rate and a high overturn rate among the few that are appealed is the specific signature: the denials are wrong and the notice is preventing challenge. Report electronic-PA channel adoption alongside it, because a notice that never reaches the requester's system is the same failure.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 5 - Denial-reason specificity and appealability
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_denials (50)

WITH denials AS (
  SELECT d.pa_request_id, d.denial_reason_code, d.denial_reason_text,
         d.notice_channel,              -- 'FHIR_API' | 'PORTAL' | 'FAX' | 'MAIL'
         d.decision_datetime, d.requesting_npi
  FROM pa_decision d
  WHERE d.decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED'
    AND d.decision_datetime BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
),
appeals AS (
  SELECT a.pa_request_id,
         MAX(CASE WHEN a.appeal_outcome = 'OVERTURNED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS overturned,
         COUNT(*) AS appeal_levels
  FROM pa_appeal a
  GROUP BY a.pa_request_id
)
SELECT
    d.denial_reason_code,
    MIN(d.denial_reason_text)                        AS example_text,
    LENGTH(MIN(d.denial_reason_text))                AS reason_text_length,
    COUNT(*)                                         AS denials,
    COUNT(DISTINCT d.requesting_npi)                 AS distinct_requesters,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ap.pa_request_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS appealed,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ap.pa_request_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)
          / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 4)                  AS appeal_rate,
    ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(ap.overturned, 0)) * 1.0
          / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN ap.pa_request_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0), 4)
                                                     AS overturn_rate_when_appealed,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN d.notice_channel = 'FHIR_API' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)
          / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 4)                  AS electronic_notice_share
FROM denials d
LEFT JOIN appeals ap ON ap.pa_request_id = d.pa_request_id
GROUP BY d.denial_reason_code
HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_denials
ORDER BY denials DESC;

-- The cell to read first: a high-volume code with a LOW appeal_rate and a HIGH
-- overturn_rate_when_appealed. That combination means the few requesters who did
-- appeal usually won, and the rest could not tell what to argue.
tests.threshold: No absolute threshold applies — the metric is comparative across your own reason codes. The pattern to escalate is a code in the top decile by volume whose appeal rate sits in the bottom quartile and whose overturn rate when appealed sits in the top quartile. reason_text_length is a crude but useful proxy for specificity and costs nothing to compute: a modal reason text under about 80 characters across thousands of denials is almost certainly a template. Low electronic_notice_share is a finding in its own right where the electronic-PA requirement binds. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-12 (Specific denial-reason communication + electronic PA / FHIR API where required). Secondary: PA-11 (Decision-timeliness SLA), PA-14 (PA denial-appropriateness sampling).

failure_map.reading: Denials carry a code but no case-specific reason text; PA-12's denial notice with specific reason does not exist as an artifact.
The notice template supports a specific reason field and it is left empty in practice.
Reviewers select a catch-all code to close cases faster; concentration on one or two codes across many reviewers is the tell.
The notice is specific about the rule applied but never states what evidence would change the outcome, so it is specific and still unappealable.
Notices are generated but not retained in a form tied to the request, so specificity cannot be assessed retrospectively.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: Denial appropriateness — overturn rate as the outcome metric the sample should have found
tests.hypothesis: Where denial-appropriateness sampling is absent or samples without regard to outcome, systemically inappropriate denials persist. The payer already holds the outcome measure: the rate at which its own denials are overturned on appeal. A high overturn rate is not evidence that appeals work; it is evidence that the original determinations were wrong, and it is strongest exactly where the appeal rate is low, because then the overturns are a sample of a much larger untested population.
tests.check: Compute overturn rate by service category, by reviewer, and by determination basis, and extrapolate the implied incorrect-denial count over the un-appealed population as a range rather than a point estimate. Then check whether PA-14's quarterly sample was drawn at all, and whether it was drawn from the strata this analysis says are worst.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 6 - Denial appropriateness via overturn rate, and sample-coverage check
-- Anchor: OIG OEI-09-19-00350 (open recommendation).
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_denials (30; the floor for material denial volume)

WITH denials AS (
  SELECT d.pa_request_id, d.service_category, d.reviewer_id, d.determination_basis,
         d.decision_datetime
  FROM pa_decision d
  WHERE d.decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED'
    AND d.decision_datetime BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
),
outcomes AS (
  SELECT a.pa_request_id,
         MAX(CASE WHEN a.appeal_outcome = 'OVERTURNED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS overturned
  FROM pa_appeal a GROUP BY a.pa_request_id
),
strata AS (
  SELECT
      d.service_category,
      COUNT(*)                                                     AS denials,
      SUM(CASE WHEN o.pa_request_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS appealed,
      SUM(COALESCE(o.overturned, 0))                               AS overturned,
      ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(o.overturned,0)) * 1.0
            / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN o.pa_request_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0), 4)
                                                                   AS overturn_rate
  FROM denials d
  LEFT JOIN outcomes o ON o.pa_request_id = d.pa_request_id
  GROUP BY d.service_category
)
SELECT
    s.*,
    (s.denials - s.appealed)                                       AS never_appealed,
    -- Illustrative range only. Appealed cases are a self-selected sample and are
    -- NOT representative of the un-appealed population. Report as a range, label
    -- it as an ordering aid, and never as an overpayment or liability estimate.
    ROUND((s.denials - s.appealed) * s.overturn_rate * 0.25)       AS implied_wrong_low,
    ROUND((s.denials - s.appealed) * s.overturn_rate)              AS implied_wrong_high,
    smp.sampled_cases,
    CASE WHEN smp.sampled_cases IS NULL THEN 'STRATUM_NEVER_SAMPLED' ELSE 'SAMPLED' END
      AS pa14_coverage
FROM strata s
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT service_category, COUNT(*) AS sampled_cases
    FROM pa_denial_sample
    WHERE sample_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    GROUP BY service_category
) smp ON smp.service_category = s.service_category
WHERE s.denials >= :min_denials          -- material strata only; smaller strata are left out of the report
ORDER BY s.overturn_rate DESC NULLS LAST, s.denials DESC;

-- Also run this grouped by reviewer_id. A reviewer whose overturn rate sits far
-- above peers on comparable case mix is a training and calibration finding, not
-- a disciplinary one, and the output should say so on its face.
tests.threshold: Overturn rate has no defensible external benchmark, and importing one would be worse than useless here because case mix drives it. Compare strata against each other and against the same stratum's own history. Material denial volume is set by :min_denials (30 denials in the period is a starting value); strata below it are left out of the report, so lower it if small categories matter to you. Any stratum at or above that floor and STRATUM_NEVER_SAMPLED is a finding regardless of its overturn rate, because it means PA-14's quarterly sample is not risk-weighted. The extrapolation columns are deliberately a wide range and are an ordering aid only — appealed cases are self-selected and systematically unrepresentative, and a point estimate built on them will not survive scrutiny. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-14 (PA denial-appropriateness sampling review — open OIG recommendation). Secondary: PA-15 (Automatic external medical review of upheld denials), PA-09 (Coverage-rule application; internal criteria not more restrictive than Medicare rules).

failure_map.reading: No denial-appropriateness sampling exists. PA-14's denial-sample review workpaper does not exist; the open OIG recommendation is unaddressed.
PA-14 specifies a quarterly cycle; one or more quarters produced no workpaper.
Samples are drawn and reviewed by the same function that issued the determinations, so the review confirms rather than tests.
The sample is drawn at random across all denials, so it is dominated by high-volume low-risk categories and structurally under-samples the strata this test identifies as worst.
Reviews are performed but dispositions are not retained per sampled case, so the error rate cannot be recomputed or audited.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: Upheld denials that never reached an external reviewer
tests.hypothesis: Where automatic external medical review of upheld denials is absent, an internal reviewer's decision to uphold their own organisation's denial is final. The data signature is direct: upheld internal appeals with no matching external-review referral record. A second, quieter signature is a referral that exists but resolves suspiciously fast or always in the plan's favour, which suggests the external review is not independent in practice.
tests.check: Left-join upheld internal appeals to the external-review referral log and count the unreferred. Then, for the referred population, report time-to-disposition and outcome distribution by external entity — an entity that never overturns is a finding about the referral arrangement.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 7 - Upheld denials with no external medical review
-- Anchor: OIG OEI-09-19-00350 (open recommendation), managed-care context.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :referral_window_days (administrative lag in days, e.g. 7 to 30; must be shorter than the period)

WITH upheld AS (
  SELECT a.appeal_id, a.pa_request_id, a.beneficiary_id, a.service_category,
         a.appeal_level, a.disposition_date
  FROM pa_appeal a
  WHERE a.appeal_outcome = 'UPHELD'
    AND a.disposition_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    -- administrative lag: an appeal upheld inside the last :referral_window_days of the period
    -- has not yet had time to be referred and is not treated as unreferred
    -- date minus integer days (PostgreSQL, DuckDB, Oracle); elsewhere use DATEADD(day, -n, end_date)
    AND a.disposition_date <= CAST(:period_end AS DATE) - CAST(:referral_window_days AS INTEGER)
    AND a.appeal_level = (SELECT MAX(x.appeal_level) FROM pa_appeal x
                          WHERE x.pa_request_id = a.pa_request_id)
),
referred AS (
  SELECT e.appeal_id, e.external_entity_id, e.referral_date,
         e.external_disposition, e.external_disposition_date
  FROM external_review e
)
SELECT
    CASE WHEN r.appeal_id IS NULL THEN 'NOT_REFERRED' ELSE 'REFERRED' END AS referral_class,
    u.service_category,
    r.external_entity_id,
    COUNT(*) AS appeals,
    ROUND(AVG(r.referral_date - u.disposition_date), 1)               AS mean_days_to_referral,
    ROUND(AVG(r.external_disposition_date - r.referral_date), 1)      AS mean_days_to_external_decision,
    SUM(CASE WHEN r.external_disposition = 'OVERTURNED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS externally_overturned,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN r.external_disposition = 'OVERTURNED' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)
          / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 4)                                   AS external_overturn_rate
FROM upheld u
LEFT JOIN referred r ON r.appeal_id = u.appeal_id
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY referral_class, appeals DESC;

-- Two findings, deliberately in one report:
--   NOT_REFERRED with material volume  -> the control is absent or partial.
--   REFERRED with an external_overturn_rate of effectively zero across an entity
--   with high volume -> the referral exists and the independence does not.
tests.threshold: NOT_REFERRED is categorical where the automatic-referral obligation applies — any count above zero is a finding, and the only tuning needed is :referral_window_days to allow for administrative lag before treating a case as unreferred. For the referred population there is no threshold, only a comparison: an external entity whose overturn rate is near zero while another entity reviewing comparable case mix overturns at a normal rate is the pattern to escalate, and with a single external entity you have no comparator at all — which is itself worth recording. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-15 (Automatic external medical review of upheld denials — open OIG recommendation). Secondary: PA-14 (Denial-appropriateness sampling), PA-19 (Qualified-clinician denial governance + segregation of duties).

failure_map.reading: No external-review referral route exists; PA-15's external-review disposition artifact does not exist.
The referral route exists on paper and no referrals were made in the period.
Cases are closed as withdrawn or reopened internally rather than referred, keeping the referral count low without changing the outcome for the beneficiary.
Referrals are made to an entity selected and paid by the plan with no independence safeguard, and the near-zero overturn rate shows it.
Referrals are asserted but no dated referral record or external disposition is retained per appeal.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: Denials with no human clinician behind them
tests.hypothesis: Medical-necessity denials require a qualified clinician's determination and segregation of duties; no denial may be issued solely by an algorithm. Where that governance is absent or nominal, the signature is arithmetic rather than statistical: a reviewer whose sign-off count per working hour exceeds what reading a case permits, sign-offs clustered in seconds-apart bursts, or a sign-off identity that matches the identity that ran the model.
tests.check: Count medical-necessity denials with no clinician identifier at all; then, for those with one, compute per-reviewer sign-offs per active hour and the distribution of inter-signature intervals. Separately check the credential of the signing identity against the determination type, and check that the signer is not the requester or the model operator.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 8 - Clinician sign-off integrity on medical-necessity denials
-- Anchor: 42 CFR 422.101(c); CMS-0057-F.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_plausible_review_seconds (60), :max_denials_per_day (100), :max_fast_signoffs (10)

WITH mn_denials AS (
  SELECT d.pa_request_id, d.decision_datetime, d.reviewer_id, d.reviewer_credential,
         d.determination_basis,         -- 'CLINICAL_REVIEW' | 'AUTOMATED_CRITERIA' | 'MODEL'
         d.model_id, d.model_version,
         d.service_category
  FROM pa_decision d
  WHERE d.decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED'
    AND d.denial_type = 'MEDICAL_NECESSITY'
    AND d.decision_datetime BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
),
sequenced AS (
  SELECT m.*,
         LAG(m.decision_datetime) OVER (PARTITION BY m.reviewer_id
                                        ORDER BY m.decision_datetime) AS prev_signoff
  FROM mn_denials m
),
per_reviewer AS (
  SELECT
      reviewer_id,
      -- a reviewer with no credential on file is reported as UNRECORDED, not skipped
      COALESCE(MIN(reviewer_credential), 'UNRECORDED') AS credential,
      COUNT(*)                                     AS denials_signed,
      COUNT(DISTINCT CAST(decision_datetime AS DATE)) AS active_days,
      ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (decision_datetime - prev_signoff))), 1)
                                                   AS mean_seconds_between_signoffs,
      SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (decision_datetime - prev_signoff))
                    < :min_plausible_review_seconds THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
                                                   AS signoffs_faster_than_plausible
  FROM sequenced
  WHERE reviewer_id IS NOT NULL                    -- denials with no reviewer are counted separately below
  GROUP BY reviewer_id
)
SELECT 'NO_REVIEWER_RECORDED' AS finding, CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS reviewer_id,
       COUNT(*) AS n, CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS detail
FROM mn_denials WHERE reviewer_id IS NULL

UNION ALL

SELECT 'MODEL_BASIS_NO_CLINICIAN', CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR), COUNT(*), MIN(model_id)
FROM mn_denials
WHERE determination_basis IN ('AUTOMATED_CRITERIA','MODEL') AND reviewer_id IS NULL

UNION ALL

SELECT 'IMPLAUSIBLE_SIGNOFF_RATE', reviewer_id, denials_signed,
       CAST(signoffs_faster_than_plausible AS VARCHAR)
FROM per_reviewer
WHERE denials_signed * 1.0 / NULLIF(active_days, 0) > :max_denials_per_day
   OR signoffs_faster_than_plausible > :max_fast_signoffs

UNION ALL

SELECT 'CREDENTIAL_MISMATCH', reviewer_id, denials_signed, credential
FROM per_reviewer
WHERE credential NOT IN ('MD','DO','NP','PA','RN_WITH_MD_OVERSIGHT')  -- adapt to your policy; UNRECORDED is listed
ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC;
tests.threshold: NO_REVIEWER_RECORDED and MODEL_BASIS_NO_CLINICIAN are categorical — any count above zero is a finding and needs no tuning. :min_plausible_review_seconds and :max_denials_per_day are the tunable pair and both are genuinely contestable: a reviewer working a queue of near-identical straightforward cases can legitimately move fast, and a low threshold here will produce indefensible output. Start deliberately high — 60 seconds and 100 per day — and note that the defensible finding is a burst pattern (many sign-offs seconds apart) rather than a daily total. :max_fast_signoffs (10 as a starting value) is how many faster-than-plausible sign-offs a reviewer may have before being listed. A reviewer with no credential on file is listed under CREDENTIAL_MISMATCH as UNRECORDED. Nothing in this test identifies an individual's misconduct; it identifies a workflow that does not permit the review it certifies. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-19 (Qualified-clinician medical-necessity denial governance + segregation of duties; no denial solely by algorithm). Secondary: PA-12 (Specific denial-reason communication), PA-14 (Denial-appropriateness sampling).

failure_map.reading: No clinician sign-off is captured on medical-necessity denials; PA-19's sign-off + SoD matrix does not exist.
The sign-off field exists and is null for a material share of denials in the period.
A single clinician identity is applied in bulk to model output, so the sign-off is a batch attestation rather than a determination.
Sign-off is captured but segregation of duties is not enforced — the signer is the requester, the model operator, or the person with the utilisation target.
Sign-offs are recorded in a field that is overwritten on reassignment, so the person who made each determination cannot be established after the fact.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: Internal criteria more restrictive than the coverage rule they implement
tests.hypothesis: Coverage determinations must apply the current national and local coverage rules, and internal criteria may not be more restrictive than them. Where that control is absent, a plan's internal criteria set drifts stricter — usually not by decision but by accretion, as a criteria vendor's rule set is adopted wholesale. The signature is a denial population whose stated basis is an internal criterion for a service the national rule covers, and a denial rate for that service far above comparable payers or above the plan's own rate before the criteria change.
tests.check: Group denials by the criterion cited and join to the coverage-rule crosswalk that PA-09 names as its evidence artifact. Flag every denial whose cited basis is an internal criterion with no mapped NCD/LCD/LCA, and every service where the internal criterion's effective date is followed by a step change in denial rate.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 9 - Internal criteria vs the coverage rule
-- Anchors: SSA 1862(a)(1)(A); OIG OEI-09-18-00260 (open rec).
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_determinations (100)

WITH cited AS (
  SELECT d.pa_request_id, d.service_code, d.criterion_id, d.decision, d.decision_datetime
  FROM pa_decision d
  WHERE d.decision_datetime BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
),
mapped AS (
  SELECT c.*, x.ncd_lcd_id, x.rule_effective_date, x.criterion_effective_date,
         x.mapping_status              -- 'MAPPED' | 'INTERNAL_ONLY' | 'UNMAPPED'
  FROM cited c
  LEFT JOIN criteria_coverage_crosswalk x ON x.criterion_id = c.criterion_id
),
rates AS (
  SELECT service_code, criterion_id, ncd_lcd_id, mapping_status,
         MIN(criterion_effective_date) AS criterion_effective_date,
         DATE_TRUNC('month', decision_datetime) AS decision_month,
         COUNT(*) AS determinations,
         SUM(CASE WHEN decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS denials
  FROM mapped
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,6
)
SELECT
    service_code, criterion_id, ncd_lcd_id, mapping_status,
    criterion_effective_date, decision_month,
    determinations, denials,
    ROUND(denials * 1.0 / NULLIF(determinations, 0), 4) AS denial_rate,
    -- denial rate for the same service in the six months before the criterion took effect
    LAG(ROUND(denials * 1.0 / NULLIF(determinations,0), 4), 6)
      OVER (PARTITION BY service_code ORDER BY decision_month) AS denial_rate_6m_prior,
    CASE
      WHEN mapping_status = 'INTERNAL_ONLY' THEN 'NO_COVERAGE_RULE_BEHIND_CRITERION'
      WHEN mapping_status = 'UNMAPPED' OR mapping_status IS NULL THEN 'CROSSWALK_INCOMPLETE'  -- NULL: criterion cited but absent from the crosswalk
      ELSE 'MAPPED'
    END AS criterion_class
FROM rates
WHERE determinations >= :min_determinations
ORDER BY criterion_class, denial_rate DESC;

-- CROSSWALK_INCOMPLETE is not a lesser finding than NO_COVERAGE_RULE_BEHIND_CRITERION.
-- It means PA-09's evidence artifact - the criteria-to-coverage crosswalk - does not
-- cover the criteria actually in use, so the control cannot be assessed at all.
tests.threshold: NO_COVERAGE_RULE_BEHIND_CRITERION is categorical in the programmes where the not-more-restrictive obligation binds, and needs no threshold; whether it binds depends on your line of business, so establish that before treating a row as a finding. The step-change comparison is the tunable half: a denial-rate rise of more than roughly a third across a criterion's effective date, on stable volume, is worth reading — but coding changes, seasonal mix and network changes all move denial rates, so treat it as a prompt to read the criterion text rather than as evidence. :min_determinations = 100 keeps the rate meaningful. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-09 (Coverage-rule application: apply current NCD/LCD/LCA; internal criteria not more restrictive than Medicare rules — open OIG recommendation). Secondary: PA-14 (Denial-appropriateness sampling), PA-16 (EPSDT / children's-services PA policy).

failure_map.reading: No criteria-to-coverage crosswalk exists; PA-09's evidence artifact is missing and internal criteria are unmapped to any coverage rule.
The crosswalk exists but was not refreshed against the current NCD/LCD/LCA releases in the period, so it maps to superseded rules.
Reviewers cite the internal criterion in preference to the coverage rule because the workflow surfaces it first.
The crosswalk maps criteria to rules but nobody compares their restrictiveness, so the mapping exists and the substantive test it was built for is never performed.
The criterion cited on each determination is not retained, so no determination can be traced to the rule it applied.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: Determinations made on incomplete utilisation data
tests.hypothesis: A coverage determination made without the beneficiary's utilisation history is a determination made blind — it cannot see the prior conservative therapy that would support approval, or the duplicate item already supplied that would support denial. Where the data-sufficiency check is absent, determinations proceed on whatever happened to be loaded. The signature is a determination timestamp preceding the availability of the beneficiary's claims history, or a data-completeness attestation that is present and always identical.
tests.check: For each determination, establish whether the beneficiary's utilisation datamart contained a full lookback window at the moment of decision, and whether the data-completeness attestation was recorded. Report determinations made against a partial or empty history, split by whether the outcome was affirmation or denial — both directions are harmful and for different reasons.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 10 - Utilisation-data sufficiency at the moment of determination
-- Anchor: OIG (2025) Part B coverage determinations utilisation data (open rec).
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :lookback_days (365)

WITH determinations AS (
  SELECT d.pa_request_id, d.beneficiary_id, d.service_code, d.decision,
         d.decision_datetime, d.data_completeness_attested
  FROM pa_decision d
  WHERE d.decision_datetime BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
),
history_at_decision AS (
  SELECT
      t.pa_request_id,
      -- claims present in the datamart AS AT the decision, not as at today.
      -- The warehouse_load_date filter is the whole point of this test: a claim
      -- loaded after the decision could not have informed it.
      -- History is NOT cut at the lookback: the earliest line available must be
      -- allowed to lie beyond it, or a full lookback could never be recognised.
      COUNT(cl.claim_line_id) AS lines_available_at_decision,       -- all history loaded before the decision
      -- the same count restricted to the lookback window, which is what the reviewer could use.
      -- Date minus integer days (PostgreSQL, DuckDB, Oracle); elsewhere use DATEADD(day, -n, d).
      COUNT(CASE WHEN cl.service_date >= CAST(t.decision_datetime AS DATE) - :lookback_days
                 THEN cl.claim_line_id END) AS lines_in_lookback_at_decision,
      MIN(cl.service_date)    AS earliest_available_service_date,
      MAX(cl.warehouse_load_date) AS latest_load_before_decision
  FROM determinations t
  LEFT JOIN claim_lines cl
         ON  cl.beneficiary_id     = t.beneficiary_id
         AND cl.warehouse_load_date <  t.decision_datetime
  GROUP BY t.pa_request_id
)
SELECT
    t.decision,
    CASE
      WHEN h.lines_available_at_decision = 0 THEN 'NO_HISTORY_AVAILABLE'
      -- date minus date gives days (PostgreSQL, DuckDB, Oracle); elsewhere use DATEDIFF(day, a, b)
      WHEN CAST(t.decision_datetime AS DATE) - h.earliest_available_service_date < :lookback_days
        THEN 'PARTIAL_LOOKBACK'
      ELSE 'FULL_LOOKBACK'
    END AS data_sufficiency_class,
    COALESCE(t.data_completeness_attested, 'NOT_RECORDED') AS attestation,
    COUNT(*) AS determinations,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.service_code) AS distinct_services,
    SUM(h.lines_available_at_decision)   AS history_lines_all_time,
    SUM(h.lines_in_lookback_at_decision) AS history_lines_in_lookback
FROM determinations t
JOIN history_at_decision h ON h.pa_request_id = t.pa_request_id
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY 1, 2;

-- Read both directions. NO_HISTORY_AVAILABLE + NON_AFFIRMED is an access finding:
-- the prior therapy that would have supported approval may simply not have been
-- visible. NO_HISTORY_AVAILABLE + AFFIRMED is a payment finding: the duplicate
-- already supplied was equally invisible. Reporting only one of them is the
-- single most common way this analysis gets used badly.
tests.threshold: :lookback_days = 365 is a generic starting window and the clinically right window varies by service — a conservative-therapy requirement may look back six weeks, a replacement-interval rule five years. Set it per service class rather than globally, or the output is dominated by an arbitrary choice. The class is set by the earliest line ever loaded; history_lines_in_lookback counts only the lines inside the window, so a FULL_LOOKBACK row with few lines in the window is a long-enrolled member with little recent utilisation, not a data gap. NO_HISTORY_AVAILABLE is categorical and always worth reading. An attestation value of NOT_RECORDED across a material share of determinations means PA-10's evidence artifact is not being produced; an attestation that is present and identical on every determination means it is being produced without being performed, which is harder to see and no better. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-10 (Utilization-data sufficiency check before coverage determinations — open OIG recommendation). Secondary: PA-03 (Complete PA package assembly & validation), PA-09 (Coverage-rule application).

failure_map.reading: No data-sufficiency check precedes determinations; PA-10's data-completeness attestation does not exist.
The check is specified per determination and is absent from a material share of them.
The attestation is defaulted to a passing value in the workflow, so it is recorded on every determination regardless of the underlying data.
The check confirms that the datamart responded, not that it contained a meaningful lookback — an empty result and a complete history both pass.
Warehouse load dates are not retained, so what data was available at the moment of decision cannot be reconstructed and this test cannot be run.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: Insufficient-documentation non-affirmation — whose package, whose checklist
tests.hypothesis: Non-affirmation for insufficient documentation is the most common PA outcome that nobody owns. Where package assembly and validation is absent on the requester side, it concentrates in specific requesters; where the payer's documentation-eligibility checklist is absent or unclear, it concentrates in specific service categories across all requesters. The two have opposite remedies, and the concentration pattern distinguishes them.
tests.check: Compute the insufficient-documentation non-affirmation rate by requester and by service category, and measure the dispersion within each. A category where the rate is high and similar across most requesters is a payer-side clarity problem; a category where the rate is normal for most and extreme for a few is a requester-side assembly problem.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 11 - Insufficient-documentation non-affirmation: requester vs category
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_requests (30), :category_wide_threshold (0.20), :low_dispersion (0.05), :requester_z (2.5)

WITH reqs AS (
  SELECT p.pa_request_id, p.requesting_npi, p.service_category,
         p.decision, p.denial_reason_category, p.resubmitted_flag,
         p.decision_datetime
  FROM pa_decision p
  WHERE p.decision_datetime BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
),
by_requester AS (
  SELECT service_category, requesting_npi,
         COUNT(*) AS requests,
         SUM(CASE WHEN decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED'
                   AND denial_reason_category = 'INSUFFICIENT_DOCUMENTATION'
                  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS insuf_denials,
         SUM(CASE WHEN resubmitted_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS resubmitted
  FROM reqs
  GROUP BY service_category, requesting_npi
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_requests
),
category_shape AS (
  SELECT service_category,
         COUNT(*)                                   AS requesters,
         AVG(insuf_denials * 1.0 / requests)        AS mean_insuf_rate,
         STDDEV(insuf_denials * 1.0 / requests)     AS sd_insuf_rate
  FROM by_requester
  GROUP BY service_category
)
SELECT
    b.service_category, b.requesting_npi, b.requests, b.insuf_denials,
    ROUND(b.insuf_denials * 1.0 / b.requests, 4) AS insuf_rate,
    ROUND(c.mean_insuf_rate, 4)                  AS category_mean,
    ROUND(c.sd_insuf_rate, 4)                    AS category_sd,
    ROUND((b.insuf_denials * 1.0 / b.requests - c.mean_insuf_rate)
          / NULLIF(c.sd_insuf_rate, 0), 2)       AS z_within_category,
    ROUND(b.resubmitted * 1.0 / b.requests, 4)   AS resubmission_rate,
    CASE
      WHEN c.mean_insuf_rate > :category_wide_threshold AND c.sd_insuf_rate < :low_dispersion
        THEN 'PAYER_SIDE_CLARITY_PROBLEM'
      WHEN (b.insuf_denials * 1.0 / b.requests - c.mean_insuf_rate)
           / NULLIF(c.sd_insuf_rate, 0) > :requester_z
        THEN 'REQUESTER_SIDE_ASSEMBLY_PROBLEM'
      ELSE 'WITHIN_NORM'
    END AS diagnosis
FROM by_requester b
JOIN category_shape c ON c.service_category = b.service_category
ORDER BY diagnosis, insuf_rate DESC;
tests.threshold: :category_wide_threshold = 0.20 and :low_dispersion = 0.05 together define 'high for everyone', which is the payer-side reading; :requester_z = 2.5 defines the requester-side outlier. All three are starting values and the classification is only as good as the peer grouping behind it, so build service categories that are clinically comparable before trusting the diagnosis column. Read the resubmission rate alongside: a high insufficient-documentation rate with a high resubmission rate and eventual approval is administrative friction, which is a real cost but not an integrity finding, and it should not be reported as one. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-03 (Complete PA package assembly & validation before submission). Secondary: PA-08 (Item-category documentation-eligibility checklists — open OIG recommendation), PA-12 (Specific denial-reason communication).

failure_map.reading: No package checklist is applied before submission; PA-03's per-request checklist artifact does not exist.
The checklist exists and is not applied — a completion rate far below the request count proves it.
The checklist is completed as a formality after submission rather than as a gate before it.
The checklist lists document types but not the content each must contain, so a complete package still fails on sufficiency.
Denial reason categories are too coarse to isolate insufficient documentation, so the rate cannot be computed and the control cannot be tested.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: High-denial categories with no documentation-eligibility checklist
tests.hypothesis: Where item-category documentation-eligibility checklists are absent, the categories that need them most are identifiable from the payer's own denial data — and the absence is usually not a decision but an omission that nobody has ranked. The signature is a category with high denial volume, high insufficient-documentation share, and no checklist entry in the checklist inventory.
tests.check: Rank service categories by insufficient-documentation denial volume and dollars, left-join the checklist inventory, and report the ranked categories with no checklist. This is a coverage report, not a detection query: its output is a prioritised build list for the PA function.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 12 - Checklist coverage against denial concentration
-- Anchor: OIG (2025) intermittent urinary catheters (open rec) - the exemplar case.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_insuf_denials (100)

WITH denial_load AS (
  SELECT d.service_category,
         COUNT(*) AS determinations,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d.decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS denials,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d.decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED'
                   AND d.denial_reason_category = 'INSUFFICIENT_DOCUMENTATION'
                  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS insuf_denials,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d.decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED' THEN d.requested_amount ELSE 0 END)
                                     AS denied_dollars
  FROM pa_decision d
  WHERE d.decision_datetime BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
  GROUP BY d.service_category
)
SELECT
    dl.service_category,
    dl.determinations, dl.denials, dl.insuf_denials, dl.denied_dollars,
    ROUND(dl.insuf_denials * 1.0 / NULLIF(dl.denials, 0), 4) AS insuf_share_of_denials,
    cli.checklist_id,
    cli.last_reviewed_date,
    CASE
      WHEN cli.checklist_id IS NULL THEN 'NO_CHECKLIST'
      WHEN cli.last_reviewed_date < :period_start - 365 THEN 'CHECKLIST_STALE'
      ELSE 'CURRENT'
    END AS checklist_class
FROM denial_load dl
LEFT JOIN checklist_inventory cli ON cli.service_category = dl.service_category
WHERE dl.insuf_denials >= :min_insuf_denials
ORDER BY checklist_class, dl.insuf_denials DESC;

-- Output is a build list. Rank by insuf_denials rather than denied_dollars:
-- the checklist saves a rework cycle per denial, so volume is the right unit,
-- and the dollar column is there to break ties.
tests.threshold: :min_insuf_denials = 100 keeps the list short enough to act on; lower it once the top of the list is built. There is no statistical threshold here at all — the report is a join against an inventory, and NO_CHECKLIST on a high-volume category is a finding on its face. CHECKLIST_STALE deserves the same weight as NO_CHECKLIST when the underlying coverage policy has changed in the interval, so check the policy dates before deprioritising it. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-08 (Item-category documentation-eligibility checklists to prevent insufficient-documentation denials — open OIG recommendation). Secondary: PA-03 (Complete PA package assembly & validation), CD-05 (documentation-checklist control).

failure_map.reading: No checklist inventory exists at all, so this query cannot be joined — which is the finding, and it takes one look at the schema to establish.
Checklists exist for a handful of categories and have not been extended to the categories the denial data has been pointing at for years.
Checklists exist and are not surfaced in the request workflow, so requesters never see them.
Checklists are written from the coverage rule's language rather than from the actual denial reasons, so following one does not prevent the denial.
No inventory records which categories have checklists or when they were last reviewed, so coverage cannot be assessed.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: EPSDT and children's services — PA as a barrier
tests.hypothesis: EPSDT obliges Medicaid to cover services necessary to correct or ameliorate a condition for enrollees under 21, on a standard broader than adult medical necessity. Where the EPSDT PA policy control is absent, adult criteria are applied to paediatric requests by default — usually because one criteria set is configured for all ages. The signature is a denial rate for under-21 enrollees at or above the adult rate on the same service, and denials citing adult-configured criteria.
tests.check: Compare determination outcomes for under-21 and 21-plus enrollees on the same service codes, and check whether the criterion cited on paediatric denials is EPSDT-scoped. Report separately the paediatric denials citing a criterion with no paediatric variant at all — that population is the control failure stated most directly.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 13 - EPSDT / paediatric PA outcomes vs adult
-- Anchor: GAO-24-106532 (open rec); EPSDT under SSA 1905(r).
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_paediatric (30)

WITH d AS (
  SELECT p.pa_request_id, p.service_code, p.criterion_id, p.decision, p.decision_datetime,
         CASE WHEN b.age_at_service < 21 THEN 'UNDER_21' ELSE 'ADULT' END AS age_band
  FROM pa_decision p
  JOIN beneficiary b ON b.beneficiary_id = p.beneficiary_id
  WHERE p.decision_datetime BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
),
rates AS (
  SELECT service_code, age_band,
         COUNT(*) AS determinations,
         SUM(CASE WHEN decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS denials
  FROM d GROUP BY service_code, age_band
),
paired AS (
  SELECT p.service_code,
         p.determinations AS paed_determinations, p.denials AS paed_denials,
         a.determinations AS adult_determinations, a.denials AS adult_denials,
         ROUND(p.denials * 1.0 / NULLIF(p.determinations,0), 4) AS paed_denial_rate,
         ROUND(a.denials * 1.0 / NULLIF(a.determinations,0), 4) AS adult_denial_rate
  FROM rates p
  JOIN rates a ON a.service_code = p.service_code AND a.age_band = 'ADULT'
  WHERE p.age_band = 'UNDER_21'
)
SELECT
    pr.*,
    ROUND(pr.paed_denial_rate - pr.adult_denial_rate, 4) AS rate_gap,
    COALESCE(cx.epsdt_variant_exists, 0) AS epsdt_variant_exists,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(cx.epsdt_variant_exists, 0) = 0 THEN 'ADULT_CRITERION_APPLIED_TO_CHILD'
      WHEN pr.paed_denial_rate > pr.adult_denial_rate THEN 'PAEDIATRIC_RATE_EXCEEDS_ADULT'
      ELSE 'WITHIN_NORM'
    END AS epsdt_class
FROM paired pr
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT d.service_code,
           MAX(CASE WHEN c.epsdt_scoped = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS epsdt_variant_exists
    FROM d LEFT JOIN criteria_master c ON c.criterion_id = d.criterion_id   -- unknown criterion = no EPSDT variant
    WHERE d.age_band = 'UNDER_21'
    GROUP BY d.service_code
) cx ON cx.service_code = pr.service_code
WHERE pr.paed_determinations >= :min_paediatric
ORDER BY epsdt_class, rate_gap DESC;
tests.threshold: ADULT_CRITERION_APPLIED_TO_CHILD is categorical where EPSDT applies and is the row to act on; it requires no rate comparison at all, only the criteria-master join. The rate gap is the softer signal and needs care: paediatric and adult case mix differ on the same code, so a positive gap is a prompt to read the criterion rather than evidence of a barrier. :min_paediatric = 30 keeps thin cells out. This is a beneficiary-protection test and its output must never be used to justify tightening anything — the only direction of remediation it supports is toward the EPSDT standard. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-16 (EPSDT / children's-services PA policy control — open GAO recommendation). Secondary: PA-14 (Denial-appropriateness sampling), PA-11 (Decision-timeliness SLA).

failure_map.reading: No EPSDT-specific PA policy exists; PA-16's annual EPSDT PA policy statement does not exist and one criteria set serves all ages.
The policy statement exists and was not reviewed in the annual cycle the control specifies.
EPSDT variants exist in the criteria master and are not selected by the workflow because age is not a routing attribute.
The EPSDT variant restates the adult criterion with a paediatric label, so the broader correct-or-ameliorate standard is never actually applied.
Age at service is not retained on the determination record, so paediatric outcomes cannot be separated at all.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: PA metrics reporting — recompute the published numbers
tests.hypothesis: Published PA metrics — volume, approval and denial rates, average decision timeframe — are computed by a reporting layer that is rarely reconciled to the transactional record. Where the reporting control is absent or unverified, the published numbers drift from the system of record in a consistent direction: withdrawn and abandoned requests dropped from the denominator, never-decided requests excluded from the timeframe average, partial approvals counted as approvals.
tests.check: Recompute each published metric from the transactional PA tables using an explicit, documented denominator, and place the recomputed value next to the published value. The output is a reconciliation, and every difference should be explainable by a stated definitional choice — an unexplainable difference is the finding.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 14 - Recompute published PA metrics from the transactional record
-- Anchor: CMS-0057-F public reporting. Params: :period_start, :period_end

WITH base AS (
  SELECT r.pa_request_id, r.track, r.received_datetime, r.decision, r.decision_datetime,
         r.request_status          -- 'DECIDED' | 'WITHDRAWN' | 'ABANDONED' | 'OPEN'
  FROM pa_request r
  WHERE r.received_datetime BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
),
recomputed AS (
  SELECT
      COUNT(*)                                                          AS requests_received,
      SUM(CASE WHEN request_status = 'DECIDED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)       AS decided,
      SUM(CASE WHEN request_status IN ('WITHDRAWN','ABANDONED') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
                                                                        AS withdrawn_abandoned,
      SUM(CASE WHEN request_status = 'OPEN' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)          AS still_open,
      SUM(CASE WHEN decision = 'AFFIRMED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)            AS affirmed,
      SUM(CASE WHEN decision = 'PARTIAL'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)            AS partial,
      SUM(CASE WHEN decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)        AS non_affirmed,
      -- denominator stated explicitly: all requests received, not just those decided
      ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 4)                                   AS denial_rate_all_received,
      ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN decision = 'NON_AFFIRMED' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)
            / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN request_status = 'DECIDED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0), 4)
                                                                        AS denial_rate_decided_only,
      ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN decision_datetime IS NOT NULL
                     THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (decision_datetime - received_datetime))/86400.0
                END), 2)                                                AS mean_days_decided_only
  FROM base
)
SELECT r.*, p.published_denial_rate, p.published_mean_days, p.published_request_count,
       ROUND(r.denial_rate_decided_only - p.published_denial_rate, 4) AS denial_rate_delta,
       ROUND(r.mean_days_decided_only  - p.published_mean_days, 2)    AS mean_days_delta,
       (r.requests_received - p.published_request_count)              AS request_count_delta
FROM recomputed r
CROSS JOIN published_pa_metrics p
WHERE p.reporting_period_start = :period_start;

-- The two denial-rate variants are printed side by side on purpose. Which one is
-- correct is a definitional question, not a data question - but a published figure
-- that matches neither, or that matches the flattering one with no stated
-- definition, is a reporting-control finding.
tests.threshold: No threshold. This is a reconciliation and the standard is exact agreement given a stated definition. The tolerance worth allowing is timing — a report run on a different cut date will differ slightly — so reconcile on the same as-at date before treating a delta as real. The delta that matters most is request_count_delta: a published denominator smaller than the received count means requests are being dropped somewhere in the reporting layer, and until that is explained none of the rates above it can be read. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: PA-17 (PA metrics reporting — volume, approvals/denials, average decision timeframe). Secondary: PA-11 (Decision-timeliness SLA), PA-14 (Denial-appropriateness sampling).

failure_map.reading: No PA metrics are published or produced; PA-17's published metrics report does not exist.
The report is specified annually and was not produced for the period.
Figures are adjusted between computation and publication with no change record.
The metric definitions exclude withdrawn, abandoned and never-decided requests, so the published rates describe a population chosen after the fact rather than the requests actually received.
No definition document accompanies the published figures, so they cannot be reconciled to anything and this test's deltas cannot be adjudicated.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: PERM data-processing error surface — rebuild it before the cycle does
tests.hypothesis: PERM separates data-processing errors — the payment was wrong because of how the claim was processed, independent of whether the service was appropriate — from medical-review and eligibility errors. The data-processing component is the one a payer can rebuild for itself between cycles, because every input is internal: pricing, duplicates, third-party liability, unit and rate application, non-covered codes. Where PERM/MEQC measurement is the only error-rate signal, a state learns its data-processing error rate once a cycle, years after the payments.
tests.check: Assemble a continuous internal proxy for the data-processing error categories: repriced amount versus paid amount, duplicates from test 1, TPL-liable claims paid as primary, units above the authorised or edited maximum, and payments on codes not covered on the date of service. Report each category as a rate against total paid, and reconcile the total against the last published PERM data-processing rate.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 15 - Continuous internal proxy for the PERM data-processing error component
-- Anchor: 42 CFR Part 431 Subpart Q (PERM/MEQC).
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :pricing_tolerance (0.01)

WITH paid AS (
  SELECT cl.claim_line_id, cl.beneficiary_id, cl.hcpcs, cl.units, cl.service_date,
         cl.paid_amount, cl.allowed_amount, cl.pricing_source
  FROM claim_lines cl
  WHERE cl.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
    AND cl.adjudication_status = 'PAID'
),
pricing_variance AS (
  SELECT p.claim_line_id, p.paid_amount,
         fs.fee_schedule_amount * p.units AS expected_amount,
         p.paid_amount - (fs.fee_schedule_amount * p.units) AS variance
  FROM paid p
  JOIN fee_schedule fs
    ON  fs.hcpcs = p.hcpcs
    AND p.service_date BETWEEN fs.effective_start AND COALESCE(fs.effective_end, DATE '9999-12-31')
  WHERE ABS(p.paid_amount - (fs.fee_schedule_amount * p.units)) > :pricing_tolerance
),
tpl_paid_primary AS (
  SELECT p.claim_line_id, p.paid_amount
  FROM paid p
  JOIN tpl_coverage t
    ON  t.beneficiary_id = p.beneficiary_id
    AND p.service_date BETWEEN t.coverage_start AND COALESCE(t.coverage_end, DATE '9999-12-31')
  WHERE p.pricing_source <> 'SECONDARY'
),
noncovered_on_dos AS (
  SELECT p.claim_line_id, p.paid_amount
  FROM paid p
  LEFT JOIN covered_code cc
    ON  cc.hcpcs = p.hcpcs
    AND p.service_date BETWEEN cc.coverage_start AND COALESCE(cc.coverage_end, DATE '9999-12-31')
  WHERE cc.hcpcs IS NULL
),
totals AS (SELECT SUM(paid_amount) AS total_paid, COUNT(*) AS total_lines FROM paid)
SELECT 'PRICING_VARIANCE'  AS dp_category, COUNT(*) AS lines, SUM(ABS(variance))    AS dollars FROM pricing_variance
UNION ALL
SELECT 'TPL_PAID_PRIMARY',  COUNT(*), SUM(paid_amount) FROM tpl_paid_primary
UNION ALL
SELECT 'NONCOVERED_ON_DOS', COUNT(*), SUM(paid_amount) FROM noncovered_on_dos
UNION ALL
SELECT 'TOTAL_PAID_BASE',   total_lines, total_paid FROM totals;

-- Add the duplicate categories from TEST 1 as further rows rather than recomputing
-- them here, so the two tests cannot disagree. Express each category as a share of
-- TOTAL_PAID_BASE and compare the sum to your last published PERM data-processing
-- rate. A proxy far BELOW the PERM rate means your categories are incomplete, not
-- that your payments are cleaner than PERM found them.
tests.threshold: :pricing_tolerance = $0.01 catches genuine repricing differences; raise it to a dollar or two if your fee schedule carries known rounding, but do not raise it far, because a systematic small variance across millions of lines is exactly the error PERM is built to find and a generous tolerance hides it. There is no target error rate here — the comparison is against your own last PERM data-processing rate and against the previous period of this same proxy. Treat a large gap in either direction as a question about the proxy first and about the payments second, because an incomplete category list is the more likely explanation. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: MD-12 (PERM / MEQC eligibility & claims sampling with error-rate measurement). Secondary: CB-15 (Duplicate claim / line detection), CB-06 (Medicaid NCCI six-methodology implementation).

failure_map.reading: No error-rate measurement exists outside the federal cycle; MD-12's sampled-case workpapers and error rate exist only when CMS requires them.
The cycle ran and the corrective-action plan it produced was not implemented, so the same categories recur.
Sampled cases are corrected individually and the underlying processing defect is not fixed, so the error rate is managed rather than reduced.
Measurement is cycle-bound only. Years of payments accumulate between measurements and nothing internal reports the rate in the interval — which is the specific gap this test closes.
Sampling workpapers do not retain the error category per case, so the data-processing component cannot be separated from medical-review and eligibility errors.

tests.family_title: Prior authorisation and claims processing
tests.name: PTP edits that fire and are overridden — the bypass rate nobody reports
tests.hypothesis: An NCCI PTP edit that fires and is then overridden produces the same payment as an edit that never fired, but it looks healthy on every hit-rate metric. Where edit-enforcement governance is absent, override authority is broad, override reasons are not required, and the override rate concentrates in a small number of operators or a small number of code pairs. The dollars behind overrides are the edit set's real leakage and are almost never reported.
tests.check: Compute, per PTP code pair and per overriding operator, the hit count, override count, override rate and the dollars released by override. Then check whether an override reason was recorded and whether the modifier that would have legitimately bypassed the edit was actually present on the claim.
tests.sql:
-- TEST 16 - PTP edit override rate and the dollars it releases
-- Reference: CMS NCCI PTP edits & Policy Manual.
-- Params: :period_start, :period_end, :min_hits (25)

WITH hits AS (
  SELECT eh.edit_hit_id, eh.claim_line_id, eh.code_pair_id,
         eh.column1_code, eh.column2_code, eh.modifier_indicator,
         eh.outcome,                    -- 'DENIED' | 'OVERRIDDEN' | 'PAID_WITH_MODIFIER'
         eh.override_operator_id, eh.override_reason_code,
         cl.modifier_1, cl.modifier_2, cl.paid_amount, cl.rendering_npi
  FROM edit_hit eh
  JOIN claim_lines cl ON cl.claim_line_id = eh.claim_line_id
  WHERE eh.edit_family = 'PTP'
    AND eh.service_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
)
SELECT
    code_pair_id, column1_code, column2_code, modifier_indicator,
    COUNT(*)                                                          AS hits,
    SUM(CASE WHEN outcome = 'OVERRIDDEN' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)           AS overrides,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN outcome = 'OVERRIDDEN' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)
          / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 4)                                   AS override_rate,
    SUM(CASE WHEN outcome = 'OVERRIDDEN' THEN paid_amount ELSE 0 END) AS dollars_released,
    COUNT(DISTINCT override_operator_id)                              AS distinct_operators,
    SUM(CASE WHEN outcome = 'OVERRIDDEN' AND override_reason_code IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
                                                                      AS overrides_no_reason,
    -- an override on a pair whose modifier indicator is '0' can never be legitimate:
    -- indicator 0 means no modifier permits the pair to be billed together.
    SUM(CASE WHEN outcome = 'OVERRIDDEN' AND modifier_indicator = '0' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
                                                                      AS overrides_on_indicator_0,
    SUM(CASE WHEN outcome = 'OVERRIDDEN'
              AND modifier_indicator = '1'
              AND COALESCE(modifier_1,'') NOT IN ('59','XE','XS','XP','XU')
              AND COALESCE(modifier_2,'') NOT IN ('59','XE','XS','XP','XU')
             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                                       AS overrides_without_modifier
FROM hits
GROUP BY code_pair_id, column1_code, column2_code, modifier_indicator
HAVING COUNT(*) >= :min_hits
    -- categorical: any override on an indicator-0 pair is reported whatever the volume
    OR SUM(CASE WHEN outcome = 'OVERRIDDEN' AND modifier_indicator = '0' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY dollars_released DESC;

-- Run the same aggregation grouped by override_operator_id. A single operator
-- carrying a large share of overrides is a workflow and authority finding - the
-- question is what queue pressure produced it, not who the person is.
tests.threshold: overrides_on_indicator_0 is categorical: a modifier indicator of 0 means no modifier permits the pair, so an override there cannot be correct and any count is a finding. Confirm the indicator values against the current NCCI files before relying on this, since indicators change between quarterly releases. override_rate has no external benchmark — compare pairs against each other and against the same pair's own history, and read dollars_released rather than the rate when deciding what to act on. :min_hits = 25 keeps the list stable. Tune to your population; a starting point, not a standard.
tests.pair: CB-04 (NCCI PTP edit enforcement pre-submission). Secondary: CB-05 (Modifier-59 / X{EPSU} governance & documentation review), CB-17 (Prepayment edit maintenance & tuning from emerging vulnerabilities).

failure_map.reading: PTP edits are not enforced; CB-04's PTP edit hit / disposition log does not exist.
Edits are loaded and set to informational, so they log hits and stop nothing.
This is the test's central case: edits fire and are overridden at volume, with overrides_no_reason establishing that the bypass is not even documented.
Override authority is granted broadly to resolve claim backlogs, so the edit's effect depends on queue pressure rather than on coding policy.
Overrides are applied without recording an operator or reason, so the bypass rate can be counted but never adjudicated.
